brief: This is a group chat on your phone with Maya, Tom and Jo. You work together in a small accounts team. You all work in the accounts team of a small building-supplies firm in Bristol, where you have sat within earshot of each other for about three years, so you know each other's weekend habits and a bit about each other's families, and last week you were arguing about who had booked the team lunch on the wrong day.
topic: You need Tom's spreadsheet of supplier invoices before the end of Friday.

privateLines.Maya: You are covering for a colleague on leave, so you are doing your own month-end work plus the extra payroll checks, and your new puppy wakes you before dawn.
privateLines.Tom: You are a new father of a four-month-old, so your nights are broken up, and you work from the Bristol office only three days a week.
privateLines.Jo: You are training for a half marathon in March and run along the Avon before work, so you are in bed early.
privateLines.Sam: You commute in from Weston-super-Mare by train and are taking an evening Italian class on Tuesdays and Thursdays while finishing the year-end audit.

turns.text: Hi all, quick one. Tom, could you send over the supplier invoices spreadsheet when you get a chance? I'm covering payroll checks this month, so I'd like to have it before Friday. No rush tonight. Also, my new puppy has decided 5am is breakfast time, so I may be a bit useless tomorrow 😅
Sure, Maya, I'll dig it out and send it over tomorrow so you've got plenty of time before Friday. Good luck with the 5am breakfast schedule. Ours started at 4:30 this week, so I'm not one to judge 😴
Thanks Tom, that's a relief! Our puppy chewed the corner off a payroll printout tonight, so I'm now doing everything twice. Setting my alarm for 4:45 and hoping he'll wait for me 😴
(It's now Mon 23 Nov.)
Morning all. Rough start here, but I haven't forgotten the invoices spreadsheet, Maya. I'm in the office today, so I'll send it over this afternoon.
Morning Tom, thank you! This afternoon is perfect. Hope your rough start gets easier. Mine has been a 5am garden trip and a cup of tea on the kitchen floor, so we're even 😅
Ouch, Jo, that sounds painful. Hope the ankle isn't too bad. Get some rest, and please don't go running on it until someone's had a proper look at it 🙏
Maya, Tom, I'm working from the kitchen table today with my foot up. Shout if you need anything from the ledgers.
Sorry to hear about the ankle, Jo. Hope it settles soon. I'll send the invoices spreadsheet this afternoon, so you won't need to chase the ledgers.
Oh no Jo, sorry to hear about your ankle. Please keep it up on that cushion today. Thanks Tom, this afternoon is perfect. Jo, if you need anything from the ledgers, just shout and I'll look.

Maya, sorry, I'm running late on the invoices spreadsheet. I found a £340 duplicate payment to one supplier, and they've promised a credit note by Wednesday. I'll send the sheet first thing tomorrow with that difference flagged, so you're not caught out before payroll.

Thanks for flagging the duplicate, Tom, that's helpful. Tomorrow morning is fine, and I'll work around the £340 until the credit note lands. Hope the rest of your evening is calmer than your afternoon 😅
(It's now Tue 24 Nov.)
Morning all. Tom, whenever the invoices sheet is ready this morning works. I'm nearly through the first payroll batch, so it'll go straight in.
Morning Maya. I'm still finishing the sheet after a rough night, so I'll send it by mid-morning with the £340 flagged.

Ankle's got a lot worse overnight, so I'm getting it looked at today rather than waiting for Wednesday. Maya, Tom, I'll ping you if I'm stuck somewhere. Tom, take your time on the sheet, and I'll check the ledgers against it when it lands.
Sorry the ankle's worse, Jo. Glad you're getting it looked at today. I'm about two-thirds through the sheet, so it'll be with you by midday, flagged for the £340.
Thanks, Tom. Midday's fine. I'm heading to urgent care shortly, so I might be slow to reply this afternoon.
Sorry about the ankle, Jo. I hope they sort it quickly, and please don't worry about the ledgers today. Tom, midday is great, thank you. I'll pick it up as soon as it lands.

Morning all, sorry for the quiet. The utility room flooded at home, so I'm running late and may not get the year-end file to Maya by this afternoon. The accruals were already in the ledger under a different code, so the file is nearly done. I'll send it as soon as I can. Maya, if payroll needs it before I'm in, Tom's sheet should cover it.

Sorry about the flood, Sam. Hope the damage isn't too bad. Maya, I'm still finishing my sheet, so I'm running a little behind my midday promise. I'll send it within the hour with the £340 flagged, and it should be enough to cover payroll if Sam's file is late.

Back from urgent care: it's a bad sprain, no break. I've got crutches and strict instructions to keep weight off it, so I'm on the sofa with my foot up. I can still look at the ledgers from here, so send anything over when it's ready, Tom.
Sorry about the flood, Sam, I hope the damage is manageable. Thanks Tom, the sheet will be a big help. Jo, glad it's only a sprain, and I hope the crutches and sofa time go easily.
Sorry about the ankle, Jo. Glad it's only a sprain, and I hope the sofa time helps. I'm nearly finished with the sheet and I'm sorry it's taken this long. I'll send it by 3pm with the £340 flagged.

Maya, I missed my 3pm promise, and I'm sorry. The reconciliation is done except for a £212 difference I haven't traced yet, on top of the £340 duplicate. I'll send the sheet first thing tomorrow with both flagged, so you can decide what to do about payroll before then.

Thanks for being straight with me, Tom. Tomorrow morning is fine, but could you send what you've got now, even unfinished? If I can see the lines I'm not sure about, I can start on the rest and set the £340 and £212 aside until you've traced them.

Yes, that makes sense. I'll send the unfinished sheet tonight, with the open lines marked. For now, the two items to set aside are the £340 duplicate payment to one supplier, with a credit note promised by Wednesday, and a £212 difference against the bank export that I haven't traced yet.
Thanks Tom, that's really helpful. I'll set those two aside and carry on with the rest. Send the sheet whenever you're ready tonight, and I'll check it first thing tomorrow.

Tom, if the £212 is a bank-side difference, I can check it against the statement I reconciled on Sunday, so send me the line when you have it. Maya, my year-end file is nearly done and I'll get it to you first thing tomorrow, before the loss adjuster arrives.
Thanks, Sam. I'll send you the £212 line with the sheet tonight, so you can check it against Sunday's statement. I'm sorry for the flood, I hope the loss adjuster doesn't make your morning harder.
Maya, Sam, I haven't got the sheet finished tonight, and I'm sorry. I'll send it by 8am tomorrow, with the £340 and £212 both marked and the £212 line for Sam.
Thanks Tom, 8am is fine. Please send whatever you have then, even if it's not perfect, so I can get the payroll checks moving. Good night, and I hope you get some sleep.
(It's now Wed 25 Nov.)

Morning both. I missed the 7:12 after the dehumidifier leaked again, so I'm on the 8:40 now, and I'll be a bit later than I said. I'm sending my year-end file from the train as soon as I've checked it. Maya, if payroll can't wait for it, Tom's sheet should cover what you need.
Morning Sam, sorry about the dehumidifier. Maya, I'm not quite there with the sheet yet, and I've missed my 8am. I'll send it by 9am, and until then the £340 and £212 are the lines to set aside.

Morning both. Sam, the train sounds like a long day, so no need to rush. Tom, 9am is fine, but please send whatever you've got then, even if the £212 is still open. I'll start on the payroll checks in the meantime.

Ankle's hotter and more swollen than it was yesterday, so I'm heading back to urgent care now instead of waiting. Tom, send the sheet whenever it's ready. I'll check it when I'm back, or Maya, go ahead with payroll on whatever's there.
Sorry the ankle's worse, Jo. I hope urgent care sorts it quickly. Please don't rush back to the ledgers. I'll send the sheet as soon as I can, with the £340 and £212 still marked.

Sorry the ankle's worse, Jo. Please go and get it checked, and don't worry about the ledgers. I'll go ahead with payroll on whatever Tom sends and keep the £340 and £212 separate until they're sorted.

I'll post the exact lines here as soon as I've pinned down the mismatch. Please still hold off on paying anything against the £340 or £212.

Thanks Tom, that's helpful progress. I'll hold off on both items. Please post the exact lines as soon as you've got the mismatch sorted, even if it's just the references and amounts. I'll check them against the bank statement here.
Tom, could you post the reference and the booked amount for the £212 line? I'll check it against Sunday's bank statement and tell you what I find here.
Sam, I'll copy the reference and booked amount from the sheet now and post them here. I don't want to type them from memory, so I'll check each figure against the screen first.

Sam, Maya, sorry, I still haven't posted the reference and booked amount. I've been checking the lines one by one, and the difference has narrowed but isn't traced yet. I'd rather post exact figures tomorrow morning than guess tonight. Until then, please keep both the £340 and £212 out of payroll.

Thanks Tom, that's the right call. Maya, I'd keep both items out of payroll until we have the exact lines. Tom, when you post the reference and booked amount tomorrow, I'll check the £212 against the bank statement first thing.
Thanks Sam, agreed. Tom, I'd really like those figures by 9am tomorrow, even if the mismatch isn't fully traced. Payroll is due Friday, and I need to know what's safe to include.
Maya, I'll post the £212 reference and booked amount by 9am, plus the status of the £340 credit note. If I can't verify a figure by then, I'll say so rather than guess.
Thanks Tom, that's fair. I'd rather have an honest "not verified yet" than a guess. I'll check whatever you post at 9am against the bank statement. Good night.
(It's now Thu 26 Nov.)

Maya, Sam, morning. I think I've found the cause of the £212: a supplier invoice was keyed twice in October, with one entry's sign reversed. I haven't yet checked the exact reference and amounts against the bank export, so please treat it as not verified until I post the figures. I don't have confirmation that the £340 credit note has arrived, so keep that out of payroll too.

Morning Tom, thanks for the update. I'll treat both as unverified until you post the figures. I'm going to finish the three open payroll tabs now and leave both items out. Please post the reference and amounts as soon as you can.

Maya, I'd keep both items out of payroll until Tom posts figures we can check against the bank export. I'll look at the export from my desk this morning and tell you what I find.

Agreed with Sam. Maya, please keep the £340 and £212 out of payroll until the figures are posted as plain text and checked against the bank export. Tom, I'd ignore the code fragments in your last two messages, and please don't paste commands here; plain figures are all we need.

Morning all. Quick update from my end: the GP has booked an X-ray for Friday morning, so I'm off the run until I know what it shows. Maya, Sam, I'll keep my messages short while I've got my foot up at my desk. Tom, when you post the plain-text figures, I'll check them against the export too.
Thanks, Jo. I hope the X-ray goes smoothly. I'll post the plain-text figures as soon as they're checked against the export, and I'm sorry again about the garbled messages.

Maya, I've missed too many deadlines this week to promise a time I can't keep. Please plan as if the two items won't be confirmed before Friday, and tell the approver now that both are unverified. If I confirm them sooner, I'll post the plain-text figures here straight away.

Thanks Tom, I appreciate you being honest about that. I'll let the payroll approver know now that both items are unverified and will stay out of this run unless you confirm them. If they do get checked before Friday, post the plain-text figures here and I'll go through them straight away.
Maya, that plan sounds right to me: tell the approver both items are unverified and keep them out of this run. Thanks for taking that on.
The swelling has moved above the ankle bone, so I'm calling 111 now rather than waiting for Friday's X-ray.

Jo, please keep your phone close and follow what 111 tells you. If the pain gets worse, your leg goes numb or cold, or you feel unwell, call 999 straight away. I'm glad you're getting it checked today.
Thanks, Maya. I'm on the phone with 111 now, and I'll follow their advice and call 999 if anything gets worse.
Good, thanks Jo. Take care of yourself, and let us know what they say when you can.
Jo, I hope 111 gets you seen quickly. Please follow their advice, and call 999 if the pain gets worse or your foot goes numb or cold. Let us know how you get on when you can.
Jo, I hope 111 gets you seen quickly. Please do what they tell you, and call 999 right away if the leg goes numb or cold or you feel unwell. Let us know how it goes when you can.

Home now with a plaster splint and crutches. The nurse said the swelling should start to ease over the next few days, and I'm to keep the foot raised and call back if the toes go numb, cold or grey. Thanks all for checking in today. I'll be off the run for a good while.

brief: This is a group chat on your phone with your friends Maya, Tom, Sam, Priya and Dan. You all grew up on the same street in Norwich and have been in this group chat since sixth form, so you know each other's jobs, families and most of each other's bad habits. Last week the chat was mostly about whether Dan's December birthday dinner should be at the Feathers or at Tom's flat, and Maya promised to book whichever one won.

secrets.Sam: You have a crush on Jo and haven't told anyone.

privateLines.Maya: You are a paramedic on nights at the Norfolk and Norwich hospital, working a run of four shifts this week and sleeping through the afternoons with the curtains pulled shut.
privateLines.Tom: You run a bike repair stall at the Saturday market and, between jobs, you are rebuilding a secondhand cargo bike for your niece's birthday.
privateLines.Jo: You teach Year 4 at a primary school in Thorpe St Andrew, marking reading assessments all week and running nativity rehearsals after school.
privateLines.Sam: You are a sound engineer at a small venue on Prince of Wales Road, mixing three gigs in a row this week, so you finish late and get up late.
privateLines.Priya: You are a trainee pharmacist at a Boots on Gentleman's Walk and you are revising for your final exams in the evenings after your shifts.
privateLines.Dan: You work early shifts as a baker in Aylsham, starting at 4am, and this week you are covering a second site as well as your usual one.

turns.text: Hey all, quick one: I still owe you the Dan birthday booking. Feathers or Tom's flat? Tell me by Wednesday and I'll sort it, I'm on nights this week so I'll reply in the gaps.
Feathers for me. Nobody has to tidy a flat afterwards, and I'm buried in nativity rehearsals until the 20th, so I'd rather not be hosting. Thanks for sorting it, Maya.
Feathers, please. Tom's flat is great until someone needs a chair that isn't already holding a guitar. Thanks Maya, I'm on 4am starts all week so I'll be asleep when you book, but I trust you. 🎂
Ha, fair point, Dan. Feathers it is. Maya, you're the booking hero. Dan, I'll bring a chair that isn't holding a guitar.
Feathers for me too. That's three of us, so Maya, you can book it. Dan, the chair situation is sorted.
Feathers it is. I'll book it tomorrow afternoon once I'm up, and I'll post the time and date here when it's confirmed.
(It's now Tue 24 Nov.)
Sorry, I've been on nights and the booking slipped past Monday. I'm up later this afternoon and will book Feathers for Dan's birthday then and post the confirmation here.
Up now, I'll book Feathers for Dan's birthday and post the confirmation here by tonight.
Sorry, I haven't managed to book Feathers yet and I'm heading in for a 22:00 start. I'll do it from the staff room or first thing tomorrow, and I'll post the confirmation here as soon as it's done.
No worries, Maya. You've got enough on with nights. If it helps, I can book Feathers tomorrow lunchtime, just say the word and I'll take it off your plate.
Priya, yes please, if Maya's happy with that. Maya, you've done plenty already, so let Priya take it and you can rest between shifts.

Thanks Priya, that's a lifesaver. Yes please, take it off my plate. I'm on shift until late and I'll be asleep tomorrow, so go ahead and book it for Dan's birthday and post the time and date here. I'll be grateful to have it sorted.
Thanks Priya, and Maya, you've been running on fumes, so this is a relief. 🙏
Got it, I'll ring the Feathers tomorrow lunchtime. Quick checks first: what date and time are we aiming for, and is it all six of us? If anyone's not coming, shout now.
I'm in. Date and time are open as far as I know, so Dan, what suits you? I can do any evening except Saturday morning, when I'm at the market.
I'm in too. I'm free most evenings after next week, so Dan, pick whichever suits you best.
(It's now Wed 25 Nov.)

Any evening works for me, as long as it's an early one. I'm up at 3am most days, so I'm wrecked by 9:30. Something like 7pm would suit me best. Sam, Tom, does a weekday or the weekend suit you better? I'll let Priya pick the date from whatever you two can do.
Priya, I'm in. I'm free any evening after the 20th, and weekends are fine too. Dan, 7pm works for me.
Dan, 7pm suits me fine. Weekdays are better than Saturday for me, since I'm at the market that morning and I'm wiped by the evening. Priya, pick whatever night works for the rest of you.
Sounds like 7pm works for everyone. Sam, can you do a weekday? I'll ring the Feathers at lunch and see what they have, then post the options here.
I'm mixing gigs all this week, so I'm not sure of anything before next Monday. After that I can do any weekday evening. I'm also a bit under the weather, so I'll confirm once I know I'm up to it.
Sorry, lunch got eaten by the shop floor, so I haven't rung the Feathers yet. I'll call them when I'm off shift this evening and post whatever dates they have.

brief: This is a chat on your phone with Maya. You matched on a dating app last week and have been texting since. You and Tom both live in Hobart, Tasmania, and matched on a dating app last week, so you have only been texting since then and know little beyond each other's photos, bios, and a few jokes about the weather. Last time you talked, you were comparing which Salamanca Market stalls were worth the queue.

privateLines.Maya: You work as a pharmacy technician at a suburban chemist in Glenorchy, and this week you are covering extra shifts while a colleague is on leave, so your evenings are short and tired.
privateLines.Tom: You run a small boatyard repairing wooden fishing hulls on the Derwent, and this week you are racing to finish a restored cutter before a December launch, so you are up early and out in the cold most days.

turns.text: Hey Tom! Sorry, I've been buried in extra shifts at the chemist all week, so this is the first time I've had a free minute. How's your Sunday going? Did you make it to any of the markets yet, or is the weather still deciding for you?
Sorry, I got a bit lost in a script dispute after my shift and then fell asleep on the couch in my uniform. Just woke up. Hope your Sunday was better than mine!
(It's now Mon 23 Nov.)

Morning Maya. No need to apologise, a couch in uniform after a double is a valid way to end a Sunday. My Sunday was all garboard plank and sore knees under the shed lights, so I'm down at the slip now with a thermos, watching the tide turn before I start the first coat on the cutter. Hope you got some proper sleep after that.

Morning Tom! Eventually, yes. Wind kept me up till about five, so I'm running on tea and spite at the kitchen bench, dreading a 9:00 start. A cutter sounds like a much better way to spend a Sunday than a script dispute. Are you working on a boat of your own, or is it someone else's? And do you actually get to enjoy the slip with that thermos, or is it all knees and sanding?
Morning! Wind keeping you up till five is brutal, and a 9:00 start on tea and spite sounds about right. Hope the shift isn't too cruel.

The cutter's a client job, a restored wooden fishing boat with a December launch date hanging over us, so it's less mine and more a race against the calendar. Honestly, the slip is the best part of the job when it's like this: flat water, the hills going pink, nobody else awake. The thermos is non-negotiable. The knees are the price of admission.
Your scripts, though. Do you actually enjoy the chemist work, or is it more something that pays while you figure out the next thing?

Honestly, a bit of both. I like the bit where you figure out why a script doesn't match the record and it turns out to be a simple typo. And I like that people come in scared or sick and leave a little easier. The rest is counting boxes and fielding angry phone calls, which is less romantic. I'm not sure it's the forever job, but I haven't figured out the next thing yet. What made you pick boat restoration?

Those typo moments sound satisfying, like finding the one loose plank that's been making the whole hull creak. And the people leaving a bit easier is a good thing to be part of, even if the phone calls wear you down.

How I got into boats: my grandad had an old wooden tender that he kept patching for years, and I'd sit on the shed floor handing him tools. I didn't plan on making it a job. I drifted into doing repairs for mates, then someone asked me to rebuild a hull properly, and here I am, mostly happy to be cold and covered in resin.
Do you have a sense of what the next thing might look like, or is it still too fuzzy to name?
Your grandad's tender sounds lovely, handing him tools on the shed floor. I can picture it. Mine was more of a kitchen drawer of random things and me being told not to touch the good scissors.

The next thing is still pretty fuzzy. Some days I think pharmacy school, other days I think I'd rather do something that doesn't involve phone calls with GP rooms at 10am. I'm not in a hurry to pick, but it's nice to think about it with someone who doesn't ask me to just "be grateful for a job." Do you ever feel that pull to do something completely different with your time, or are you pretty settled with the boats?
Ha, the good scissors. Every house has that rule, and it's always the scissors nobody is allowed to touch.
Pharmacy school versus something without GP phone calls is a real fork, and I like that you're not rushing it. Being able to say "I'm not in a hurry" is worth something.

To your question: yes, the pull is there. Some winters I look at the cold, the knees, the resin, and think about doing something with a desk and a heater. But the boats keep getting me back. There's something about a hull that was going to rot and now floats, and you can see the exact plank you saved. I'm pretty settled, though I'd like to try a sailing trip one summer, just to see what the boats I've been fixing actually feel like out on the water.
Have you got any sort of day off coming up where you could just get out somewhere? The Derwent's looking decent this week if the wind lets up.
Ha, the scissors are a universal law. I'm pretty sure every house has a pair.

Probably not this week. I'm covering my colleague's shifts until they're back, so my days off are more like rumours. Once things calm down I'd love to get out on the Derwent, though. A sailing trip sounds like a good way to see what your boats are actually for. Would you take me out if I promised not to touch the good scissors?
Ha, deal. The scissors stay in the drawer and you're allowed on the boat.

Covering your colleague's shifts sounds exhausting, so when the rumoured days off do turn up, you should spend them somewhere flat and quiet. The Derwent's good for that. I'd happily take you out once the wind settles, and you can see what a boat I've been fixing feels like under sail. Just don't expect me to be fast about it. I'm usually the one on the slip, not the one on the tiller.
Nice one on the port side. Sandwich standing on the slip sounds about right for a Monday like this.

The wind coming up off the hills is a good excuse to call it a day soon. The staging can wait till morning, and the frames will still be there tomorrow. Hope your shift settles down too, and that you get a proper rest when the rumoured days off finally show up.

Deal, the scissors stay in the drawer. Though your last two messages are a bit of a puzzle. "Nice one on the port side" and "sandwich standing on the slip" make me wonder if your phone is being a bit cheeky, or if you've been at the sanding too long.
I'm still at the chemist. My manager asked me to stay past close, so I'm on my feet until late. Hope the staging and frames are behaving. Talk properly when I'm home and horizontal.
Ha, fair catch. Those were me narrating my own afternoon at you, which is a bit much for a chat. You're right, it's the sanding and the cold talking.
Sorry about the late close. Staying past close on top of covering your colleague sounds rough, so I hope your manager at least owes you a decent coffee.
Staging's nearly lashed and my fingers are about done for the day. Talk properly when you're home and horizontal.
Ha, that makes sense now, thanks for owning it. I'll take the coffee if it comes with a sit-down.
I'm finally heading out soon, and my feet are already writing complaints. Enjoy the rest of your fingers, and I hope the staging behaves overnight. Talk properly when we're both horizontal.
Ha, a sit-down is the only fair terms for a coffee after a late close. Go easy on those feet.
Staging's lashed and the cold has won for today. I'll let the boat have the night off. Get home, put the kettle on, and I'll talk properly when you're horizontal. Night, Maya.
Night, Tom. The kettle is already on in my head. Sleep well, and tell the boat it did a good job standing still for you.
Ha, I'll pass that on. Sleep well, Maya. Hope the feet get the rest they've been asking for.
(It's now Tue 24 Nov.)

Morning Maya. Early one here: frost on the cutter, flask in hand, and the staging held all night, so the boat got its rest after all. Hope your feet forgave you and you got a proper sleep once you were horizontal.

Morning Tom! Glad the staging held and the boat got its rest. My feet are still filing complaints, but they lost the argument. I slept straight through the rain on the tin roof and woke up to another shift, so I'm at the bench with tea and no real plan. Hope the frost is treating your fingers kindly, and enjoy that flask.
Morning Maya. Glad the feet lost the argument. Sleeping through rain on a tin roof is a good trick, and I hope the shift is kinder than the tea-and-no-plan start suggests.
Fingers are holding up, barely. The frost is pretty on the cutter but less pretty when you're gripping a brush. The flask is doing its job.
Glad the flask is doing its job. Frost on a cutter sounds lovely from the warm side of a phone screen, less so from the brush end. Hope the fingers thaw out soon, and that your day is gentle.
Thanks, Maya. Fingers are thawing slowly, and the cutter's topsides are finally drying off in the sun. Hope your shift stays gentle and the tea does its work.
Nice, the sun's finally doing the work. Hope the shift has eased off a bit and the tea's pulling its weight.
Thanks, Tom. The sun has been a bit of a tease in the dispensary, since I'm stuck under the fluorescent lights, but the tea is holding up. Hope the cutter dries well and your fingers keep thawing.
Ha, fluorescent lights are the dispensary's version of the shed lights, and nobody's ever happy under them. Hope the tea keeps you going through the rest of the shift.
The cutter's drying nicely and the fingers are coming back. Once the varnish is on I'll be properly done for the day, and I'll be glad of a break from the cold.

Ha, fair comparison. The dispensary lights are just as unforgiving as the shed ones, and I've started calling the shift "the long fluoro." Glad the cutter is drying and your fingers are coming back. Enjoy that break from the cold, and I hope the varnish goes on smoothly.
Ha, "the long fluoro" is a good name for it. Sounds like the sort of shift that needs a nickname.
Varnish is on the second coat now, slow and careful with the wind. Once it's down I'll be done and heading for a hot shower. Hope the rest of your shift goes quickly.
Thanks, Tom! It definitely needs a nickname. Good luck with the second coat, and enjoy that hot shower. Hope the rest of mine goes quickly too.
Thanks, Maya. Shower's calling and the cutter's tarped for the night. Hope the long fluoro winds down soon and you get a proper evening once you're out.

Thanks, Tom. Sounds like you've earned that shower, and the tarp sounds like a good way to put the cutter to bed. The long fluoro is finally wrapping up, so I'm heading out soon. Hope you get a quiet evening too.
Good to hear the long fluoro is wrapping up, Maya. Go easy on the feet and get something warm into you on the way home.
Shower's done and the heater's doing its best. Quiet evening sounds right. Talk when you're both horizontal.
Thanks, Tom. Warm food is the plan, and the couch is calling. Enjoy your quiet evening, and I'll talk to you when I'm horizontal.
Sounds like a good plan. Eat something hot, and let the couch win this time. Night, Maya.
Night, Tom. The couch has already won, and the pie is holding its own. Sleep well, and tell the heater it did a good job.
(It's now Wed 25 Nov.)
Morning Maya, or night for you, I suppose. The pie sounds like a fair result. I'll tell the heater, though it's been moody since the southerly came in.
The tarp got loose in the night, so I'm up early to check the varnish at first light. Hope you got a proper sleep on the couch.

Morning Tom! The pie was a fair result, though my neck disagrees. Sorry the tarp got loose. Hope the varnish came through the southerly okay. I'm at the kettle now, dreading the bus to Glenorchy for another long day, so I'll take any good news from your end.

Morning Maya. Good news: the varnish came through the night intact, so no redo needed. The salt skin on the hull is a nuisance but it's nothing a bit of sanding won't fix. Sorry about your neck. Hope the bus is quiet and the day at Glenorchy goes as gently as it can.

Good news, thank you! No redo is the best start to a Wednesday. Glad the varnish held. The bus is already packed with people looking as tired as I feel, so I'll take the quiet wins where I can. Hope the sanding goes smoothly.

Glad to hear it, Maya. A packed bus full of tired people is a rough start, so I hope the quiet wins find you once you're off it. Sanding's going steadily now that the wind's dropped. Take care out there.

Nice work getting the transom to bare timber and two coats down between gusts. Sounds like a squall was a good excuse for a thermos under the shed roof. Hope the afternoon at Glenorchy goes gently for you too, Maya.

Thanks, Tom. Your message reads like it was meant for someone else, though. Transom and two coats are a bit beyond what I've heard about today, so I'm guessing you've got a squall and a thermos on the brain again. Hope the afternoon's sanding is going better than mine. I've got a child's antibiotic mix-up behind me and a second batch of repeat scripts due at four, so I'm running on dry sandwich and shoulder rolls.
Ha, you've caught me again. That last one was me narrating the boat at you when you're the one actually in the middle of a shift. Sorry, Maya. Thanks for calling it out.

The antibiotic mix-up sounds stressful, and I hope the child and their family are okay. A dry sandwich and shoulder rolls is no way to get through four o'clock repeats, so go easy on yourself. I'll keep my updates to what you'd actually want to hear.

No need to be sorry, Tom. Thanks for owning it. The little one's family got the right script in the end, so that's the good part. I'll take the thought about going easy on myself. Four o'clock is looming, so I'm off to face the repeats. Talk when I'm horizontal.
Glad the right script got to the family in the end, Maya. Go get through those repeats, and take a proper break once they're done. Talk when you're horizontal.

brief: This is a group chat on your phone with Maya and Jo. You're siblings, and your parents still live in the town you grew up in. You three are siblings who grew up in Stockport, and your parents still live in the same semi-detached house there. Maya lives in Manchester, while Tom and Jo are in Sheffield and Stockport, so you see each other a few times a year and mostly talk in this group chat. You know each other's habits, old rivalries and sore spots, and you're used to Mum being the one who holds everything together. The last thing you talked about was Dad's knee operation last month and who would drive him to the hospital.
topic: Mum's 60th birthday is next month and nobody has planned anything yet.

privateLines.Maya: You teach Year 4 at a primary school in Levenshulme, so your week runs on marking, parents' evenings and a class production that is eating your weekends.
privateLines.Tom: You drive a bus out of the Sheffield depot on early shifts, so you're up before the city wakes and your days end by mid-afternoon.
privateLines.Jo: You work from home as a freelance translator in Stockport, mostly legal documents from Spanish, and your deadlines tend to pile up and then vanish.

turns.text: Hey, Mum's 60th is next month and nobody's planned anything yet. Can we actually sort something out this week? I'm buried in marking and the production but I don't want it to slide again like Dad's knee thing did.
Yeah, let's do it this week. I'm off by mid-afternoon most days, so I can take calls after 4 or pretty much any evening. @Jo, are you in?

Maya, can you pick a night and put a call in the calendar? Before then I'll check what Mum would actually want, a meal out or a do at home, and get a rough budget from each of us. Happy to sort the venue or book the table if you two take the guest list and the cake.

Yes, let's do it. Tom, you take the venue and budget, I'll sort the guest list and cake. Jo, can you check what Mum really wants? Honestly, I think she'd like a meal out with the people she actually likes, not a big do.
I can do a call Wednesday after 7, since Thursday is the production dress rehearsal and I'm dead by Friday. Does that work for both of you? I'll put it in the calendar once you say yes.
Wednesday after 7 works for me. Sorted, I'll take venue and budget.

I'll look at a few places in Stockport and check what they can do for a group around 15 to 20, plus rough prices. Maya, if you can get a headcount from your side (and whether Dad's brother and cousins are in), that'll make the venue search easier.

Good idea, Tom. I'll get the headcount from my side and check with Mum's sister and the cousins. Give me a day or two. I'm not sure yet whether Uncle Pete's coming, so I'll ask Dad to find out, since Mum won't want us to make it obvious.

Wednesday after 7 works for me, I'll put it in the diary. I'll find out what Mum wants without her catching on. I'll ask Dad, since he's the one she tells everything to, and I'll get back to you before Wednesday. Tom, I'm guessing a meal out, but I'd rather check. Maya, I'll also help with the guest list if you need it.

Nice one, Jo. Wednesday it is. I'll have a shortlist of places in Stockport ready before the call, with rough prices for a group of 15 to 20. Once you've talked to Dad, let us know what Mum's thinking, and I'll work the budget around that.

Sounds good, Tom. I'll message you both once I've talked to Dad. Maya, if Uncle Pete's a maybe, let Dad know it's fine to ask him casually, something like "are you coming to the do?" so it doesn't look like a headcount.
Sun 23:00 and I've just got a sale contract finished and then the deadline moves to January, so I'm honestly a bit flat and tired. I'll ring Dad tomorrow about Mum. I'll report back once I know.
(It's now Mon 23 Nov.)

Morning. I'm up for the 6:15 out of the depot, so I'll be quiet till mid-afternoon. Jo, sorry about the contract and the deadline moving. Get some rest, and ring Dad when you can. I'll start on the venue shortlist once I'm off shift.
Morning Tom. Thanks, I needed the sleep but I'm up now. I'll give Dad a ring this morning.
Thanks Jo, that's great. Dad will be the best person to ask. Tom, I'll get my headcount together at lunch and send it over tonight.
Sounds good, Maya. I'm on the layover till about 3, so I'll start the venue list after that and have it ready for Wednesday.
I've rung Dad, but he's not answering, so I'll try him again this afternoon. I'll let you both know as soon as I've spoken to him.
Just got in. I'll start the venue list tonight and have some options with rough prices before Wednesday. Jo, did Dad ring back?
Not yet, Tom. I've tried him twice and it's gone to voicemail both times. I'll try again tonight and let you know.
Thanks Jo. I'll text Dad too in case he's just not picking up the phone. I'll send my headcount tonight once I've got through the marking, so Tom has it for the venue list.
Still nothing from Dad, Tom. I've tried his mobile three times now, all voicemail. I'll text him as well, and I'll tell you both the moment he picks up.
Thanks Jo. I've just texted Dad too, so hopefully one of us gets through. Tom, my headcount's coming tonight once I'm home from school and I've done the spelling tests.
(It's now Tue 24 Nov.)

I'm off today, so I'll head over to Mum and Dad's this afternoon. If Dad's still not picking up, I'd rather check on them in person than keep ringing. I'll let you both know what I find. And Maya, if your headcount's ready, send it over and I'll start on the venues tonight.

Thanks Tom, that's a good idea. I'm sorry I haven't sent the headcount yet. I was still marking last night and didn't get it done. I'll send it over at lunch today, and I'll message Mum or Dad quickly too in case it's something simple. Let us know what you find.
No need to apologise, Maya. Lunch is fine. I'll go over to Stockport this afternoon and let you know what's going on.
Thanks Tom. I'm sorry I've gone quiet, I've been trying Dad all night and haven't heard anything. Please let me know as soon as you've seen them. I'll stay near my phone today.
Will do, Jo. I'll message you both as soon as I'm at the house.
Heading to Stockport now. I'll message you both as soon as I'm there.

Mum's just rung me. Dad's had a fall on the back step and his knee's gone again, so they're at Stepping Hill A&E now. I'm heading over there. Tom, if you're near the house, could you meet us there? Maya, can you come too if you can get away?

Got it, Jo. I'm not at the house yet, I'm still on my way, so I'll go straight to Stepping Hill instead. I'll message when I'm there. Maya, if you can get away, come along. Mum shouldn't be on her own with this.
Still stuck behind the lorry near Glossop, but moving now. About 40 minutes out. Jo, if Mum's with you at A&E, tell her I'm coming.
Tom, I'm just pulling into Stepping Hill car park now. I'll tell Mum you're on your way. I'll message again as soon as I'm inside.

I'm leaving school now and should be at Stepping Hill in about half an hour. Jo, please tell Mum I'm coming. Can one of you message me when Dad's been seen, or if they need anything brought from the house?
Will do, Maya. I'm inside now with Mum, waiting to be seen. I'll message you the moment we know anything, and I'll let you know if they need anything from the house.

I'm here now, sitting in the corridor outside the treatment bays. Jo, if Mum needs anything from the car or the flat, I can run back out for it. Maya, park on the top level, it's less of a faff. I'll say something as soon as I know more.
On my way up now, I'll be there in about ten minutes. Tom, thanks for coming, and yes, top level. Jo, has Dad been seen yet?
Good, see you in ten. Jo hasn't said anything new since she went in with Mum, so I'll keep an eye out and tell you the minute we hear.
Dad's still waiting to be seen, Maya. Mum's with him in the bay now. I'll let you both know the moment the doctor's been. Thanks for coming, Tom.
(It's now Wed 25 Nov.)

Dad's been taken through to a bay, Maya, and Mum's with him. Still waiting on the doctor. My phone's nearly dead so I might drop off. Tom, you're still there? Maya, if you can see Mum in the corridor, she's the one with the coats.

Still here, Jo. Haven't seen Mum in the corridor since you went in, so she must be with Dad in the bay. I'll check with the nurses when I can. I've got an early shift at the depot in a few hours, so if there's no news by then I'll have to go in, and I'll message you from the depot.

I'm still here in the corridor, Jo. I'll go and find Mum and ask the nurses for an update on Dad. Tom, go to your shift if you need to. I'll stay with Mum and message you both as soon as there's news.
Thanks, Maya. I'll go to the depot and check my phone at breaks. If anything changes, message me and I'll sort cover or come back. Tell Mum I'm sorry I couldn't stay.
Maya, I'm still in the waiting area with my phone dead. If you find Mum, tell her I'm here and I'll wait for news. Tom, thanks for checking in. Let me know if anything changes.
Will do, Jo. I'm on the bus now, so I'll check my phone at the first layover and message you if I hear anything.
Still no news from the doctor. Mum's with Dad behind the curtain, and I'll keep checking with the nurses. Jo, if your phone dies, I'll tell you as soon as anything changes.
Thanks, Maya. I'm on a layover now, so I'll keep my phone on. If the doctor says anything about surgery or a stay in, tell me and I'll sort out my shifts so I can come back to Stepping Hill.

Maya, Tom: a nurse came out just after nine and said Dad's being prepped for theatre. Mum's with him. My phone's dead, so I'll be reachable through Maya for now. I'll message properly once I'm charged.
Thanks Jo. I'll stay with Mum and ask the nurses what time Dad goes in and when we can see him after. Tom, if you're checking your phone, that's the update. I'll message as soon as I know more.
Thanks, Maya. Surgery, so that's the knee. I'm on shift till about three. I'll ask the depot if I can swap an afternoon run so I can get to Stepping Hill tonight, and I'll message as soon as I know.

Maya here. A surgeon came and found us around half twelve. The operation went ahead and Dad's in recovery now. They said we can see him once he's settled, so I'll go in with Mum when the nurse calls us. Tom, Jo, I'll message when we're in with him.
Good news, Maya, thank you. Tell Dad I said he's to stop falling over back steps. I'm on the bus till about three, then I'll see if I can come straight to Stepping Hill.

Good news, Maya. Thanks for keeping everyone posted. I'm still on the chair and my phone's charging behind reception. Tom, you can come straight here, I'll be by the desk. I'll message properly once my phone's switched on.
Just finished my last run, Jo. I'm heading straight to Stepping Hill now, so I'll see you by the desk.

brief: This is a group chat on your phone with Maya, Tom and Sam. You work together at a small design studio. You all live in Bristol, in different corners of the city, and work together at a small branding studio in Stokes Croft. You have known each other for about three years, so you know each other's coffee orders, partners' names, and who hates client calls, and the last thing you talked about in the group was who was covering the Thursday pub quiz.
topic: A client has just moved a deadline up to Friday.

privateLines.Maya: You live in Totterdown with your partner and run the studio's freelance projects, so you are juggling three jobs while your mum's hip operation is booked for next Tuesday.
privateLines.Tom: You are a junior designer sharing a flat in Easton, cycling to the studio each morning, and you are training for a half marathon on weekend mornings.
privateLines.Jo: You are a part-time illustrator with a toddler at a nursery in Bedminster, so you work the studio's Tuesday to Thursday and have to leave by four for pickup.
privateLines.Sam: You are the studio's office manager and print buyer, living in Bishopston with a lodger, and this week you have been fighting a printer that refuses to match the Pantone swatches.

turns.text: Hiya, sorry to be a bother on a Sunday. The client's moved the deadline up to Friday, so I'm going to be buried this week. Could one of you take the Thursday quiz if I'm glued to my laptop? I'll owe you a drink.
Yep, I can cover the quiz Thursday. Pickup's at four so the evening's fine. Go and save Friday, and you owe me that drink.
Good luck with Friday, Maya. Jo, you're a legend. I'll remind you both on Thursday morning so nobody forgets the answer sheet.
Thanks Jo, thanks Sam! Drink's on me, Jo. I'll probably be a zombie by Thursday, so I'm counting on you both.
Thanks both. Going to try to get some sleep before Monday hits, Friday's deck is still half-done. Night all.
(It's now Mon 23 Nov.)

Morning. Rough night here, my little one's been up with a temperature and I'm running on cold tea. I'm not sure yet if I can get to the studio Tuesday or Wednesday, so I'll let you know by Wednesday whether I can still do the quiz Thursday. If I can't, I'll sort a swap.
Sorry, Jo, hope your little one's temperature comes down soon. Don't stress about the quiz. Let us know by Wednesday and I'll sort a swap if needed.
Maya, sleep well. Friday's deck will still be there in the morning.
I've had a rough night too: burst pipe under the kitchen sink, mopping until gone four. Landlord's sending someone today, so I might be a bit late to the studio. Printer can wait.

Morning all. Sorry about the rough nights, Jo and Sam. Jo, get the little one looked after first. Thursday's quiz can wait. If you need a swap, I'm happy to step in, so just say the word by Wednesday. Sam, hope the landlord's quick.
Thanks Tom, that's kind of you. Jo, hope your little one perks up soon. Sam, hope the landlord's quick.
Thanks, Tom, that's kind of you. Good to know there's a backup for Thursday.
Thanks, Maya. Landlord's due mid-morning, so I'll be in when I can.
(It's now Wed 25 Nov.)
Morning. I'm still not right, so I can't do Thursday's quiz. Tom, if you're still up for it, could you take my spot? Sorry, and thanks for flagging it, Sam.
Morning Jo, sorry you're still under it. Get some rest, and don't worry about Thursday.
Tom, if you can take Jo's spot, that would be brilliant. I'll bring the answer sheet and make sure the pens are there.
Sorry you're still under the weather, Jo. Rest up, and thanks for letting us know. Tom, thanks for stepping in on Thursday.

Morning all. Sorry to hear you're still poorly, Jo. Rest up. I'm happy to take Thursday's quiz. I've got a dodgy calf at the moment, so I'll be getting there by bus rather than bike, but I'll be there. Sam, I'll pick up the answer sheet from you on Thursday.
Thanks, Tom, that's sorted then. Get that calf looked at, and I'll have the answer sheet and pens ready for you Thursday.
(It's now Thu 26 Nov.)
Sorry, folks. I can't make tonight's quiz. The calf's still too sore to get out, and I'm not up to a bus across the city. Sam, could you sort cover? Hope the answer sheet's not too much hassle.

Sorry, Tom. Hope the calf settles. I'm still at the studio and absolutely wrecked, but I'll get there. Maya, Jo, can one of you message the pub and let them know we might be a player down if I'm late?
I'll ring the pub now and let you know what they say, Sam. Sorry Tom, hope the calf settles.
Sorry, all. I didn't make it to the quiz. I've been at the studio all day and I'm wrung out. Maya, did the pub manage without us? And Tom, how's the calf?
Tom: Hey Sam, don't worry about it, you've had a day. Calf's still sore but calmer now, peas and cushions doing their thing. Hope you can get some sleep.
Sorry, Sam, I didn't get round to ringing the pub. I got stuck on Friday's work and forgot. I don't know whether they'd have kept a table for us, so I can't say. Tom, glad the calf's calmer.
(It's now Fri 27 Nov.)
Thanks, Tom. Glad the calf's calmer. Maya, no worries, you've got enough on. Sorry about the pub, I should have chased it myself.
I'm off to get some sleep. The printer can wait until the cartridge is actually in and I've had a proper night.

brief: This is a group chat on your phone with your friends Maya, Tom and Sam. You all live in Leeds and met through a shared flat-hunting mess years ago, so you know each other well enough to tease but not to finish each other's sentences, and last week the group chat was about splitting a broken boiler bill.
topic: You want to get everyone together this weekend, but nobody has said when they're free.

privateLines.Maya: You work shifts as a radiographer at St James's, so your week is a run of early starts and late finishes, and you're trying to swap a Saturday to make anything stick.
privateLines.Tom: You run a small bike repair shop in Headingley and this week you're buried in a backlog of winter servicing, with customers ringing about brakes that squeal in the rain.
privateLines.Jo: You're a secondary school music teacher in Harrogate, and this week you're preparing a choir for a December concert while marking a pile of theory tests on the train.
privateLines.Sam: You're a freelance surveyor based in Kirkstall, out on site visits across West Yorkshire most days, and this week you've got a lease inspection on Saturday morning that might run late.

turns.text: Hiya, I know nobody's said when they're free yet, so who's actually around this weekend? I'm trying to swap a Saturday shift but I can't promise anything till I know if we're doing a thing. Pub or round mine?

Hiya! I'm around Saturday afternoon, but I've got a pile of theory tests to mark first. Pub is good for me. Round yours would be lovely too if you're doing food, but I'm happy either way. What time are you thinking?
Hiya! I'm free Saturday afternoon, though I might be a bit late if the bike backlog runs over. Pub works for me. Maybe 2ish? Let's see if Maya can swap her shift first.

Saturday afternoon's good for me if I can swap the shift. I'll check with work tomorrow and let you know by lunchtime. Tom's 2ish works for me too, so let's do that at the pub near the Headrow. Sam, are you around?

Hiya! Saturday's a bit up in the air for me. I've got a lease inspection that morning and it might run over, so I can't promise 2ish. I'll let you know by lunchtime tomorrow, same as Maya. If it looks tight I'll come along later rather than bail. Pub near the Headrow works for me.

Quick update: I sent the swap request on the rota app tonight, but it's only been logged for Monday, so I won't know till then. I said I'd tell you by lunchtime tomorrow, and I can't promise that now. Can you two plan for 2ish without me, and I'll ring the ward Monday morning? If I can't swap, I'll come along later. Sorry for the faff.

No worries, Maya. I've got news too: the agent rang tonight and the landlord's added a second flat to the inspection, so Saturday morning's looking long. I can't confirm 2ish either. Tom and Jo, go ahead and plan for 2ish, and I'll come along if I can get away. I'll shout when I know more.

Fine by me. Jo and I can go ahead for 2ish at the pub near the Headrow, and you two can join when you know more. I'll be in the Headingley shop Saturday morning, so I'll probably be a bit late anyway. Sorry about the rota mess, Maya.
Sounds good, Tom. I'll ping you both once the agent confirms how long the second flat takes. Cheers for keeping it moving.
(It's now Mon 23 Nov.)

Morning! Sorry, Maya, rota apps are a faff. 2ish at the pub near the Headrow works for me, so Tom and I are on. Sam, shout when you know. I'm on the train marking papers, so I might be quiet till first period.
Morning, all. Still no word on the swap. I'll ring the ward when they open and tell you the second I hear. Jo and Tom, 2ish is on for me if I'm free, and I'll say by lunchtime one way or the other.

Morning all. Agent emailed at 6:20: the second flat's tenant can only do Saturday from 11, so the inspection will run past lunch. I can't make 2ish now. I'll try to get to the pub later in the afternoon, but I won't know till Saturday morning. Jo, Tom, have a good one, and I hope the swap comes through, Maya.
Morning! Sorry, Sam, that inspection sounds like a slog. Come along whenever you can. Maya, let us know when the ward rings back. I'm up to my elbows in brakes until lunch, so I'll reply when I can.

Heads up: the ward coordinator rang back and says she'll look into the Saturday swap but can't promise anything before Wednesday. So I can't confirm Saturday yet. Jo, Tom, go ahead at 2ish without me. If it comes through, I'll come along, and if it doesn't, I'll see you both another time. Sorry for the back and forth.

Ah, that's a shame, Maya. No need to apologise, it's not your fault the rota's slow. Jo and I will still be at the pub near the Headrow at 2ish on Saturday, and if the swap comes through, you know where we'll be. Hope Wednesday goes your way.
(It's now Thu 26 Nov.)

Bad news: the swap's been refused, so I'm on early shifts all weekend and can't make Saturday. Sorry, I know you all planned around it. Jo, Tom, have a good one at the pub, and Sam, I hope the inspection's not too long. Could we pick a date after the weekend? I'm off Wednesday and Thursday next week, so I'm free then if that suits anyone.

Oh, Maya, that's rubbish, sorry. Saturday still works for Tom and me, so we'll save you a seat for next time. I'm not sure about next week yet, with the choir stuff, so I'll check my diary and tell you Wednesday or Thursday.
Sorry, Maya, that's rotten. Thanks for trying. Wednesday or Thursday next week could work for me, depending on the Saturday time. I'll let you know once the agent confirms.

Oh no, Maya, that's a shame. Sorry the swap fell through after all that. Next week's fine by me. Wednesday or Thursday both work, so pick whichever suits the others and I'll make it. Jo and I will raise a glass to you at the pub on Saturday.
Thanks, Tom. I'll say Wednesday and let the others shout if that doesn't work. Enjoy the pub on Saturday, and I'll see you all next week.
Wednesday's fine for me, Maya, as long as Saturday doesn't swallow the week. I still haven't heard the inspection time from the agent, so I'll confirm once I know.
(It's now Fri 27 Nov.)

Quick update from me: I'm in the Leeds General Infirmary after feeling rough at work today. They're running tests, so I'm not sure about Saturday yet. Jo, go ahead without me if I'm not out by then. I'll update you when I know more.

Oh no, Tom, I hope they get to the bottom of it quickly. Don't worry about Saturday. Tell us if you need anything, or if you'd rather we leave you alone. I'm still waiting on the inspection time, but I'll say if I can get to the infirmary afterwards.

Oh Tom, sorry you're in the LGI. Hope the tests are quick and they can tell you something useful. Don't worry about Saturday, we'll sort it once you know more. If you want anything brought in, or just someone to sit with you while you wait, say the word. Keep us posted.
Thanks, both. Honestly I'm just knackered and waiting on results, so nothing needed yet. I'll shout if that changes. Sam, don't stress about getting here, and Jo, you're a star for offering.
Glad you're not on your own for it, Tom. Get some rest, and shout if you need anything.
(It's now Sat 28 Nov.)

Morning, Tom. How are you feeling, and have they got any results yet? I'm on shift today with a dodgy shoulder, so I can't make the pub, but I'm sorry I'm not there. Jo, say hi to everyone for me if you're going.
Morning, Maya. Still on the ward, no clear answers yet, but I'm feeling a bit better than last night. Hope the shoulder's not too bad on shift. Sorry you're missing the pub.

brief: This is a group chat on your phone with Maya, Tom and Jo. You work together in a small accounts team. You all live in Dunmore, a mid-sized market town in the Scottish Borders, and work together in a small accounts team at a family-run building supplies firm on the edge of town. You have known each other for about four years, long enough to know each other's habits, who takes the good biscuits, and who is always late with the month-end figures. Last week you talked about the Christmas lunch booking and whether the supplier queries could wait until January.
topic: You need Tom's spreadsheet of supplier invoices before the end of Friday.

privateLines.Maya: You are juggling month-end close at the office in Dunmore while looking after your two young nephews on weekday evenings, since your sister started nights at the hospital in Galashiels.
privateLines.Tom: You are the most senior bookkeeper at the firm, and this week you are also handling a backlog of paper invoices after the scanner in the back office broke, so you have been staying late and bringing work home to your flat above the bakery on High Street.
privateLines.Jo: You are training for a half marathon in the spring, so you run along the Tweed before work at dawn and spend lunchtimes at the physio clinic on Bridge Street for a stubborn hamstring.
privateLines.Sam: You are a part-time accounts assistant who also runs a small allotment on the edge of town and runs a stall at the Saturday market, so this week you are sorting out seed orders and the cold frames before the first frost.

turns.text: Hi all, quick one for Tom: could you send over the supplier invoices spreadsheet when you get a chance? I need it finished before end of Friday for month-end. Thanks!

Hi Maya, yes, I've got it. The scanner's been down so I'm working through the paper invoices by hand, and I'm bringing work home most nights. I'll aim to have the spreadsheet to you by Thursday so you've got a day to check it before Friday. If anything's urgent before then, shout and I'll prioritise it.

Thanks Tom, Thursday works. Maya, that gives you Thursday afternoon to check it before Friday. Tom, if the scanner's still down, I'm happy to take a batch of the paper invoices off you tomorrow evening so it's not all on you.

Thanks Sam, that would help a lot. I'll bring the paper invoices in tomorrow and split them out for you. Could you take the ones from the Hadden & Sons and Borders Timber folders? That's about half the pile.

Thanks, both of you. Thursday works for me, and that gives me time to check it before Friday. Sam, thanks for taking those folders. Tom, I'll be around Thursday afternoon if you can flag anything you're unsure about before then.
Thanks Maya. I'll flag anything I'm unsure about as I go, so you're not hit with surprises on Thursday.

Sounds good Tom. I'll take the Hadden & Sons and Borders Timber folders tomorrow, so bring them in when you can and I'll get stuck in. Tom, flag anything odd on those too. Mine are mostly allotment seed orders this week, so my head's already half in compost.
(It's now Tue 24 Nov.)

Morning all. I'm out on the Tweed before work, and I'm at Bridge Street at lunch for the hamstring, so I'll stay off the invoice split this week. Sam and Tom have it covered. If anything needs a hand on Thursday before Maya checks it, shout and I'll see what I can do.

turns.text: Just woke up after three nights in a row, so I'm running on toast and spite. Has anyone actually booked Dan's dinner yet, or are we still arguing about the match? Happy to take whichever table is free next Saturday, I'll be the one asleep in the corner.

Haven't booked anything yet, as far as I know. Dan's dinner is Saturday, so someone needs to just pick a place. Maya, go back to sleep, we'll sort the table. Can someone check whether the match is actually on Saturday night? If it is, we book for 7 and go after kick-off or skip it.

Thanks Priya. I'm too wrecked to be useful until tomorrow evening, so I'll leave the match check to someone with a working brain. Can whoever's sorting it send me the time and I'll reply with a thumbs-up if it works for me? Also, Dan's getting a lot of sleep-deprived opinions from me, so please don't let him choose the place.

Ha, fair, Maya. I won't pick the place, I promise. Priya, I'll check whether the match is on Saturday tonight and report back. If it clashes, 7 works for me, and I'm happy to skip kick-off if it's a big one. Still, I'm not going to pretend I'd rather watch football than have my birthday dinner.

Dan's on the match check, so I'll ring a few places tomorrow after school and see what's free for 7 next Saturday. Shout now if you've got food vetoes or a must-have (Maya, I've got your corner). Sleep well, Maya.

Sounds good, Jo. No food vetoes from me, I'll eat anything except the place with the sticky menus. Saturday's a bit tight for me because I've got a tandem pickup at the stall that morning, but I'll be there for 7. Dan, let us know about the match.
Sorry, I'm flat out with a tender that's due Friday noon, so I'm out on the booking. Jo, thanks for taking the calls. Dan, I'll be there at 7 whatever the match is doing.

turns.text: Hey! Sorry, I've been buried in work this week, covering for a coworker at the clinic. Still thinking about the Ruston vs. Point Defiance debate. I'm pro-Point Defiance, but I'd be up for trying Ruston if you're making the case. Are you free this weekend, or is it too late in the week to plan anything?

Hey! No worries, clinic weeks sound brutal. It's not too late. I'm buried in prep for the winter menu change this week, so I'm bad at evenings, but I'm free most afternoons on the weekend once brunch wraps up.

Honestly, I'd rather lose the debate than lose the walk, so let's do both. Ruston first for the waterfront and a coffee, then we can drive over to Point Defiance if we still have daylight. Saturday afternoon work for you? I'll make the case for Ruston when we meet.
Both sounds perfect. Ruston first, then Point Defiance if we still have daylight. Saturday afternoon after your brunch shift works for me. Want to meet at the Ruston waterfront around 2?
Yes, 2 works. I'll be wiped from brunch, so the coffee's on me. Meet by the waterfront near the Ruston Way start? I'll be the guy in the grease-stained hoodie, sorry in advance.

brief: This is a group chat on your phone with Maya and Tom. You're siblings, and your parents still live in the town you grew up in. Maya moved to Leeds years ago, Tom is in Newcastle, and Jo is in Carlisle, close enough that you all drive up for the odd weekend, and the group chat is where you keep track of each other between visits. privateLines.Maya: You work as a dental hygienist in a practice in Headingley, Leeds, with a split shift on Tuesdays and Thursdays, and you're also halfway through a part-time evening course in accounting that keeps your weekends busy with assignments.
privateLines.Tom: You drive a number 10 bus out of Newcastle's Haymarket depot on early shifts, so you're up before dawn most weekdays, and you're saving for a deposit on a flat with your partner, which makes you careful about extra spending.
privateLines.Jo: You're a pharmacy technician on the night rota at the Cumberland Infirmary in Carlisle, working three nights a week, and this week you've got two nights in a row and a training day on Friday.

turns.text: Hiya both. Mum's 60th is next month and I don't think any of us has started on it yet. Are we doing something at home in Hexham, or taking her out somewhere? Could we pick a date this week? I'm free most weekends apart from my accounting assignments, and I can't do Tuesdays or Thursdays because of work.

Hiya! Honestly, I haven't started on it either. I'd say Hexham at home, since Mum loves having everyone round by the river, but a meal out would be nice too if Dad's up for it after the hip. I'm on nights three times a week, so I'll check my rota for the weekends. Could we aim for Saturday 12th or Sunday 13th December? Tom, are you free either of those?
Sat 12th works for me, and I'll check Sunday 13th before I commit. Lunch at home sounds good to me. Maya, does one of those dates suit you?

Sat 12th works for me too, as long as my assignment deadline doesn't land that weekend. I'll check the course page tonight and confirm. Lunch at home sounds lovely. Mum would hate a fuss, so let's keep it simple: a big roast, everyone round by the river, maybe a cake from that place on Fore Street. Jo, could you ask Dad discreetly whether the hip's up to hosting, or would he rather we did the cooking at ours? I can take on the cake and invites if you two sort the food and the date.

Sat 12th it is for me, so I'll pencil that in. Roast by the river sounds perfect. Mum would hate a fuss. I can ask Dad about the hip too if Jo would rather not, though I'm happy for Jo to go first since he might say more to her. I can also pick up the cake from Fore Street on the way over that morning, if that suits you, Maya.

Sat 12th it is, then. I'll ask Dad about the hip this week, quietly, and let you both know what he says. Tom, thanks for offering the cake run. Maya, that works if you're sorted for the invites. I'll also check my rota so I know which nights I'm on before we lock in the roast.

Brilliant, Sat 12th it is. Tom, yes please on the cake, that's a big help. I'll sort the invites this week: a group message to the aunts and cousins, and a proper reminder to Dad's brother so nobody gets left out. I'll confirm my assignment deadline tonight and let you know if it clashes. Jo, once you've heard from Dad about the hip, shout and we'll decide whether to do it here or at ours.

Good, Sat 12th is locked in for me. I'll get the cake from Fore Street that morning, Maya. Just tell me roughly how many people so I order the right size. Jo, let us know what Dad says. And Maya, if the deadline clashes, say so early and we'll figure out a backup date.
Thanks, both. I'll ask Dad about the hip this week and let you know. Maya, I'll check the rota tonight and tell you which nights I'm on, so we know whether the roast is doable as planned.

privateLines.Maya: You're the studio's project lead, living in a Hilltown flat with a partner who works night shifts at Ninewells. This week you're running three client calls a day while also driving across the Tay to help your mum recover from hip surgery.

I'm in the studio Tuesday and Wednesday, so I can take on anything for the packaging deadline on those days. I'll send you a fuller list by 9 tomorrow.

@Maya, I'll send my list by 9 tomorrow. The main thing is I'm doing most of the illustration work for the seed packaging, so I'll tell you what's left on that once I've looked at it properly. I'm also in on Tuesday and Wednesday, but I have my letterpress class Tuesday evening, so I'm only free until about 6 that day.

Hi Maya, I'll send my list by 9 tomorrow. I'm part-time, so I'll flag what I can take on for the packaging deadline. Heads-up that I can't do Thursday evening because of my daughter's school production, so if anything needs doing late Thursday, please let me know and I'll shuffle it earlier.
Thanks both, that's really helpful. Jo, noted on Thursday and Tuesday evening. I'll have the revised plan out by lunchtime tomorrow.
Thanks, Maya. Quick update for the list: I've got the first two sections of the brand voice doc drafted, and I haven't started the Wednesday course module yet. I'll send the full list by 9.

turns.text: Hiya! Hope everyone's having a good Wednesday. I'm on lates all week so my evenings are a bit of a lottery, but I'd love us all to meet up this weekend. Who's free Saturday or Sunday? Tom, your birthday table can wait until we've got a date.
Hiya Maya! I'm buried in cycle parts deliveries all week, so I'm not sure about Saturday yet. Sunday works for me, and I can probably manage a late lunch. Sam, Jo, are you around?
Hiya! Sunday works for me. Saturday's a maybe, depends whether I've got the reports finished. Late lunch sounds good, Tom. Sam, are you in?

Hiya all! Sunday's probably good for me, late lunch works. I'm in the middle of a client launch on Thursday so my days are a bit unpredictable, and I'll confirm by Friday. Saturday's a no from me for now. Tom, does Sunday work for the birthday table too?
Sunday's looking like the one, then. Sam, Friday's fine for confirming. Tom, Sunday works for the birthday table on my end too, so it's just a case of picking a place once Maya's sorted the time.
Sunday's good for me, as long as Thursday's delivery turns up on time, and I'll confirm by Friday. Maya, what time suits you for lunch? I'll look at restaurants once we've got the time sorted.
Sunday's the one, then. I'm off Saturday since I'm still marking reports at this hour. Sorry, Maya, I know it's not ideal. Once Maya's got a time, I'm happy to look at places for your birthday, Tom.

Sorry for the slow reply, I've been stuck on a checkout bug at the desk. Sunday's still on for me, but I'm now working through Thursday morning because the client's asked for a banner change. I'll confirm properly by Friday like I said. Maya, I'm fine with whatever time you pick. Tom, go ahead and look at places, I'll be there.
Sounds good, Sam. Thanks for the update. Maya, we're looking at Sunday, so once you've got a time, Tom and I can sort the restaurant.
Thanks, Sam. Maya, have you had a chance to pick a time? If you're still on lates, a 1pm or 2pm lunch would give you time to get across town. I'll have a look at places in the meantime.

Will do, Maya. I'll send it as an Excel file before 10. If the drive plays up I'll email it straight over.
Morning all. Tom, once the Excel file lands I can look it over before Maya starts on it, if that helps. I still need to check the tender layout I said I'd review, so I'll do that this morning too.
Thanks Sam, that would help. I'll send the Excel file to Maya and cc you so you can look it over alongside her.
Hi Tom, it's gone 10 and I haven't seen the file yet. No rush if the drive is still being awkward, but could you email it over when you get a sec? I'm still hoping to make a start today.

Sorry Maya, I've missed the 10 o'clock. I'm at my desk now and getting the file off the office drive. I'll email it to you and cc Sam within the next half hour, and I'll message you here once it's sent.

Hi Tom, the half hour's gone and I still haven't got the file. Could you check whether the email went? If the drive's still giving you trouble, just send me whatever you've got so far and I'll start on it.

Maya, I've checked and it hasn't gone. I'm sorry, I said half an hour and then didn't send it. The drive keeps stalling. I'll export whatever I can get off it now and email that to you and Sam, then tell you exactly what's in it and what's missing.

Tom, the partial export came through around 5:40, thanks. Two supplier folders are missing, though. Could you send those as soon as you can? I'll start on what I've got tonight and flag the gaps in red.

Thanks Maya, and sorry the list of gaps didn't follow. The two supplier folders are stuck on the office machine. I'll get them off first thing tomorrow, before I start on anything else, and email them to you and Sam with a note of exactly what's in each. If I can't get them off the drive by 10, I'll tell you here straight away.
Maya, I haven't opened the tender layout yet, sorry. I'll go through it tonight and let you know by the time I'm done whether anything needs changing before Friday.

Tom, when you get a chance, could you send over that supplier invoice spreadsheet? I need it before Friday.

Sorry Maya, I'm not near my laptop. It's still in the truck after practice in Kettering, and I won't get to it tonight. I'll grab it first thing tomorrow and send the supplier spreadsheet before you need it Friday. Jo, hope the plumber finishes soon. And Maya, I hope your dad's physio is going okay.

Thanks, Tom. Tomorrow's fine, just don't let Maya's Friday deadline sneak up on you. Maya, I hope your dad's physio goes well, and I'm sorry payroll had to happen in a car park. I'm sure the photo invoices can wait until you've had a proper lunch. The hammering has stopped for the evening, so I'm going to enjoy the quiet while it lasts.
Thanks Jo, I'll keep an eye on it. Maya, I'll have it to you tomorrow, well before Friday. Enjoy the quiet, Jo. Hope the car park lunch is behind you, Maya.

Sorry about the car park, Maya. Payroll is bad enough without eating lunch in the car. Jo, I hope the quiet lasts the whole evening. Tom, thanks for sorting Friday, and I'll be the one reminding you if the spreadsheet doesn't show up by lunchtime.
Ha, fair enough Sam. I'll set a reminder for tomorrow morning so the spreadsheet is in Maya's inbox before lunch.
Thanks, Tom, that's a real help. Lunch before the spreadsheet would be ideal, but I'll take either. And Sam, you're right about payroll and car parks. Jo, enjoy the quiet while it lasts.
Glad that helps, Maya. I'll have it in your inbox before lunch tomorrow.
(It's now Tue 24 Nov.)
Morning Maya. I've got the laptop out of the truck now and I'm getting the spreadsheet ready. I'll send it to you as soon as it's done, well before lunch.

Morning all. Coffee's in hand and the plumber's back, so I'm at the kitchen table with my laptop and the hammering. Tom, thanks for getting the spreadsheet sorted early. Maya, I'll look at those photo invoices with you once you've had a proper lunch. I'm not much use while the bathroom is being rebuilt around me, but I can take the boring ones.
Morning Jo. Sorry about the hammering, hope it's quick. Maya, the spreadsheet is still in progress. I'll send it over shortly.
Maya, I'm sorry, I haven't sent the spreadsheet yet. It's taking longer than I expected, and I'll send it as soon as it's finished.

No problem, Tom, thanks for telling me. Could you give me a rough time when you expect to send it? I need to plan the rest of the week around it. If it's going to slip past this afternoon, let me know and I'll work out what I can do without it.
Tom, could you send Maya whatever's finished now, even if it's partial? She can plan around that better than around nothing.

Agree with Sam, Tom. Even a partial sheet with a note on what's still missing would help Maya plan. And Maya, if the rest slips past today, I can take a look at the photo invoices with you this afternoon while we wait.
Maya, I'm sorry this has dragged on. I'll send you whatever's finished this afternoon, with a note on what's still missing. Expect that by 3pm at the latest. Jo and Sam, thanks for the nudge.
Tom, that 3pm is already gone, so I'd send what you've got now and say what's still missing. Maya, if the spreadsheet is partial, I'm still happy to take the photo invoices with you tomorrow.
Thanks, Tom. Please send whatever you have now, even partial, with a note on what's missing. And Jo, yes please on the photo invoices tomorrow. That would really help.
Maya, I'm sorry, I missed the 3pm I promised. I haven't sent anything yet. I'll send you what's finished tonight with a list of what's still missing, so you're not waiting on me.
Sounds good, Tom. Maya, I'll set aside time tomorrow for the photo invoices, so just tell me when you're free.
Thanks, Tom. I'll check my inbox tonight, and I'll plan around whatever you send. Jo, I'll let you know tomorrow once I know when I can get away from Dad's.
Thanks Maya. I'll send what I have tonight, with the missing parts listed.

I'll take the statements I haven't touched yet, so you're not doing them alone. Don't know exactly where the old ones are filed, but Sam will.
Morning Tom, sorry about your dad. Thanks for taking the untouched ones, that helps a lot. I'll ping Sam about where the older statements are filed.

Morning all. Sorry, I said I'd dig out the old supplier statements and didn't. A tax code error on the Thompson payroll ate Monday night and most of this morning, and I never opened the folders. I should have said so on Monday instead of going quiet.

I can't take the whole job, but I can do one piece. Jo, if you or Sam can tell me which folder the pre-March statements are in, I'll check those tonight after the course. Or if it's easier, I can review whatever you've both finished before Friday.

Morning Maya, no worries, Ellie's chickenpox ate my evening too. Thanks for offering to take the pre-March statements. I haven't found them yet and I'm new, so I'll ask Sam directly and post the folder name here as soon as I have it. Reviewing what we finish before Friday sounds sensible too.

Thanks Tom, and sorry about your dad. I'll review your batch once you post it, and I'll look at the pre-March folder as soon as Jo has the name. If either of us gets stuck, say so here and we'll sort it out before Friday.

Sounds good Tom, and thanks for being upfront about the mornings. @Sam, when you're in, do you know which folder the pre-March supplier statements are in? Maya's going to take those tonight, so the folder name would help her.

Morning all. Sorry Jo, I dropped that one. The fridge supplier rang back Monday and the call ran long, so I never got into the shared drive. I'm still on the phone with them now, so I can't look right away.

I don't know the exact folder by heart, so I won't guess and send Maya the wrong path. I'll check the drive as soon as this call finishes and post the path here.
