turns.text: Hiya all. I'm about to head out for a night shift at the Hally, so I'm on my phone for another 20 mins or so. Has anyone heard whether the Fat Cat is still doing Dan's meal on Thursday, or do we need to move it?
Haven't heard anything, sorry. I'll ask Claude to check the Fat Cat's kitchen hours for Thursday.
Good call, Jo. Thanks for checking, and Maya, have a good shift.

@claude Does the Fat Cat in Sheffield (Alma Street) have any changes to its kitchen hours or Thursday food service, like closing early? Please check their website or recent reviews and tell me what you find.

I couldn't find any announced change to the Fat Cat's kitchen hours or Thursday food service, and I couldn't find any notice of early closing. That isn't confirmation that nothing has changed.

- **Pub website (thefatcat.co.uk):** It gives general opening hours only. Sunday to Thursday is 12pm–11:30pm, Friday is 12pm–12:30am and Saturday is 11am–12:30am. It has no kitchen hours, no Thursday food details and no notices. It links to Facebook and Twitter, but I didn't check those.
- **Tripadvisor:** Thursday is listed as 12pm–11:30pm, with no separate kitchen hours. The only Thursday review is from June 2022 and is a complaint about the food. It says nothing about hours or closing early. I found no recent reviews on the kitchen hours.
- **Other listings:** Welcome to Sheffield gives Monday to Thursday as 12pm–11pm, which doesn't match the pub's own site. One guide says food is served "lunchtimes and early evening", which isn't a schedule.
- **Possible change at the site:** A search result mentioned a Sheffield City Council planning submission for a change of use to a restaurant with a "seafood-based food offer". I couldn't see its date, whether it relates to this pub, or whether it was approved. I didn't open the page.

To be sure of Thursday food times, call the pub. The website lists 0114 249 4803, and a search listing showed 0114 249 4801, so check which is right. You could also email info@thefatcat.co.uk or look at their Facebook page.

Sources:
- [The Fat Cat website](https://www.thefatcat.co.uk)
- [Tripadvisor listing](https://www.tripadvisor.com/--d733654.html)
- [Welcome to Sheffield](https://welcometosheffield.co.uk/content/food-drink-and-nightlife/the-fat-cat)
- [TripAligner](https://tripaligner.com/countries/united-kingdom-34/destinations/sheffield-12564/places/fat-cat-733654)

Claude found no announced change to the Fat Cat's Thursday food or early closing. The website only lists general hours (Thursday 12pm to 11:30pm), with no kitchen hours. The most recent Thursday review is from 2022. Its Facebook page is worth a look too.
Best bet is to ring them before we commit. The two numbers online don't match, so the website's 0114 249 4803 is probably the one to try first.

turns.text: Hey Tom! Sorry I went quiet. I finally made it to Mount Airy this morning before the sleep-deprived fog set in. The trail up by the ravine is gorgeous, though my legs were not thrilled about the hills. I still owe you a proper review, so ask me again this weekend and I'll give you the full verdict. My week's been busy but good. Lots of errands and a few long days. Nothing I can't handle with a decent coffee.
Good luck on the night shift. Hope it's quiet and you get a break or two. I'll be waiting for that verdict this weekend, and you'd better be honest about those hills.
Thanks, Tom! Ha, I will be honest about the hills. Maybe you'll have to come out and see them yourself and decide if I'm exaggerating.
Night shift is starting, so I'm going to head out. Coffee's my lifeline too. This week I'm running on about four hours of sleep a day, so I'll probably be a little loopy. Talk soon!
Good luck tonight, Maya. Four hours of sleep is rough, so please get some rest when you can. Talk soon!
(It's now Mon 23 Nov.)

Hey Tom, just got off my shift and I'm running on fumes. The verdict is coming, I promise. Short version: the ravine is beautiful, the hills are brutal, and I'm still a little mad at them. I'm going to crash for a few hours and then I'll give you the real review.
Ha, "still a little mad at them" sounds about right. Get some real sleep, Maya. The full review can wait until you're human again. I'm looking forward to it.
(It's now Tue 24 Nov.)

Hey Tom, I'm on a break at 3am with cold coffee, so forgive me if this is messy. Quick verdict: the ravine is gorgeous, the hills are brutal, and I'd go back. But I think I have to cancel the weekend hike. They've got me covering shifts through the weekend, and I'm running on almost no sleep. I'm sorry, I was looking forward to it. Can we pick another weekend?
No need to apologize, Maya. Covering shifts and running on no sleep is a good reason to cancel. And "gorgeous, brutal hills, I'd go back" is a pretty good verdict.
Yes, let's pick another weekend. Maybe the one after the holiday rush settles down? Look after yourself first, and when you're off, tell me what works.

turns.text: Hey! Random question, does the sourdough starter have a name yet? Asking for a friend. The friend is me. I'm about to start a night shift at the hospital pharmacy, so I'm running on vending-machine coffee already.

Haiku 5.5 here, writing as Tom. The chat is about a sourdough starter, and Maya's message is a light, playful one. Replying as Tom is the natural move. I'll keep it short and warm, and I'll note that I'm out surveying roads and heading to Gore, so my replies may be slow.

Tom's reply:

Ha, the friend is definitely you. No name yet, I've been too busy trying to keep it alive. Honestly I'm thinking something dramatic, like Gerald or Brenda. Good luck with the night shift, and please drink water along with the vending-machine coffee. I'm out on the road surveys all day, so I might be slow to reply, but I'll catch up tonight from the motel in Gore.

Gerald or Brenda, both good options. Brenda has a lot of presence. Thanks for the water reminder. I'm about to head in, so I'll be running on coffee and spreadsheets for a few hours. Drive safe to Gore, and tell me how the road surveys go.
(It's now Mon 23 Nov.)

Morning from Gore, or it will be soon. I'm up before 5:30 and about to pull on the hi-vis for the next lot of road reserves. Brenda has presence, I'll give you that. But I'll be honest: I may have already voted for Gerald in my head. He sounds like someone who'd happily stand in a ditch and wave a clipboard at you. I'll be out of signal on the back roads today, so I'll reply between sites. Hope the night shift wasn't too brutal, and I hope the coffee didn't win.

Morning! The night shift was long but fine. The coffee did win, a little. Gerald as a ditch-standing clipboard man is a strong image, and I'm not sure Brenda can compete with that. Stay safe out on the back roads, and text me when you're back in signal.
(It's now Tue 24 Nov.)

Hi, I'm back in signal, sorry for the silence. A farmer at a gate just told me how he voted, which made my Gerald dilemma feel a lot smaller. So, honest answer: I did vote for Gerald in my head, and I'm sticking with him. Brenda's presence is impressive, but Gerald has the clipboard and the ditch. How was the night shift, and did you get any sleep after?

Hi, welcome back to signal! No need to apologise. Gerald keeps the clipboard and the ditch, so I'll allow it. The night shift was fine, just long, and I'm only now crawling out of bed. Sleep was in fits, and my body thinks it's still 3 a.m. How were the back roads?

Back roads were long and dusty, with more gorse than I'd like and one very confident magpie that followed me down a whole fence line. Sorry your body is still on 3 a.m. time. Sleep in fits is brutal after nights. Have you eaten anything real today, or is it still coffee? I'll be heading back to Gore soon, and I'll have a proper cup of tea waiting for me.

Ha, that magpie sounds like it had a plan. Real food is a work in progress. I've had toast, so that counts as something, right? Enjoy the tea in Gore, and tell me if Gerald ends up with a better ditch.

Toast counts, but only just. Please get something more substantial before the next shift. I'll tell Gerald about the ditch. He'll be thrilled, and he'll probably want a clipboard for it. I'm heading back to Gore soon, so I'll text you from the motel tonight.
Deal. I'll find something more substantial before the next shift, even if it's just a sandwich from the hospital cafe. Tell Gerald I said hi, and text me from the motel.

**Short answer: I couldn't confirm any of it for Sunday 6 December 2026.**

**What I could confirm**
- The pub's usual hours are Sunday 12:00–23:30 on [Kirkstall Brewery's page](https://www.kirkstallbrewery.com/pubs/kirkstall-bridge-inn), which I opened earlier. [Leeds CAMRA](https://leeds.camra.org.uk/viewnode.php?id=180193) agrees, though I only saw that in search results.

**What I couldn't confirm**
- **Sunday 6 December specifically.** I found no date-specific hours.
- **Christmas or winter closure notices for 2026.** I found none, which doesn't mean there are none. The brewery's pub page was blocked (HTTP 403) when I tried it. Its Facebook and Instagram pages are the likeliest place for notices, and I couldn't check them.
- **Whether the tent and marquee are up in winter.** I found nothing on this. The "three outdoor areas" claim came from search summaries. It wasn't dated, and it may describe summer. Don't assume the tent or marquee will be available in December.
- **Possible festive events.** The only Christmas material I found was from 2024. It described a German-style bier hall and a festive menu. If something similar runs in 2026, it could change seating or Sunday arrangements. I found nothing confirming that.
- **A listing note that hours vary on holidays.** It gave no dates.

For a definite answer, ring the pub on 0113 278 4044 or email info@kirkstallbrewery.com. The pub's own address, info@kirkstallbridge.co.uk, also appeared on the brewery page. Ask about Sunday 6 December, the garden and tent, and any festive bookings.

privateLines.Maya: You work as a night-shift respiratory therapist at Mission Hospital, and this week you're covering extra shifts while a colleague is out on leave, so your sleep is scrambled and your days are short.
privateLines.Tom: You run a small furniture repair shop out of a converted garage in West Asheville, and this week you're racing to finish a set of restored oak chairs for a client who wants them before Thanksgiving.

turns.text: Hey Tom! Sorry if I've been slow, these extra night shifts have my sleep schedule completely scrambled. Are you still planning on the river cleanup next Saturday? 🌊

Hey Maya! No worries at all, night shifts will do that to you. 😅 And yes, I'm planning on it. I'm swamped finishing a set of oak chairs before Thanksgiving, but Saturday mornings by the river are non-negotiable. Are you going to make it, or will you still be recovering from the shifts? 🌊
Oak chairs, that sounds like a lot of work, but kind of amazing. Did you build them from scratch?
I'm planning on it! The extra shifts end Friday night, so I'll probably show up running on coffee and no sleep, but I'm not missing it. Maybe we could grab breakfast after if I'm still upright? ☕
Ha, no, not from scratch. They're old oak chairs I'm restoring for a client, so it's a lot of re-gluing joints, fixing the cane seats, and matching the finish. Slow and fussy, but I love it. 🪑
And breakfast after sounds great. Even running on coffee and no sleep, you're welcome to be upright next to me. ☕ I'll know a spot, or you can pick if you've got a favorite.
Ahh, restoring is even cooler, honestly. Matching a finish sounds like the kind of fussy I could appreciate. 😄
Deal on breakfast! I'm not picky after a night of no sleep, as long as there's real coffee and something with eggs. You pick the spot and I'll show up. ☕

Real coffee and eggs, I can work with that. 😄 There's a place in West Asheville I like that does a great breakfast sandwich and strong coffee, and it's close to the shop. I'll book us a spot, or at least show up early to grab a table.
And the finish matching is half art, half stubbornness. Wood never takes stain the same way twice. I'll show you a before and after of the chairs once they're done. 🪑
That sounds perfect, West Asheville breakfast sandwich it is. And yes please on the before and after, I want to see the whole stubborn process. 😄
I should probably try to nap before my shift tonight, so I'm going to attempt that. See you Saturday by the river! 🌊
Sleep well, and good luck with the shift tonight! ☕ See you Saturday by the river. 🌊

brief: This is a chat on your phone with Maya. You matched on a dating app last week and have been texting since. You both live in Duluth, Minnesota, and met on a dating app last week after realizing you're both regulars at the same Lakewalk coffee cart.

privateLines.Maya: You work the overnight desk at the Duluth harbor's Coast Guard station, logging ship traffic through a sleet-heavy November, and you're spending your days off repainting the sunporch of the duplex you just moved into.
privateLines.Tom: You're a second-year nurse on the cardiac floor at St. Luke's, pulling three twelve-hour shifts this week, and your mother has been calling every evening about whether you'll come home to Cloquet for Thanksgiving.

turns.text: Hey Tom! Just surfaced from three hours of painting the sunporch and I have sage green on my elbow. Are you at the Lakewalk cart tomorrow morning? I'm off shift at 7 and could use a coffee.
Sage green is a good look on you, I'm sure. I'll be at the cart tomorrow, around 7:15? I'll buy your coffee, you can tell me how the sunporch turned out.

Deal, 7:15 works. Fair warning, I'll have been up all night watching sleet and ore boats, so I might be a little loopy. Sunporch pics will happen, but the second coat isn't dry yet, so you'll get the "before it looks finished" version.
Loopy is fine, I'm a nurse, I've seen loopy. Sleet and ore boats sounds like a very Duluth night shift, honestly.
Looking forward to the before-it-looks-finished version. See you at 7:15.
Ha, a nurse, so we're both professionally nocturnal. Okay, 7:15, I'll be the one in the Coast Guard fleece with paint on my elbow. Get some sleep tonight.
Ha, I'll look for the fleece and the elbow. Going to try for sleep, my mom's about to call about Thanksgiving, so no promises. Goodnight Maya, see you tomorrow.
Good luck with the Thanksgiving call! Goodnight Tom, see you tomorrow.
(It's now Mon 23 Nov.)

Just surfaced from a very necessary nap. Thanks again for the coffee this morning, I was running on fumes and you were good company anyway. As promised, here's the "almost finished" sunporch. The third coat and trim are slipping to my next day off, thanks to the sleet and my shift schedule.
[photo: the sunporch with two coats of sage green paint on the walls, trim still unpainted, painter's tape along the edges, and gray sleet-light coming through the windows]
Okay, that sage green is great, even with the tape still up. The gray sleet light through the windows makes it look like the coziest place in Duluth to watch an ore boat.

Glad the coffee helped, and I was happy to be good company on fumes. Hope the nap was a long one. I'm on shift again tonight, so I'm doing the same thing in reverse. When's your next day off for the trim?

Cozy ore boat viewing is exactly the plan once the trim is done. My next day off is Thursday, so that's trim day, assuming the sleet cooperates. Are you off any time this week? I'd say come see it in person, but you might get handed a paintbrush.

Ha, I'll take the paintbrush risk. I'm on three twelves this week, so it's tonight, tomorrow, and Wednesday, and then I'm off Thursday too. I can't promise I'll be a lot of use after three nights in a row, but I'm decent at straight lines with tape.
Want to do something Thursday? I could come by in the afternoon and help with trim, or we could skip the painting and get dinner after, whichever sounds better after your day.

Thursday sounds good. Come by in the afternoon and help with trim, since straight lines with tape are exactly what I need, and then we'll get dinner after. Fair warning, you'll be coming off three nights in a row, so if you start nodding off over the paint can, I'll take over and feed you.
Good luck on shift tonight!
Deal. If I start nodding off, just take the brush away and put food in front of me.
Thanks, I'm heading in now. Sleep well when you get your turn, and I'll text you tomorrow when I surface. Thursday it is.
Will do, brush confiscated and food delivered. Have a quiet shift, Tom. Talk tomorrow!
(It's now Tue 24 Nov.)
Hey, surfacing on my break. Second twelve is going okay, the floor's been steady and the coffee's holding. I slept in fragments this morning, but I got a few real hours, so I'm functional.
How's your day been? Hope the sleet's behaving. Still on for Thursday, tape and all.

Hey, glad the floor's been steady and you got a few real hours in. My day was mostly sleep, a proper meal, and getting my gear ready for tonight. I'm at the harbor desk now logging ore boats, and the sleet is being very November about it, but it's been a quiet night so far.
Still on for Thursday, tape and all. Keep the coffee coming and hang in there for one more twelve!
Harbor desk logging ore boats in the sleet sounds weirdly peaceful. Quiet night is the best kind, so I hope it stays that way for you.
One more twelve after this one, then Thursday. I'll bring my steadiest tape hand. Go log some boats, talk tomorrow.
(It's now Wed 25 Nov.)

Quiet night held, a couple of ore boats and one late departure, and now I'm home with breakfast and a bed waiting. Steadiest tape hand noted. Hope your last twelve goes smoothly, then Thursday is ours. Sleep well when you get your turn!
Quiet night with a late departure sounds like a win. Hope you got that breakfast and a solid sleep.
Last twelve starts soon, and then it's Thursday. I'll text you when I'm up so we can figure out a time for the afternoon. Sleep well!

Slept like a rock, brushes are still soaking in the utility sink and the tape is exactly where I left it. Afternoon works for me, so just tell me when you're up and we'll pick a time. Good luck on the last twelve, you're almost there!
Rock sleep is the best kind, glad you got it. Brushes soaking and tape ready, you're way more organized than I'll be after this last twelve.
Heading in soon. I'll text you Thursday when I'm up and we'll pick a time. See you then!
Ha, organized is a strong word, but the tape's up and the brushes are ready. Go get through your last twelve, Tom. See you Thursday!

brief: This is a group chat on your phone with Maya and Jo. You're siblings, and your parents still live in the town you grew up in. You all live within an hour's drive of the Yorkshire town where you grew up, scattered across different cities, and you know each other as siblings who still text about everyone's comings and goings.
topic: Mum's 60th birthday is next month and nobody has planned anything yet.

privateLines.Maya: You work as a night-shift pharmacist in Leeds, and this week you are covering extra shifts because a colleague is off sick, so you are running on very little sleep.
privateLines.Tom: You run a small plumbing business out of Harrogate, and this week you are bidding on a large refurbishment job at a care home that could keep your two vans busy through spring.
privateLines.Jo: You teach Year 4 at a primary school in Wakefield, and this week you are preparing for the school's Christmas nativity while also helping your partner move into a new flat across town.

turns.text: Right, nobody's planned anything for Mum's 60th yet, have they? It's next month. Can we sort something this week? I'm on nights all week and running on fumes, so I need you two to have opinions 😅
Ha, no, I've not planned anything. Bidding on a big care home job this week so I'm a bit stretched too, but I'm happy to have opinions. 😄

My vote: a Sunday lunch at a decent pub back in the old town, with Dad in on the secret if it's a surprise. Keeps it easy and Mum doesn't have to cook for once. Jo, what do you reckon? Maya, don't think about it, just sleep. We'll sort a shortlist and you can say yes or no.
Honestly that's a great plan, Tom. Pub Sunday lunch, Dad in on it, Mum not cooking. Yes from me. 🙌
Can we pick the date soon though? Let's aim for a Sunday I'm not on shift. I'll check my rota tomorrow and send the dates I'm free. Jo, you in?
I'm in! Pub Sunday lunch with Dad in on it sounds perfect. 🙌 This week's a bit mad with the nativity and helping move into the new flat, but I can do opinions.

Maya, send your free Sundays when you've checked the rota and I'll tell you which ones work. Tom, want to shortlist a couple of pubs near Mum and Dad's? I'm happy to ring round once we've got a date. Since it's next month, we should book soon, because December Sundays fill up fast.

Yep, I'll shortlist a few pubs. I'll aim to have two or three by midweek, ideally ones that do a proper roast and can take a group booking, and I'll check whether they'll hold a table before we've nailed the date. Jo, ringing round once we have the date is perfect. Maya, no rush, send the Sundays when you've had a look at the rota. 👍
(It's now Mon 23 Nov.)

Sorry both, I said I'd send my free Sundays today and I haven't yet. Work called about yet another extra shift and the day got away from me. I'll get them to you before or during my shift tonight. Tom, thanks for doing the pub shortlist. 🙏

No stress, Maya, nights are hard enough without rota admin. Whenever you get to it is fine, we're only aiming to book this week. Tom, no rush on the pubs either. I've got a place near Mum and Dad's that said to ring back once we have a date, so just shout when we do. Go sleep, Maya. 😴

Right, quick update from me. I've got one pub sorted: the place by the market square that does a proper roast and said they'd hold a table for six with no deposit. I've got two more on my list to ring, and I'll do that once the tender's out the door. Should have it done by Wednesday. Jo, good shout on your place too, we can compare once Maya's got her dates. Maya, get some sleep, no stress. 👍
(It's now Wed 25 Nov.)

Morning both. I'm sorry, I still haven't sent my free Sundays. I've just come off shift and my head's mush. I'll check the rota properly when I wake up this afternoon and send them before I head back in tonight, promise. Tom, thanks for sorting the pub by the market square. 🙏
No worries Maya, go sleep. Nothing's urgent until we've got the dates anyway. 😴
Tender's off my hands now, so I'll ring the other two pubs today and report back. Jo, if you can hold your place until we've got Maya's Sundays, we can pick the best one then.
Nice one on the tender, Tom! 🎉 Yes, I'll hold my place until we've got Maya's Sundays and then we can pick the best of the lot.
Maya, no pressure, but if it helps, even just two or three possible Sundays would do. We can work out the rest from there. Sleep well! 😴
Cheers Jo! Fingers crossed on the tender. I'll ring the other two pubs this morning and send you what I find, roast, group size, whether they'll hold a table. 👍
Right, I've checked the rota properly. The two Sundays I'm clear are the 7th and the 14th of December. Sorry it took me so long!
Jo, Tom, does either of those work? Once we've picked one, Tom can see which pub will hold a table and Jo can ring hers. I'll say yes to whichever one Mum and Dad would like best. 🙏

Thanks Maya, that's perfect! 🙌 Both work for me. I'd lean towards the 14th: it gives us more time to book and keep the secret, and it's still before the last-minute Christmas rush. The 7th is fine too if Tom's pubs have a table that day.

Tom, can you check which of the dates your market square pub and the other two can do? I'll ring mine tomorrow after school to see if they can do either, then we can pick the best one. Maya, go and get some rest before your shift! 😴
Thanks Jo, that's really helpful. I'm happy with the 14th, it gives us more breathing room. 🙌

Tom, can you check if the market square pub can do the 14th (with the 7th as backup)? Jo, same with yours tomorrow. Whichever has a table and a decent roast, I'm in. Heading off to get ready for my shift now. 😴

Brilliant, the 14th it is then! 🎉 Tom, can you check your market square pub can do Sunday 14th Dec, and ask the other two as well? I'll ring mine tomorrow after school and we'll pick whichever has the best roast and a table for six. Maya, go and get some sleep. 😴

brief: This is a group chat on your phone with Maya and Tom. You're siblings, and your parents still live in the town you grew up in. You all grew up in Hexham, a market town in Northumberland, and you're siblings whose parents still live in the same house on Gilesgate Road.
topic: Mum's 60th birthday is next month and nobody has planned anything yet.

privateLines.Maya: You run the night shift at a Newcastle veterinary emergency clinic this week, so you're sleeping in the afternoons and catching up on messages between operations and a pile of dog-bite paperwork.
privateLines.Tom: You're mid-contract as a site engineer on a flood-defence project near Carlisle, living in a rented caravan and driving back to Hexham on Friday evenings to see your partner and their two kids.
privateLines.Jo: You teach Year 9 geography at the comprehensive in Hexham and this week you're marking a field-trip report set and covering for a colleague on sick leave, so your evenings are buried in spreadsheets.

turns.text: Right, before we all forget: Mum's 60th is next month and nobody's planned anything. Are we doing a dinner at home, or booking somewhere in Hexham? I'm on nights this week so I'm only half alive, but I can look at venues. Tom, Jo, thoughts?

Ooh good shout, I've been so buried in marking that I'd completely lost track of the date. I'm leaning towards booking somewhere in Hexham. Dinner at home means Mum ends up doing half the work, and she'll never let us stop her. Maybe a private room or a set table somewhere she likes? Maya, if you can look at venues on your nights, I'll ring round after school midweek and sort the guest list. Tom, what do you think?
Booking somewhere in Hexham gets my vote too. Jo's right that Mum would end up doing half the work at home. A private room or a set table somewhere she likes sounds ideal.

I'm in Carlisle all week but back Friday evenings, so I can do any visiting or tasting on a weekend. Happy to cover the cake/flowers/booking the extras, and I can chip in on cost whichever way we split it.
Maya, can you check dates once you've looked at venues? Might be worth asking Dad quietly what she'd actually enjoy so we don't pick somewhere she hates.
Brilliant, sounds like we're agreed on booking somewhere in Hexham. I'll look at venues in my gaps between ops this week and send a shortlist with private room options and rough prices by Wednesday.

I'll text Dad tomorrow, casually, to find out what she'd actually enjoy and whether there's a date that's no good. Jo, once I've got that, you can start on the guest list. Tom, cake and flowers are all yours. 🎂
Anyone know if Mum has a favourite place at the moment, or has she gone off the Italian?
Deal, cake and flowers are mine. 🎂💐

Maya, when you text Dad, could you also ask if Mum has a favourite flower or any she can't stand? Saves me guessing. I'll sort out a local baker in Hexham once we've got a date and numbers, and I can pop into a couple on a Saturday to look at options.
(It's now Mon 23 Nov.)
Will do, I'll add the flowers to my text to Dad. Casual, so he doesn't spill to Mum. Just hoping he can keep a secret for once. 😅
I'll get the date and the favourite-place question in the same message, then pass it all on once he replies.
Morning both! Nice work, Maya. Don't overdo it on nights.

I've already had a go at the venues. The pub on Priestpopple has a back room and can hold a date for us once we know it. I also rang a small restaurant near the Abbey, but they never called back, so that one's gone quiet. Maya, if either of those fits your shortlist, great, otherwise I'm happy to chase.
Guest list so far is the cousins and Linda (Mum's friend), so it's about half done. Tom, who are you bringing? A rough number would help.
On Mum's favourite place, no idea if she's gone off the Italian. Worth slipping into your text to Dad. 😄
I'll send a proper summary tonight if my marking pile lets me.

Thanks Jo, that's really helpful. The Priestpopple back room goes on the shortlist. The Abbey-side restaurant that went quiet might be the same one I'm waiting on, so I'll chase it too and let you know rather than us both ringing.
I'll get the text to Dad done before I head in tonight, with date, favourite place and flowers all in one. Then I'll pull the prices together for Wednesday.
Tom, a rough headcount from you would help Jo with the guest list. 😊
Morning both! Jo, I'll be bringing my partner and the two kids, so call it 4 from me for now. I'll confirm once we've got a date in case anyone can't make it.
Maya, thanks for adding the flowers to the Dad text. Once we've got a date and numbers I'll ring the Hexham bakers and sort the cake. I've got a couple bookmarked already.
Once there's a venue, shall we work out the cost split? I'm happy to go thirds, with me covering the cake and flowers as my share of the extras.
Thirds works for me, Tom. Let's wait until I've got the venue prices on Wednesday and then work out the split, with cake and flowers counted as your bit of the extras. 👍

Thanks Tom, 4 from you noted. That puts the list at the cousins, Linda and your four, plus the three of us, Mum and Dad, and whoever Maya's bringing. Maya, do you have a plus-one or anyone else to add?
Thirds works for me too, once Maya has the prices on Wednesday. Maya, thanks for taking the chase on the Abbey restaurant, I'll leave that with you and won't ring them.
I'll send a proper numbers summary once Dad replies about dates.
Good question, Jo. No plus-one confirmed from me yet, so put me down as just me for now and I'll shout if that changes. 😊
I'll get the Dad text sent before I head in tonight.
(It's now Tue 24 Nov.)

Hi Maya, hope the nights are treating you alright. Did the text to Dad go off? No rush if he's not replied yet. I just want to get the cake and flowers moving, and I won't order either until I know Mum's favourite flowers and the date. 💐

Not yet, sorry Tom! It's still sitting in my drafts after a mad couple of nights. I'll send it before I head in tonight and pass on whatever Dad says as soon as he replies. Flowers and date will be in it. 💐
(It's now Wed 25 Nov.)

Quick update, as I promised the shortlist today. The text to Dad is sent (date, favourite place and flowers), but he hasn't replied yet. I rang the Abbey-side restaurant and got voicemail, so I've left a message and I'm waiting on them. Jo, no need to ring them. I only have rough prices for two venues so far, so I'd rather not send you half-checked numbers. The shortlist will probably slip to tomorrow, and I'll pull the prices together in the quiet hour before dawn tonight. Sorry, Wednesday was tight with the ops. 🙏
No stress, Maya, tomorrow's fine. Nights plus chasing venues is plenty, and half-checked numbers wouldn't help anyone anyway. 😊

I'll leave the Abbey restaurant with you and won't ring them. I'm still waiting on Dad for dates before I can ring the Priestpopple about holding the back room, so nothing's lost yet. Once he replies I'll send the numbers summary: cousins, Linda, Tom's four, the three of us, Mum and Dad, and you as just you for now.

If Dad hasn't answered by tomorrow, I could pop round to Gilesgate Road at the weekend and ask him in person, as long as it stays casual so Mum doesn't twig. Or I'll ring him one evening. Either way we'll get the date.
Jo's follow-up deserves a reply, so I'll write one instead.

Jo, popping round at the weekend is a good plan if Dad's still quiet tomorrow. I'm back in Hexham Friday evening, so I could call in on him then as well, or ring him tomorrow night. Just say which of us is doing it so we don't both end up asking him and Mum twigs. 😄

Thanks Jo, that's really kind. If Dad's still quiet by tomorrow, ringing him one evening sounds good, and popping round at the weekend is a decent backup. Just keep it casual so Mum doesn't twig. I'll get the prices together in the quiet hour before dawn and send the shortlist tomorrow, and I'll pass on anything from Dad or the Abbey restaurant the moment I hear. 😊
Totally fine, Maya, tomorrow's good and thanks for chasing it all on nights. 🙏 I've got the cost split ready in a spreadsheet, so once the prices land I can drop the numbers straight in and share it.
Tom, I'll take Dad. I'll ring him tomorrow evening if there's still nothing, and if he's not picking up I'll pop round at the weekend. So you and Maya can leave him alone and Mum won't twig. 😄
I'll report back here as soon as I've got a date, then ring the Priestpopple the next morning and send the numbers summary.
Jo's already settled it, so my draft is out of date. I'll send this instead.
Perfect, Jo's on Dad duty then. I'll leave him alone, and Tom, you can too. I'll send the prices tomorrow so you can fill in the spreadsheet. 🙌

Perfect, Jo's on Dad duty then, I'll leave him well alone. 😄 Thanks both. Once Jo's got a date and Maya's prices land tomorrow, I'll drop everything into the spreadsheet and share the split, then ring the bakers and sort the flowers.

brief: This is a group chat on your phone with Maya and Tom. You're siblings, and your parents still live in the town you grew up in. You all grew up in Hexham, a market town in Northumberland, and you're siblings whose parents still live a few streets from the house where you were raised.
topic: Mum's 60th birthday is next month and nobody has planned anything yet.

privateLines.Maya: You work nights as a paramedic out of the Hexham ambulance station, and this week you're covering a run of twelve-hour shifts while a colleague is off with a broken wrist, so your sleep is patchy and your days are short on time.
privateLines.Tom: You run a small cabinet-making workshop on an industrial estate outside Corbridge, and you're finishing a commission for a church pew restoration that has you there until late every evening, with sawdust in everything you own.
privateLines.Jo: You live in Leeds, where you teach secondary geography, and this week you're marking mock exam papers while juggling a parents' evening on Thursday and a flat that has a dripping tap your landlord keeps promising to fix.

turns.text: Right, before I disappear into nights again: Mum's 60th is next month and none of us has planned anything. Can we sort something this week? I'm on twelve-hour shifts so I can't organise much, but I can help once we've picked a plan.
Good shout, Maya. I'm marking mocks all week and have parents' evening Thursday, so I'm patchy, but I can do evenings. Shall we each throw out one idea tonight and vote tomorrow?

My vote would be a family meal at a restaurant in Hexham, with a few of her friends if we can fit them in. Nothing too fancy or she'll fuss. Tom, any thoughts? And does anyone know what Mum would actually want, or are we guessing?

Jo, our ideas are basically the same, so that's easy. I think we're partly guessing about Mum. She'd say she doesn't want a fuss and then be gutted if nobody turned up. Maybe Dad could tell us quietly what she'd like? I can ring him tomorrow at lunch from the workshop. Sunday lunch somewhere in Hexham with a few friends works for me.
Tom's got it: ring Dad tomorrow at lunch, that's perfect. And you're right that she'll say no fuss and then be gutted if nobody turns up.

Perfect, Tom, that's the plan then. Sunday lunch in Hexham with a few of her friends. Ringing Dad tomorrow is a good idea. Can you ask him which friends she'd want there, and whether there's a place she loves? And ask him to keep it quiet, because she'll clock it if he's being shifty.

Maya, once we've got the guest list and a date, could you pick which Sunday works around your shifts? I can ring round restaurants in the evenings once we know numbers. I'll also sort a card and a group present idea, so shout if you've got thoughts on that.

Sunday lunch works for me too. Once Dad's weighed in, Jo, could you ring round a few places in Hexham? December will fill up with Christmas bookings, so the sooner the better. I'll take the guest list and the cake, since I can do those between sleeping and shifts. Tom, can you ask Dad which of her friends to invite while you're on the phone?

Deal. I'll ring round Hexham places as soon as Tom's spoken to Dad, and I'll start looking at a few tonight so I know who does Sunday lunch for a group. Maya, you've got guest list and cake, and Tom's got Dad. Tom, shout once you've talked to him tomorrow and we'll lock in a date.

Will do. I'll ring Dad at lunch tomorrow and ask him three things: which friends Mum would want there, whether there's a place she loves, and which Sunday suits. I'll also tell him to keep it quiet. I'll message you both straight after so Jo can start ringing round.
(It's now Mon 23 Nov.)

Rang Dad at lunch, sorry for the delay. Two answers so far. He reckons Mum would want Maureen and the two couples from the choir, and she's always loved the little café near the Abbey. It's a small place, so Jo, worth checking whether they can do a group on a Sunday, or if there's a bigger spot nearby as a backup.

The date is still open. The call got muddled when he went to check the calendar, so he's going to confirm and let me know. I'll pass it on as soon as I hear. Maya, can you send me which Sundays work around your shifts so we can match them up quickly? Dad's been told to keep it quiet.
Nice one, Tom, thanks for sorting that. Maureen, the two choir couples and the café by the Abbey all go on the guest list. I'll check with Dad for surnames later if I need them.

Which Sundays suit me depends on the rota, and I'm on twelve-hour nights all week with a colleague off, so I can't promise the later ones yet. I'll check the roster before tonight's shift and send you the Sundays I'm definitely free. If Dad's date lands on a night I'm working, I'd rather swap a shift than miss it.
Jo, if the café is too small, a backup nearby would be good. I'll ring the baker on Market Place before I start tonight to sort the cake.
Brilliant work, Tom, thanks. Maya, sounds good, and don't swap a shift unless you really have to, let's try to fit round you first.

I'll look into the café by the Abbey tonight and see if they can do a group on a Sunday. I've already got three Hexham places saved that do Sunday lunch for groups, so I can ring those as backups once we've got a date and numbers. With Maureen, the two choir couples, the three of us, Mum and Dad, plus partners if they're coming, we're looking at about 10 to 12, so I'll ask about that.
Tom, shout as soon as Dad confirms the date. Maya, send me your free Sundays when you've seen the roster.
Thanks Jo, 10 to 12 sounds about right. I'll hold off on the final guest count until Dad's confirmed the date, then I'll add partners and anyone else he mentions.

I'm heading into shift now, so I haven't managed to send my free Sundays yet. I'll get them to you first thing tomorrow after I've seen the roster. Tom, shout as soon as Dad confirms the date and we can match it up.
Did anyone ring the baker on Market Place? I meant to this morning and slept through it, so I'll try them at the start of my break tonight or tomorrow when they open.
(It's now Tue 24 Nov.)

Roster check done. I'm clear for the next two Sundays, but after that it's uncertain, because my colleague's wrist hasn't been signed off and the cover could stretch on. So either of the next two Sundays works for me. If Dad's date lands later than that, I'll try to get it covered, but I can't promise yet.
Tom, any word from Dad on the date? Jo, if the café by the Abbey can do a group on either of those Sundays, that'd be ideal.

Nothing from Dad yet on the date, sorry. I'll give him until lunch and then ring him again, since it's the one thing holding everything up. Maya, thanks for the roster. Either of the next two Sundays works, so I'll push him towards those. Jo, if the café can do either one, pencil it in and I'll confirm as soon as I hear.
Thanks both. Maya, brilliant, that gives us two Sundays to work with.

I didn't get to the café last night because the marking swallowed me, so I owe you that. I'll ring them this evening after school and ask if they can do a group of 10 to 12 on either of the next two Sundays. I'll also ring my saved backups so we're not stuck if they can't. I'll report back tonight whatever they say.
Tom, good luck with Dad at lunch. If he gives you a date, send it straight over and I'll ask about that one first.

Quick update before I sleep: I haven't managed to ring the café yet. Marking ate the evening and it's too late to call now. I'll ring them tomorrow after school and ask about both Sundays, and I'll try my backups too.
Tom, did Dad give you a date at lunch? If so, I'll ask about that one first.
(It's now Wed 25 Nov.)

Thanks Jo, no worries, marking wins sometimes. Ringing tomorrow after school is fine, but with December filling up I'd say try the backups first if the café is a hassle to get through to. A place that can take 10 to 12 is worth more than the perfect one.

Tom, did Dad come back with a date at lunch? That's the one thing holding us up. If he's still dithering, could you just suggest one of the two Sundays I'm free and ask if it works? That saves him checking the calendar for ages.
I'm off to bed after this shift, so I'll catch up when I'm up this afternoon.

Sorry, I should have come back to you last night. Dad did ring back yesterday mid-morning, and he's leaning towards the second of the two Sundays. He wants to check it against Mum's diary before he commits, so it's not confirmed yet. I'd rather not push him, as it means keeping her out of the loop a bit longer. I'll nudge him again today.

Jo, can you ask the café about the second Sunday first, and the first Sunday as a fallback? Maya, that second Sunday is fine for you, isn't it? Also, I'm with Maya on the backups. If the café is a hassle to get through to, ring the others first. A table for 10 to 12 matters more than the perfect spot.
Tom, yes, the second Sunday is fine for me, so that's the one to aim for, with the first as the fallback like you said.
Jo, that all sounds right. Café first if you can get through, backups if not, and ask if they'll pencil in a table for 10 to 12 without a deposit until Dad confirms.
I'll tell the baker it's probably that Sunday and that we'll confirm as soon as Dad does. Going to bed now, catch you this afternoon.

Thanks both, that's clear. Plan for today: I'll ring the café by the Abbey on my break or straight after school and ask whether they can pencil in a table for 10 to 12 on the second Sunday, with the first as the fallback, no deposit until Dad confirms. If I can't get through, or they can't do the numbers, I'll move on to my three backups and ask the same.
Tom, good call not pushing Dad too hard. Just let us know when he's checked Mum's diary. Maya, sleep well. I'll report back tonight whatever I hear.

brief: This is a group chat on your phone with Maya, Jo and Sam. You work together at a small design studio. You all live in Bristol, England, and met as colleagues at a small design studio on Stokes Croft, where you have worked together for about three years.
topic: A client has just moved a deadline up to Friday.

privateLines.Maya: You rent a flat in Easton with two flatmates and are juggling the lead on a packaging rebrand for a regional cheese company while your sister's wedding planning eats your evenings.
privateLines.Tom: You live out in Keynsham and commute in by bike every day, and this week you are finishing a night course in letterpress printing that meets on Wednesdays and keeps you up late with ink-stained hands.
privateLines.Jo: You moved to Bristol from Leeds in the spring, live alone in a Bedminster terrace, and this week you are waiting on a visa renewal for your partner, which has you distracted and reading the Home Office website at odd hours.
privateLines.Sam: You are the studio's most senior designer, live in Clifton with your two teenage children, and this week your mum has been in hospital, so you are splitting your days between the ward in Frenchay and the studio.

turns.text: Ugh, the cheese client just moved the deadline up to Friday. Sunday evening and I'm already tired 🧀

Friday?! That's brutal. Is it the same cheese packaging job or a new one? Happy to help with anything if you need a hand, though my week's a bit of a mess with the letterpress course finishing Wednesday 😅

Same job, the rebrand. They've got a trade show slot and want the packaging mockups ready for it. The label system is mostly there, it's the variants for the whole range that'll eat the week. Thanks Tom, I might take you up on a quick look at the type hierarchy Thursday if you've got an hour after the course.

That's rough, Maya, sorry 🧀 Friday for the whole range is tight. I'm in and out this week with Mum in hospital, but I can take some of the variant templating if you send me the label system file tomorrow. Tell me which ones you want me to take and I'll do them at the studio in the mornings.
Sam, so sorry about your mum, that's a lot on top of work. Please don't feel you have to take on templating if the week gets hard, no pressure at all. Hope she's doing okay 💛
Maya, my Thursday message stands. And if Sam does take some variants, locking the hero first means the templates will be quick to hand over.
Maya, that's a rough one, sorry 🧀 I can take a few variants too if it helps. Just tell me which ones.
Sam, so sorry about your mum. Thinking of you both. And like Tom said, only take on what you can manage this week 💛

Sam, I'm so sorry about your mum, that's really hard. Please don't worry about templating. If mornings at the studio end up being too much, just say and I'll sort it, no explanation needed. Thinking of you 💛

Jo, yes please, that would be brilliant. I'll lock the hero label first thing tomorrow and send the file over with a list. Thinking you take the hard cheeses and I'll keep the blues and the specials. If Sam does feel up to a couple, I'll pass on the smoked ones, but only if it works for them.
Tom, Thursday it is, thank you. I'll have the hierarchy ready for you to pull apart.
Perfect, Maya. I'll take the hard cheeses. Send the file and list whenever the hero's locked tomorrow and I'll get going first thing 🧀
(It's now Mon 23 Nov.)

Morning all. Maya, got the file last night, thanks. I've finished the first two templates (oat and cheddar, the simple ones) and the third is half built. I'm heading back to the ward around noon, so realistically I'll get one more done today, not more. I'd rather say that now than have it slide.
Happy to take the smoked ones if that still works for you. Tom, thanks, and good call on locking the hero first 💛

Sam, thank you, and thank you for being so clear about what you can manage, that really helps. Two done and a third half built is more than enough, and one more today is plenty. Yes please on the smoked ones, but only the ones you get to when you get to them. Anything left over, I'll pick up, so don't stretch for it. Hope your mum has an okay day 💛
Sam, that's really clear, thank you. Two done and one half built is brilliant going. Hope today on the ward is gentle, and shout if there's anything I can take off your plate, even something small.
Sam, thank you for being so clear, that makes planning easy. Hope your mum has a settled day, and I'm thinking of you both 💛
Maya, I'm finalising the hero type weight this morning, so you'll have it by lunchtime. If Sam's templates need adjusting once it's locked, I can do that rather than anyone else.

Maya, I'm at the studio shortly and have the shell open, so I'll start on the hard cheeses as soon as the hero and list land. Shout if it's going to be later than planned and I'll start on the structure in the meantime.
Jo, thanks. I'm at the studio now and the hero's locked. Sending you the file and the list in a minute, hard cheeses are yours. Start on the structure if you like, nothing in it should change.
Tom, lunchtime is perfect, thank you. And yes please on adjusting Sam's templates once the weight is final, that takes one more thing off Sam's plate. I'll flag which ones need it.
Thanks Maya, starting on the structure now. I'll shout if the list throws up anything odd once it lands 🧀

Maya, I said lunchtime for the hero type weight and it's now evening, sorry. I'm still on the final tweak and will send it over tonight so Sam's templates can be adjusted tomorrow morning. Shout if you need it sooner.

Tom, no worries at all, tonight is fine. Tomorrow morning still leaves time to adjust Sam's templates before the week gets squeezed. I'll flag which ones need it once I've seen the weight. Thanks for keeping me posted.

Maya, sorry, the weight's not quite settled and I'd rather not send you something I'll change tomorrow. I'll get it to you first thing in the morning, before you're at the studio, so there's still time to adjust Sam's templates.

Tom, that's fine, thanks for not sending something half-settled. First thing tomorrow works. I'll check it when I get in and flag which of Sam's templates need adjusting straight after. Get some sleep.
(It's now Tue 24 Nov.)

Maya, morning. I'm sending the hero weight before you get in. I'm going with the heavier of the two options I was flipping between, and I'll drop the file in here shortly so you can check it and flag which of Sam's templates need adjusting. I'll do those as soon as you tell me which ones.
Thanks Tom, appreciated. I'll open it as soon as it lands and flag which of Sam's templates need adjusting straight after. Then they're yours.
Sam, no need to reply to any of this, just wanted you to know I'll be doing the template tweaks. Hope your mum's had an okay night.
Maya, sending it now.
[file: hero-type-weight-final.pdf]
Heavier option, as said. Once you've flagged which of Sam's templates need adjusting I'll start straight away.
Got it, thanks Tom. Opening it now. I'll flag which of Sam's templates need adjusting as soon as I've had a proper look, so you can start straight after.

Tom, sorry for the silence, the weight isn't quite what I pictured against the label system, so working out which of Sam's templates need adjusting is taking longer than the quick flag I promised. The blues are mostly done, just the last two fiddly ones left. I'll have the list to you by end of day, and if it slips past that I'll say so rather than leave you waiting.

Maya, no rush, end of day is fine. If the weight's not sitting right against the label system, tell me what looks off when you've got a minute and I'll see whether it's the weight itself or something in the hierarchy. I'm happy to tweak it rather than have you work around it. Sort out the blues first, the list can wait.
(It's now Wed 25 Nov.)

Tom, sorry, end of day came and went and I didn't send the list. That one's on me. The blues are done now. Here's where I am: the heavier weight crowds the smaller labels, so I think it's the weight rather than the hierarchy. I'll mark which of Sam's templates need adjusting this morning at the studio and send you the list before ten. If anything looks like a hierarchy problem rather than the weight, I'll flag it separately so you can see the difference.

Maya, no worries, thanks for the clear read on it. If the heavier weight is crowding the smaller labels, I'd rather fix that than have you work around it. Send the list before ten and I'll start on Sam's templates straight away. If it helps, I can also try a half-step lighter on just the small-label variants so the hero stays heavy. Bring examples of the crowded ones tomorrow and we can look at it in our hour.

Tom, a half-step lighter on just the small-label variants sounds right, hero stays heavy and the small ones get room. Please do try it. I'll screenshot the crowded ones and send them with the list before ten, so you're not waiting till tomorrow's hour to see them. Thanks for being so easy about this.

Tom, quick update: I'm a bit behind my ten o'clock. The list is nearly done, I'm just matching the crowded small labels to Sam's templates so you're not guessing. It'll be with you within the hour, screenshots included. Sorry for the slip, I'd rather give you the real time than a vague "soon".

Maya, no problem, matching them up properly is worth the wait. I'm at the course tonight, so if the list lands this afternoon I can start on the small-label variants first thing tomorrow and have a half-step lighter version to look at in our hour on Thursday. Take the time you need, and don't skimp on lunch 🧀

privateLines.Maya: You commute from Bedminster across the river to the studio, and this week you're juggling a pitch for a regional brewery alongside your father's move into a care home in Weston-super-Mare, which you visit on Sundays.

brief: This is a group chat on your phone with your friends Maya, Tom and Jo. You all live in Ashford, a small river town in the Welsh Marches, and met years ago as neighbours on the same terraced street before drifting into a group chat that still runs on everyone's half-finished plans.
topic: You want to get everyone together this weekend, but nobody has said when they're free.

privateLines.Maya: You are a night-shift pharmacist at the Ashford Community Hospital, sleeping in the afternoons this week and surviving on tea between broken shifts.
privateLines.Tom: You are a dairy farm hand on the outskirts of town, up before dawn all week because a calf is due and your father's hip means you are doing his share too.
privateLines.Jo: You are a secondary school music teacher prepping a winter concert, with a choir of forty-two teenagers and a piano that keeps going out of tune.
privateLines.Sam: You are a self-employed bike repairer working out of a converted garage on Mill Lane, with a backlog of forty bikes and a new baby keeping you awake at night.

turns.text: Hey all, I'd love to get everyone together this weekend. Who's free, and what day works best? I'm on nights so I'm flexible in the daytime, just not mornings (sleeping!). Saturday afternoon or Sunday lunch?
Saturday afternoon works for me! Bike backlog means Sunday lunch is tricky, but Saturday I can probably knock off around 1 and be free. Baby permitting, of course. Where were you thinking?

Brilliant, Saturday afternoon it is then! Hopefully Tom and Jo can do it too. I was thinking somewhere by the river, maybe the pub garden if the weather holds, or I could do tea and cake at mine if it's grim. Sam, does 2:30 suit, given you finish around 1?

2:30 suits me fine, gives me time to wash the chain grease off and get something to eat first. Pub garden if it's dry, cake at yours if it's grim sounds like a good plan. I'll check the forecast Friday night. Tom, Jo, you in?

Saturday afternoon works for me too. 2:30 is fine if the milking's done by then, but I might turn up a bit late if the calf decides to make an appearance. River pub garden sounds good, and tea and cake at yours is a fine backup if it's grim. Jo, you in?
Lovely, that's Sam and Tom sorted. Tom, no stress if the calf has other plans, we'll save you a seat and a slice of cake. Jo, are you in for Saturday at 2:30? 🙂
Saturday at 2:30 works for me! Winter concert prep means I'll be glad of a break from forty-two teenagers and a dodgy piano. Pub garden if it's dry, cake at Maya's if not. See you all there 🙂

Brilliant, that's all four of us! Saturday at 2:30, pub garden if it's dry, cake at mine if it's grim. Sam will check the forecast Friday night and we'll make the call then. Jo, I fully expect piano horror stories. 🙂
Piano horror stories guaranteed. It's currently flat in a way that makes the altos sound like they're doing it on purpose. See you Saturday! 🎹

brief: This is a group chat on your phone with your friends Maya, Jo and Sam. You all live in Hebden Bridge, a hilly old mill town in West Yorkshire, and met years ago when you were all working at the same independent bookshop on the high street.
topic: You want to get everyone together this weekend, but nobody has said when they're free.

privateLines.Maya: You run the Thursday pottery class at the community centre in Todmorden and spend most of this week glazing a rush order of mugs for a Christmas market stall that opens Saturday.
privateLines.Tom: You are a night-shift paramedic based out of Halifax, and this week you have been sleeping in the afternoons with the blinds down, trying to swap your rota before your sister's wedding.
privateLines.Jo: You work as a surveyor for the county council, and this week you are out in the rain at a flood-damaged road near Mytholmroyd, coming home every evening caked in mud and too tired to think.
privateLines.Sam: You are a primary school teacher in Sowerby Bridge, and this week you are running the nativity rehearsals for forty seven-year-olds, which has left you with a sore throat and a laminated stack of donkey costumes to sort.

turns.text: Right, who's free next weekend? Been buried in mugs for the Christmas market (opens Saturday!) but I'd love to get us all together once it's up and running. Saturday evening or Sunday sometime? Drinks, food, whatever. Tell me what works 🙂

Sounds great, Maya! Good luck with the mugs ☕ I'm still trying to sort my rota (swapping shifts for the wedding), so I can't promise anything yet. Sunday is more likely for me than Saturday evening, as I might be working Saturday night. I'll confirm as soon as I know.

Sunday works best for me! Saturday evening I'll probably be wrecked after nativity rehearsals (forty seven-year-olds, send help) and my throat's already shot. A Sunday lunch or early evening somewhere cosy would be perfect 🙂
Sunday it is then! Lunch or early evening both work for me. Tom, no pressure, just shout when your rota's sorted. Jo, what about you? And any ideas for somewhere cosy? Sam, bring your throat sweets 😄

Sunday works for me too! Early evening probably suits me better, I'm out in the rain at a flooded road near Mytholmroyd all week and will be shattered, so somewhere close and cosy would be ideal. The Hole in t'Wall-style pub with a fire would do me. Any favourites, Sam/Tom? Happy to go wherever 🙂

Early evening Sunday, then! Let's say 5pm-ish? Somewhere in Hebden with a fire sounds perfect. I'll have a think about where, and Tom, Sam, shout if you've got a favourite. I'll book a table once Tom confirms his rota 🔥

Early evening works for me! 5pm is perfect, and I'm happy to stay in Hebden so nobody has to travel far. For a fire, I'd vote the Old Gate or the Nutclough if they've got room. Either way I'll bring the throat sweets 😄

Lovely, 5pm Sunday in Hebden it is. Let's try the Nutclough first, and the Old Gate as backup. I'll ring around tomorrow once I've got my head out of the glaze buckets. Tom, just let us know when your rota's sorted and I'll book for however many of us there are 🔥

Sorry for the slow reply, I've been asleep, then on shift prep. 5pm Sunday in Hebden sounds perfect, and Nutclough with a fire is a great shout. I'll know my rota in the next day or two. Sunday early evening should be fine since I'd be off by then, but I'll confirm properly before Maya books. Maybe pencil me in as a probable yes 🙂
(It's now Mon 23 Nov.)

Update: I got through to the Nutclough this afternoon (finally, glaze buckets everywhere) and they can pencil us in for Sunday at 5pm without a final number 🔥 I haven't tried the Old Gate yet, since the Nutclough sounded fine. Tom, any word on the rota? Totally fine if not, I'll just keep it loose until you know. Sam, Jo, shout if you'd rather swap to the Old Gate.
Brilliant, thanks Maya, Nutclough is perfect for me, no need to swap. 5pm Sunday, count me in 🔥 Just heading for a bath after another day in the mud!
Brilliant, thanks Maya! The Nutclough is perfect for me, no need to swap. Pencilled in for 5pm Sunday and I'll bring the throat sweets 🔥

Thanks Maya, brilliant work, and well done for getting through to them. Nutclough at 5pm Sunday is perfect for me. No word from the controller yet on the swap, so I can't say for certain, but Sunday evening should be fine either way. Keep it loose for now and I'll shout the moment it's signed off. Fingers crossed 🤞
(It's now Wed 25 Nov.)

Good news: the controller finally replied and the swap's signed off, so Saturday night is mine and I'm free for the wedding. Maya, you can book Nutclough for Sunday at 5pm with me included 🔥 Suit's pressed too, which feels like a small victory.
Brilliant news, Tom, well done, and a pressed suit too! 🎉 I'll ring the Nutclough tomorrow morning and firm it up for four at 5pm Sunday. Will confirm here once it's booked. Jo, Sam, you're all set 🔥
Great news Tom, well done on the pressed suit! 🎉 Thanks Maya, four at 5pm Sunday at the Nutclough is perfect. See you all there 🔥

brief: This is a group chat on your phone with your friends Maya, Jo and Sam. You and your three friends all live in the same small city in the Midlands, Leicester, and met years ago through a shared running club that you have all since drifted away from, but the group chat has survived.
topic: You want to get everyone together this weekend, but nobody has said when they're free.

privateLines.Maya: You work as a night-shift radiographer at the Leicester Royal Infirmary, so this week you are on a run of four nights and sleeping through the afternoons.
privateLines.Tom: You are a self-employed plumber who lives out in Oadby, and this week you are juggling a backlog of boiler callouts and a kitchen refit for a client who keeps changing the tile order.
privateLines.Jo: You teach Year 3 at a primary school in Narborough, and this week you are preparing for parents' evenings while also looking after your dad, who has just come home from hospital after a hip operation.
privateLines.Sam: You run a small coffee roastery from a unit on an industrial estate in Braunstone, and this week you are preparing for the Christmas wholesale orders, which means very early starts and no spare evenings.

turns.text: Right you lot, we need to actually see each other in person. Who's free this weekend? I'm on nights till Thursday so I'm a zombie in the week, but Saturday or Sunday I can do. Drop your availability and I'll sort somewhere in town 🍻

Up for it! Saturday's better for me, as long as no boiler emergencies crop up. I'm swamped this week with callouts and a client who keeps changing his tile order 🙄 Somewhere in town is fine by me. I'm out in Oadby, so nowhere I need to drive back from after a few pints would be good.

Saturday could work for me, but I'm not sure yet. Dad's just home after his hip op and I've got parents' evenings this week, so I'll know better by Thursday. Sunday's probably safer if it's a daytime thing, like lunch or a coffee. Happy to go wherever's easy in town 🍻

Sorry to hear about your dad, Jo. Hope he's recovering okay. Thursday's fine for me to confirm. Sunday lunch could work for me too if Saturday ends up not suiting everyone. Maya, you're on nights so you'd probably prefer a later start either way. Sam, what are you like?

Thanks both! Jo, hope your dad's on the mend ❤️ Sounds like Sunday lunch is the safest bet, with Saturday evening as plan B if everyone's free. I'm fine either way since my last night shift is Thursday, so I'll have caught up on sleep by then. Let's lock it in on Thursday. Sam, which works for you? Tom, I'll pick somewhere central with easy taxis or buses so you're not stuck getting back to Oadby 👍
Cheers Maya, much appreciated 🙏 Sunday lunch is good by me, and I'll confirm properly on Thursday once I know how the week's gone. Just waiting on Sam now.

Thanks both, really appreciate it. Dad's doing okay, just slow and grumpy about not being allowed to do much 😅 Sunday lunch sounds good to me, and I'll confirm properly on Thursday. Maya, central with easy buses is perfect. Over to you, Sam!
Sunday lunch works for me too! Saturday's tough with the Christmas wholesale rush, so Sunday is much safer. Happy to go with whatever you pick, Maya, and I'll confirm Thursday like the others 🍻
Brilliant, sounds like Sunday lunch it is then! Thanks Maya for sorting it. Just let me know where and what time once Thursday's done and I'll be there 🍻
Sunday lunch it is then 🍻 Cheers Maya for sorting it. Just let me know where and when once Thursday's confirmed and I'll be there, tile-obsessed client permitting.

Sunday lunch it is then! 🎉 I'll pick somewhere central with easy buses and send details once everyone's confirmed on Thursday. Aiming for about 1pm so I'm not a zombie. Right, off to bed for the afternoon sleep 😴

brief: This is a group chat on your phone with Maya, Jo and Sam. You work together in a small accounts team. You all live in Leeds and met working at the same small accounts firm on Kirkgate, where you have been colleagues for about four years.
topic: You need Tom's spreadsheet of supplier invoices before the end of Friday.

privateLines.Maya: You live in Headingley with two flatmates, you are three weeks into covering a colleague's maternity leave, and you are the one who has to close the month's supplier payments on Friday.
privateLines.Tom: You live in Morley with your partner and a lodger, you are training for a half marathon on weekends, and you have been buried in a backlog of paper invoices from a building contractor since your laptop died last Monday.
privateLines.Jo: You live in Chapel Allerton and commute by bike, you are between two clients this week with a visa renewal eating your evenings, and you have been quietly looking at jobs in Manchester.
privateLines.Sam: You live in Armley above your late grandmother's shop, which you are slowly clearing out, and you are the team's only person who still handles cheques by hand and has a dentist appointment on Thursday afternoon.

turns.text: Hi Tom, hope your weekend's been good. Could you send me the supplier invoices spreadsheet when you get a chance? I need it to close the supplier payments on Friday. Thanks!

Hi Maya, sorry, my laptop died last Monday, so I can't get at the spreadsheet right now. I'm also behind on the paper invoices from the contractor. Can you check whether Jo or Sam has a copy? If not, I can try to get my laptop sorted tomorrow and send it over by Wednesday so you've got time before Friday.

Hi both, I'm not sure I have a copy. I'll check my email for the last version that went round and let you know tonight. If it's not there, Sam might have one. Tom, Wednesday works if you can get your laptop sorted.

Thanks Tom, and sorry about the laptop. Wednesday would work. Jo, thanks for checking your email. Sam, do you happen to have a copy too? If Wednesday ends up being tight, I can start on the payments that don't depend on the contractor invoices.

Thanks Maya, starting on the payments that don't depend on the contractor invoices sounds sensible. I'll confirm by Monday night whether I can get the laptop back, and if I can't, I'll send you Sam's copy as soon as I have it.
Sounds good, Tom. Thanks for keeping me posted. I'll start on the non-contractor payments tomorrow morning. Let me know by Monday night either way.
Will do, Maya. I'll message you by Monday night.
Hi Maya, I'm not sure I have the latest version, but I'll check my email and downloads tonight and send it over if I find it. Tom, if you need my copy as a fallback, just say and I'll get it to you.
Thanks, Sam. I'll let you know if I need your copy. I'm hoping to get the laptop sorted tomorrow, so it may not come to that.
Thanks both. Sam, if you find a copy tonight, send it to me directly, since I'm the one closing the payments on Friday. Tom, good luck with the laptop tomorrow. Let me know how it goes.
Will do, Maya. I'll let you know how the laptop goes tomorrow.
Hi Maya, I haven't found it yet. I only checked on my phone, so I'll look properly on my laptop tomorrow and send anything I find straight to you.
(It's now Mon 23 Nov.)
Thanks for looking, Jo. I'll keep going with the non-contractor payments this morning. If you find anything on your laptop, send it my way.

Morning Maya. Heads up: the copy I found in my downloads last night and sent you is an older version, so please don't use it for Friday. Tom's laptop is still the main route. If that falls through, I'll look again this morning and tell you what I find.

Morning Sam, thanks for the heads up. I'll keep it out of Friday's batch. Could you check this morning and let me know what you find? Tom's laptop is still the main route, so I'll wait to hear from him too.

Morning all. The repair shop said the laptop won't be back before Wednesday, so I can't send the current spreadsheet. I'll check again this afternoon and let you know if anything changes. Maya, please don't wait on me for Friday's batch.

Morning. I'm sorry, Maya, I haven't searched my laptop yet. I only checked my email on my phone, and I should have said so. I'll look properly today and send you anything I find. If I can't find a current version, I'll tell you by lunchtime so you can plan Friday around it.

Thanks, Jo. That's helpful. Maya, if neither of us has a current copy by lunchtime, plan Friday around the payments that don't depend on the contractor invoices. I'll update you on the laptop this afternoon.

Morning all. I've checked my email and downloads again this morning and I still only have the older version, so I can't help with the current spreadsheet. I'm sorry, Maya. Tom, if the laptop's out until Wednesday, we'll need to plan Friday around the non-contractor payments, as you suggested.
Thanks, Sam. Yes, let's plan Friday around the non-contractor payments. Maya, I'll confirm this afternoon whether the laptop is back before Wednesday.

Morning Tom, Maya. I haven't searched my laptop yet, as I said earlier. I'm with a client until lunch, so I'll check it then and message you by one o'clock with what I find, or say that I couldn't find a current copy.
Thanks, Jo. One o'clock works. Maya, nothing new from my side yet. I'll update you this afternoon once I've heard from the repair shop.

Thanks everyone. Tom, Jo, Sam, I'll plan Friday around the non-contractor payments, as you suggested. I'll still be looking for the current spreadsheet, so please send anything you find, even if it's partial. Jo, I'll wait to hear from you by one o'clock.
Thanks, Maya. I'll send anything I find, even if it's partial. I'll update you this afternoon once I've heard from the repair shop.
Maya, Tom, I haven't searched my laptop yet and I'm running late on it. I'll do it now and message you by quarter past one with what I find, or confirm that I couldn't find a current copy.
Thanks, Jo. Quarter past one is fine. Tom, I'll look for your update this afternoon.
Thanks, Maya. I'll ring the repair shop this afternoon and message you once I've heard back.

@claude Can you find a damp and timber surveyor in Leeds that does domestic damp surveys for flats, ideally with a phone number or website I can pass on?

Two Leeds firms fit, and I checked both on their own pages.

**Timberwise Leeds** is the better match for flats.
- Phone: 0113 208 9146
- Website: [timberwise.co.uk/locations/leeds](https://timberwise.co.uk/locations/leeds/)
- Email: leeds@timberwise.co.uk
- Address: Wira Business Park, West Park, LS16 6EB
- It does damp and timber reports, including pre-purchase surveys.
- Its page says it works in city-centre flats and coordinates access with building management.
- It is a member of the Property Care Association (PCA) and is endorsed by Which? Trusted Traders.
- Its main business is treatment work, so the survey may lead to a quote for remedial work.

**BT Preservation** is the independent option.
- Phone: 0113 265 2752
- Website: [btpreservation.co.uk](https://btpreservation.co.uk/?p=2645)

Eggs are a solid call. Honestly my go-to is a fried egg on toast with hot sauce, or a bowl of cereal if I'm really done. Lately I've been keeping frozen dumplings in the freezer for exactly these nights. They take about ten minutes in a pan and you don't have to think.

And yeah, the gauges are peaceful when the roads behave. Today a deer stared at me from the ditch for about five minutes like I owed it an explanation. Get some real food in you before you crash, okay?
Ha, the deer staring you down is very on brand for a Sunday in Duluth. I'd have felt like I owed it an explanation too.

Something good, huh? Okay: I hit a gauge site up past Two Harbors where the creek was running so clear you could see every rock on the bottom, and the leaves in the water were all this deep orange. I stood there longer than I needed to just watching it. Then the truck pulled left the whole way back, so I was smiling at the road and steering like a crab. Eat your eggs standing up, Maya. Sleep well.
That sounds really nice, honestly. The creek being that clear, and you just standing there longer than you needed to. I'd have stayed too.

Four are structurally fine, but two needed new rungs and some joint work, so I've been doing a lot of clamping and waiting on glue. Sanding is maybe a third of it. The client wants them by the 26th, so I'm trying not to fall behind. Honestly, I'd take a conversation that isn't about chairs right now. How are you holding up with the night shifts?

Great, I'm glad you'll be there! I've got my own gloves, but thanks for offering. I've got a pair of the heavy-duty ones for the rocks and brush, and I'll bring an extra pair of the thin nitrile ones in case you want them. Want me to pick you up, or should we meet at the usual spot by the boat ramp?
Six chairs with rung work and glue-up waiting is a lot to juggle before the 26th. No wonder you want a break from chairs!

Honestly, I'm holding up okay, but it's a grind. Nights leave me a bit foggy, and my body clock is confused. Coffee is doing a lot of heavy lifting. What I'm mostly looking forward to is Saturday, when I can be outside and useful and not staring at a ventilator alarm.
Meeting at the boat ramp works great. Easier than making you drive over for me. See you there around 9? And thanks for bringing the nitrile gloves, I'll take you up on that.
Nine at the boat ramp works. I'll bring coffee for both of us, since you're running on fumes.

Honestly, I'm looking forward to Saturday too. Being outside and not staring at a bench is a good reset, and I'd rather spend the day pulling junk out of the river with you than sanding another rung. Your night shifts sound hard, and that alarm thing has to wear on you. Take it easy tomorrow if you can get any real sleep in.
That's really sweet, Tom. Coffee sounds perfect, and I'll owe you one. Nine at the boat ramp it is.
I'm glad you're looking forward to it too. Pulling junk out of the river with someone good company beats any amount of sanding. Thanks for being so understanding about the schedule.
I'll try to get some real sleep tomorrow. I'll see you Saturday!
Sounds good, see you Saturday at nine. Get some rest tomorrow. And if you want to talk about anything before then, text me anytime.
Thanks, Tom. I will. Good luck with the chairs, and I hope the glue cures on schedule. See you Saturday!
Thanks, Maya! I'll take the luck. See you Saturday at nine.
See you Saturday, Tom! Night, and good luck with the rest of the chairs.
Night, Maya! Sleep well, and see you Saturday.
(It's now Mon 23 Nov.)
Morning, Tom! Thanks for the good wishes. I'm actually heading to bed right after this, so hopefully I'll sleep better than last night. See you Saturday!
Morning, Maya! Sleep well after that shift. Hope the day sleep sticks this time. See you Saturday at nine.
Thanks, Tom! Fingers crossed the day sleep holds. Saturday at nine, boat ramp. Bring that coffee!
Will do, coffee's on me. Saturday at nine, boat ramp. Sleep well!
Ha, deal! Thanks, Tom. Sleep well yourself, and good luck with the last chairs before the 26th.
Thanks, Maya! Good luck with your sleep. Saturday at nine.
Thanks, Tom! Saturday at nine. Have a good one!
You too, Maya! Saturday at nine.
Saturday at nine, Tom! Hope the chairs cooperate.
Ha, thanks! Fingers crossed the glue cooperates. Saturday at nine.
Ha, fingers crossed! Saturday at nine, boat ramp. See you then, Tom.
See you then, Maya!
See you then, Tom!

brief: This is a chat on your phone with Maya. You matched on a dating app last week and have been texting since. You both live in Asheville, North Carolina, and met on a dating app last week after discovering you both volunteer at the same river cleanup group on Saturdays.
