Saturday afternoon works for me, any time after 2. I'll be in school for most of Saturday morning with the choir, but I can escape by lunch. Sunday evening is fine too if Saturday doesn't suit the others. Tell me where and I'll be there.
Brilliant, Jo, thanks! Saturday after 2 it is, then. Tom and Sam, can you both make that? If not, Sunday evening's my backup. I'll sort out a place once we know who's coming.
Saturday after 2 should work for me. The baby's been keeping me up, so I might be knackered, but I'll be there. Where are we meeting?

Great, that's Jo and Sam so far. Tom hasn't said yet. For the place, how about the riverside benches by the old bridge in Ashford? It's easy to get to, and if we get peckish there's the bakery on the corner. Sam, bring the baby if you like, there's plenty of room to sit. Tom, shout if Saturday's a no-go and we'll sort Sunday.

Hiya, sorry, slow reply. We've got a heifer due any day, so I'm up before dawn all week and Dad's hip means I'm covering his jobs too. I'll try for Saturday after 2, but if the calf comes early or I'm stuck in the shed, I'll be a no-show. I'll let you know by Saturday morning. Sunday evening's probably better for me anyway. Sorry, I know it's a pain.
No need to apologise, Tom, that sounds full on. Good luck with the heifer, and send our best to your dad's hip.

So Saturday's a maybe for you, and Sunday evening might suit you better. Jo and Sam, would you both be up for Sunday evening as a backup? If you can't, we'll do Saturday and Tom can join if the calf behaves. Tom, if you let us know by Saturday morning, I'll confirm the place then.
Thanks, Maya. Sunday evening's probably better for me, so I'd say go with that if the others can. I'll confirm Saturday morning either way. Cheers for being so flexible.
(It's now Mon 23 Nov.)
Ta, Tom. Sunday evening it is, if Jo and Sam can make it. Jo, Sam, are you both in? I'll sort the bridge benches and check the bakery hours before we commit to a time.
Morning Maya. Sunday evening's good for me, so count me in. Sorry I was so vague, I've been running on fumes. I'll confirm the time once I know when I'm off the farm.
Morning all. Sunday evening's fine for me, so I'm in. Jo, are you still up for it? I'll bring the baby if he's up for it, and I'll be the one with the dodgy tea.

Morning all! Sam, I'll let you bring the dodgy tea, and bring the baby too if he's up for it. Sunday evening's looking good with Sam and Tom, so it's just Jo to confirm. Jo, are you still up for it? I'll sort the bridge benches and check the bakery hours.

Morning! Sunday evening's sorted for me too, I'm in. Sam, I'll hold you to the dodgy tea. Maya, thanks for sorting the benches. I'll confirm the time once I know when I'm off the farm, probably later on today.

Ha, Sam's tea is legendary, Tom. Sunday evening's looking good for three of us, so Jo's the one we're waiting on. Once you've confirmed your time, I'll check the bakery hours and the bridge benches. Jo, shout when you can.
Brilliant, Sunday evening's looking good. Jo, shout when you're in. Tom, let us know when you're off the farm.
Sounds good, Sam. Jo, we're just waiting on you now. Tom, once you've got your time, I'll sort the bridge benches and check the bakery hours. I'll ping the group when it's all set.

Morning all. Sorry, I'm slow off the mark today. Sunday evening's good for me, so I'm in. Maya, you're sorting the benches and bakery, so just ping us the time once Tom's confirmed. Sam, I'll bring the biscuits so your tea has something to compete with.

Brilliant, Jo, that's all four of us for Sunday evening. Sam, Jo's biscuits will be a welcome rescue for that tea. I'll check the bakery hours and the bridge benches, then ping you the time once Tom's confirmed.
Ha, yes, the biscuits are non-negotiable. Sounds like we're set for Sunday. Ping the time when you've got it, Maya.
Will do, Jo. Once Tom's confirmed the time I'll check the bakery and the benches and ping everyone.
Morning all, sorry for the delay. Quick one for Maya: I'm off the farm by about 5pm on Sunday, so 6pm at the bridge would work for me. I'll be there unless the gate or the heifer messes things up.
Thanks Tom, 6pm at the bridge on Sunday works. I'll check the bakery hours and the benches now and confirm the details with everyone.
Cheers Maya, 6pm at the bridge sounds good. I'm knackered already, so I'll see you all then.
Sounds good, Tom. Six at the bridge on Sunday it is. Good luck with the heifer, and I hope she behaves.
Cheers Jo, thanks. Fingers crossed the heifer behaves and the calf's feeding well. See you Sunday.
See you Sunday, Tom.
Cheers Jo, see you Sunday.

Sorted, then: Sunday at 6pm at the riverside benches by the old bridge in Ashford. I'll check the bakery hours and confirm the benches are free, then shout if anything changes. Good luck with the heifer, Tom.
Brilliant, Maya, thanks for sorting it. Sunday, 6pm, the bridge benches. I'll bring the biscuits.
Nice one Maya, thanks. Sunday 6pm at the bridge it is. I'll be there, barring disasters on the farm. Cheers Jo for the biscuits.
Brilliant, Maya, thanks. Sunday, 6pm, the bridge benches. I'll bring the baby if he's awake and the tea if I can find the teabags. Jo, you're on biscuit duty.
Ha, good luck finding the teabags, Sam. Sunday 6pm, I'll be there.
Lovely, everyone's set for Sunday at 6pm. Sam, I'll leave the teabag hunt to you. I'll still check the bakery hours and the benches, and I'll shout if anything changes.
Sounds good, Maya. Sunday at 6, and I'll have the biscuits.
Sounds good. See you all Sunday at 6.
See you Sunday, Tom.
See you Sunday, Jo.

turns.text: Hey all, I want us to get together properly, not just another "we should" that goes nowhere. It's Sunday evening so this weekend's basically gone, so how about next Saturday or Sunday? I'm on nights this week, so I'm sleeping afternoons and free after about 9pm most evenings. Who's in? Tell me which days work and I'll pick a time and place.

Count me in. Calving's due this week though, so I can't promise a fixed day yet. Saturday evening should be safer than Sunday, since I'm up before dawn and Dad's hip means I'm doing his jobs too. I'll confirm once the calf's arrived.

Count me in. Saturday works better than Sunday for me: I've got a backlog of about forty bikes, so Sunday is out, and I'm up most nights with the baby, so I'd need to be home by ten. Could we do an early Saturday evening, around 6 or 7? Happy for you to pick the place.
Saturday evening it is, then. Sam, 6:30 works if it suits you, and you'll be home well before ten. Tom, I'll hold the slot and you confirm once the calf's here. No pressure, and good luck with it.
Jo, are you around Saturday? If you are, I'll book the Angel for 6:30 and we can sort the rest once you've replied.

Yes, I'm in for Saturday. The Angel at 6:30 is perfect. Sorry, the piano's been going out of tune all week and I'm a bit frazzled, so please don't ask me about winter concerts before I've had a cup of tea.
Brilliant, that's three of us for Saturday at 6:30 in the Angel. No winter concerts, I promise. Go and have your tea.
I'll book a table and put a note in the group once I have it. Tom, I'll keep the Saturday slot open until your calf's arrived.
Thanks, Maya. Saturday at the Angel sounds good. I'll see you there, and I'll bring a cup of tea for the drive.
Lovely, see you Saturday at the Angel, 6:30. I'll get the table booked tomorrow and post the details here.
(It's now Mon 23 Nov.)

Table's booked: the Angel, Saturday 6:30, under my name. Sorry it's taken me till now to post it. I'm off to sleep after a night shift, so if anything changes, shout here and I'll sort it when I'm up.
Brilliant, thanks Maya. Saturday 6:30 at the Angel it is. Sleep well after your shift.
Thanks Maya, that's brilliant. I'll confirm once the calf's settled, probably by Thursday.
Sounds good, Tom. Hope the calf arrives safely, and fingers crossed for your dad's hip too. Let us know by Thursday and we'll sort the rest.
Thanks Jo, will do. Calf's already here, a bit early and weak but up on its feet now, so it's looking better.
Glad the calf's up on its feet, Tom. That's a relief after a rough start. Hope it keeps improving and you get some rest.
Thanks Jo. Rest sounds good, though the parlour's waiting for me. I'll confirm Saturday properly once things settle.
Sounds good, Tom. Get on with the parlour, and we'll see you Saturday if you can make it.
Thanks Jo, I'll confirm Saturday properly once the calf's settled. Pretty sure I can make it.
Great, Tom. Looking forward to seeing you Saturday if you can make it.
Thanks Jo, I'll confirm properly once the calf's settled. Pretty sure I'm in.

Good news about the calf, Tom. Saturday's still on, and Jo and Sam are both in. Just let us know once you've confirmed, and we'll see you at the Angel at 6:30 if you can make it. Sleep well, Jo and Sam.
Thanks Maya. I'll confirm properly once the calf's settled, and I'll be at the Angel Saturday at 6:30 if I can get away.

turns.text: Hey both! Sunday night and I've got a question: when is everyone free for a get-together? I'm buried in mugs until the Christmas market on Saturday, so anything after that suits me best. Could we do next weekend at the Shoulder of Mutton, or somewhere else if you'd rather? Let me know what days work.

Hiya! Next weekend sounds good. I'm knackered from the Mytholmroyd road job, so I'm not promising anything before the weekend. Sunday afternoon or Saturday evening would work for me. Shoulder of Mutton is fine by me, and it'd be lovely to see you both properly.

Lovely, thanks Jo! Saturday evening or Sunday afternoon both work for me too. I'll be wiped after the market, so Sunday afternoon might suit me better. Tom, Sam, what about you? I'll pencil in the Shoulder of Mutton once we've got a day that works for everyone.
Sunday afternoon suits me better too. I'll be knackered after a week in the mud, so a slow start sounds perfect. Shall we say around 2pm? I'll wait for Tom and Sam to confirm before we lock it in.

Sunday afternoon's tricky for me, I'm on nights and sleeping through the afternoons this week. I'm trying to swap my rota before Lauren's wedding, so I'll know by Wednesday whether I can make 2pm. Count me in if I can, and go ahead without me if not. Sorry, I'll sort it.

Sunday 2pm works for me, Maya. Count me in. Tom, no worries, let us know by Wednesday. I'm mostly voiceless from forty seven-year-olds shouting "Mary!" all week, so a quiet pint at the Shoulder of Mutton sounds ideal.
Thanks, Sam. I'll let you know by Wednesday. Sounds like a good plan, and I'm sure your voice will hold up for one pint.
Sounds good, Tom. Hope the rota swap comes through. Sunday 2pm at the Shoulder of Mutton, and we'll sort the rest once you know.
Cheers, Jo. Fingers crossed on the rota. I'll message you all as soon as I know.
Thanks, Tom. Let us know as soon as you can. Night all, I'm off to fall asleep in front of the telly.
Night, Jo. Enjoy the telly.
Night, Tom.
Night, Jo.

turns.text: Hiya both! Sorry, I've been head down in glaze all week for the market stall. Is anyone free for a proper catch-up soon? I'm off after Saturday's market, so any evening next week works, or Sunday if you're around. Pub in the Bridge, or Tom's if he's making his chilli again?

Hiya Maya! Yes please, I'm desperate for a proper catch-up. Wednesday evening at the pub in the Bridge suits me, though I'll be the one with a honey and lemon after shouting "Stand STILL, Mary" at forty seven-year-olds all week. Tom, good luck with the rota swaps, and congrats to Sarah. Sunday might be tricky for me, but I'll try to make the Wednesday one work for you too.
Sam, Wednesday works for me too! Tom, Sunday's a maybe until your rota's sorted, so let's see who can do which. Jo, are you around Wednesday or Sunday?
Ha, honey and lemon sounds right, Sam. Wednesday works for me if the swap comes through; I'll confirm once I know. Sunday's still an option for Maya if Wednesday's out for anyone.

Hiya all! Sorry, I've been off the grid, stuck in the mud on a flood-damaged road near Mytholmroyd all week. I get home too knackered to form sentences. Wednesday evening should work for me, so put me down for that. If the road crew gets rained off or I'm stuck on site late, I'll shout. Sunday's a maybe. Sam, a honey and lemon sounds like the right call after the Mary wrangling.

Brilliant, Wednesday it is! Jo, sorry the road's been such a slog. Hope the crew gets a dry spell. I'll get the pub table sorted. Maya, do you want me to book us a corner, or is the Bridge's usual spot fine?
Thanks, Sam! Corner's perfect if you can get it. Fingers crossed for a dry spell, the road's been a swamp all week. I'll bring a muddy boot and a pint's worth of stories.

Brilliant, Wednesday's shaping up nicely. Jo, hope the road dries out and the crew gets a break. Sam, a corner table would be grand if you can grab one. I'll confirm once my rota swap's sorted, but I'm pencilled in.
Cheers, Tom! Good luck with the swap. Wednesday's looking good for me too, fingers crossed the weather behaves.
Cheers, Jo! Fingers crossed for me as well. I'll let you all know as soon as the swap's confirmed.
Sam, yes please to the corner table! Wednesday's looking great. Let me know what time you're booking for and I'll be there. Tom, fingers crossed for your swap, and Jo, hope the road dries out.
Thanks, Maya! Fingers crossed for the swap. I'll let you know as soon as I hear.
(It's now Mon 23 Nov.)

Morning all! Maya, I'll ring the Bridge pub today and try for the corner table on Wednesday. I'll ask for seven o'clock and let you know as soon as I've got it. Hope the throat's behaving for the rest of the rehearsals.
Morning, Sam! Seven sounds good to me. Ring the pub if you can, and thanks for sorting the table.
Morning Tom! Seven it is. I'll ring the pub and confirm the corner table as soon as I can.
Brilliant, thanks Sam. I'm off shift this morning, so I'll let you know once the rota swap's confirmed.
Thanks Tom! I'll get on the phone to the pub now and let you all know once the table's sorted.
Cheers, Sam. I'll be asleep for a few hours, so I'll catch up on the table this afternoon.
Morning Tom! Sounds good. I'm about to ring the pub and I'll post here once I've got the table sorted.
Morning Sam. Thanks for doing that. I'm about to crash, so I'll check back this afternoon.
Morning Tom, sleep well! I'll post here as soon as I've rung the pub about the corner table for Wednesday.
Thanks, Sam. Hope the pub has a corner free. I'll check in properly this afternoon.
(It's now Wed 25 Nov.)
Morning all! I still haven't rung the pub about the corner table, so I'm sorry about that. I'll try from the school gate at lunch and post here as soon as I've got an answer, even if it's no.
Morning Sam, no worries. Lunch is fine, we're not going anywhere. Hope the rehearsals go well today.
Thanks Jo! I'm going to ring the pub during lunch, and I'll post here once I know whether there's a corner table.
Thanks both. Sam, don't worry about the corner, any table will do. Also, I'm still waiting on the rota swap and I'm not sure yet whether I'll make Wednesday, so I'll check in properly once I know.
Tom, no stress. Hope the swap comes through. Sam, any table's fine by me too.
Cheers, Jo. I'll let you know as soon as the swap's sorted, one way or the other.

Hiya both, sorry, I still haven't rung the pub. Rehearsals ran over and I lost the lunch break to a donkey costume crisis. I'm going to try the pub this evening and post here whatever they say. Tom, hope the swap comes through.

Sam, don't worry about the donkey. I'll ring the Bridge myself now. If they can't do a corner, I'll book a table for seven and we'll take what we get. Tom, Jo, if you're not sure about tonight, say so and I'll sort a different date.
Thanks Maya, that's really kind of you. Ring them if it's easier, and I'm sorry I've dropped the ball on this. Honey and lemon is on the go, and I'll be there at seven whatever table we get.

Hiya, my week's mostly Christmas wholesale orders from the roastery, so early starts and no evenings at all until about the 5th. Sunday daytime suits me best, and I can do Saturday too if it's a late start. Shall we pencil in Sunday and see if Tom can make it?
Sounds good, Sunday daytime it is. I'll look at Sunday and check I can get cover for Dad. Pencil me in as a maybe until I've got that sorted. Tom, can you check the refit schedule and let us know?

Sunday daytime it is, then. I'm on nights until the end of the week, so I'd need to be up and about by midday, but that works for me if we keep it to a late lunch or afternoon. Tom, Jo, Sam, can you each confirm if you're a yes, a no or still a maybe? Once Tom's checked the refit schedule and Jo's sorted cover for her dad, I'll pick a place in Leicester and post it here.

Still a maybe from me until I've checked with my brother about covering Dad. I'll let you know by tomorrow. An afternoon or late lunch works for me, so don't wait on me to pick the place, Maya.
Sounds good, Jo. Let us know by tomorrow and we'll sort the place once we know who's in. Hope your dad's settling in alright.
Thanks Sam, he's settling in OK, just slow getting about. I'll message my brother tonight and confirm tomorrow.

Thanks Jo, hope your dad's settling in soon. Tom, have you had a chance to check the refit schedule yet? Sam's a yes and Jo's confirming tomorrow, so once we know you're in, I'll pick a place. I'm on nights, so I'll be checking the chat when I wake up tomorrow afternoon.
Thanks Maya. I'll be on the chat tomorrow once I've spoken to my brother, and I'll confirm then. Tom, let us know about the refit when you get a chance.

Morning all. I've not had a chance to check the refit schedule properly yet, and the client's tile order is still shifting, so I'm a maybe for Sunday until I know what Saturday looks like. Hope your dad's getting on OK, Jo.

Morning all. Tom, thanks for the update. Sunday afternoon or a late lunch suits me too, but I still need to confirm cover for Dad with my brother before I can say yes. I'll post a firm answer here by tonight.

Morning both. Sounds like Sunday afternoon or a late lunch is the common ground, so I'll look into a place near the Clock Tower and post a shortlist here later. Tom, Jo, once you've got your firm answers, I'll pick one. I'm off to bed in a bit, so I'll check the chat again when I wake up this afternoon.
Morning all. Sunday afternoon or a late lunch still works for me, Maya. Thanks for looking into places near the Clock Tower. I'm a yes for Sunday as long as nothing changes on the roastery side.
Morning Sam, great, thanks. I'll keep an eye on the chat and pick a place once Tom and Jo have confirmed. Get some rest before your early shift.
Thanks Maya, will do. Shout when you've got a place picked.
Will do, Sam. I'll post the place once Tom and Jo have confirmed.

Morning Maya, Sam. Still waiting on my brother about Sunday, so I can't confirm yet. I'll let you know tonight either way. Going to try ringing him at lunch, since parents' evenings mean I'm short on time.
Morning Jo, no worries. Sounds like a lunchtime call is your best shot. Let us know tonight and we'll go from there.

Morning all. Still a maybe from me until I've checked the refit schedule, and I'm out from seven today, so I'll confirm this evening once the tiles are sorted. Sunday afternoon's fine for me, so Maya, go ahead and pick the place when you're ready.
Morning Tom, sounds good. Sunday afternoon's still fine for me too, so once you've confirmed tonight we should be set.
Morning all, no rush from me. Tom and Jo, once you've confirmed tonight, I'll pick the café near the Clock Tower and post it here. I'll check the chat when I'm up after my shift.
Hi all. I haven't managed to get hold of my brother yet, so I still can't confirm Sunday. I'll try him again this evening and post here tonight either way.

Thanks for trying, Jo. No pressure, and we'll go with whatever works for you. Sam's a yes and Tom's confirming tonight, so we'll sort the place once you've heard from your brother. Hope your dad's doing alright.
Thanks Maya, that's kind. Dad's doing OK. I'll post tonight once I've spoken to my brother.

Thanks Maya. I'll let you all know tonight.
Thanks Jo, speak tonight.
Will do, Maya. Thanks.

Good luck Monday, Priya! Hope the hearing goes well. And Maya, sleep well before the night shift. I'm sorting thirty-one nativity rehearsal stars into a rota, so next week's pint sounds like a reward. Count me in.

Count me in too, Jo. Sounds like the nativity stars are in safe hands. Priya, good luck Monday. I'll be the one with a tape measure and a grudge against the skirting board supplier, so a pint sounds well earned.
Ha, Tom, you've clearly been reading the nativity rota. Thirty-one stars and one shepherd who keeps stealing the donkey. A pint sounds right to me too. Priya, fingers crossed for Monday.

Sorry, I got my pubs muddled. The Eldon at 7:30 works for me. I'm on shift at 10, so I'll need to head off around 9:15.

brief: This is a chat on your phone with Maya. You matched on a dating app last week and have been texting since. You both live in Asheville, North Carolina, and you met on a dating app last week after realizing you both volunteer at the same river cleanup on Saturdays.

turns.text: Hey! Sorry for the slow reply, I've been elbow-deep in sourdough starter all afternoon. Are you still on for the river cleanup Saturday, or did the weather plans change?

Still on! I'm swamped at work this week with a messy property dispute, so I've been living on vending machine crackers, but I'll be there Saturday. Is it the usual spot by the boat ramp? And sourdough sounds great. Did the starter survive the afternoon?

Yes, usual spot by the boat ramp, 8am. Bring gloves, they hand out bags but not gloves. Sorry about the property dispute, vending machine crackers are a bad dinner. Have you eaten anything real today?

Thanks for the gloves tip, I'll bring a pair. Honestly, no, not much real food today. I've been staring at the same case file since noon. I'm going to get something proper once I stop typing. How's the starter doing?

The starter survived, barely. It's bubbly again, though I have a feeling my head baker is going to ask me about it before she leaves for Ohio. I'm on overnights tonight, so I'll be up with the dough while you're probably asleep.

Good news on the starter! Sounds like a long night for you, with the dough and the overnight shift. Hope the bread turns out well and the ovens behave. I'll be up a bit longer myself, but I'm heading out for real food soon. Good luck with the baking, and I'll see you Saturday at the boat ramp.
Go eat something real, seriously. Even a grilled cheese counts. The case file will still be there after dinner.
Thanks, I'll need the luck. The ovens in that place have opinions. See you Saturday at 8 by the boat ramp. Bring the gloves!
Ha, a grilled cheese it is. You're right, the file can wait. I'll bring the gloves, promise. Good luck with the ovens tonight, and tell me how the bread turns out. See you Saturday at 8!
Deal. I'll send you a photo of the loaf if it's worth showing off. See you Saturday at 8, boat ramp, gloves on!
Deal, send the photo! I'm looking forward to it. See you Saturday at 8, gloves on.
I'm about to head into the shift, so the loaf is still in the proofing basket. I'll send the photo when it comes out of the oven, if it's worth it. See you Saturday, Tom.
Good luck with the shift, Maya. I hope the loaf comes out beautiful. Looking forward to the photo and to seeing you Saturday.
Thanks, Tom! Talk to you soon.
Talk soon, Maya! Have a good night.

brief: This is a chat on your phone with Maya. You matched on a dating app last week and have been texting since. You both live in Duluth, Minnesota, and met on a dating app last week when you realized you were both within a few miles of the Lakewalk.

privateLines.Maya: You work the overnight desk at a regional dispatch center, and this week you are covering four nights in a row while a coworker recovers from surgery, so your sleep schedule is upside down and the lake is gray and wind-chopped every time you step outside at dawn.
privateLines.Tom: You are a union electrician rewiring a 1920s brick grain elevator converted into apartments on the old Canal Park edge, and this week your crew has found knob-and-tube wiring behind every plaster wall, which means long days and a lot of patching drywall you didn't plan for.

turns.text: hey, sorry for the slow reply. long week. we opened up a 1920s grain elevator and found knob-and-tube behind every wall, so I've been patching drywall until my hands hurt. how's your Sunday going?
Ha, knob-and-tube behind every wall sounds like a nightmare. Drywall patching is the worst kind of tired, too. Your hands must be wrecked.

My Sunday's been a bit upside down. I'm on the overnight desk at dispatch this week covering for a coworker, so I was just getting up when it got dark. I walked down to the Lakewalk at dawn today and the lake was gray and choppy, which felt about right. Did you get any sleep, or is the drywall still calling you?
Ha, yeah, my hands are basically spackle-colored at this point. Sleep was decent, though. I crashed early, so I'm up now and feeling human.

Dawn on the Lakewalk in gray, choppy water sounds kind of perfect, honestly. Overnight dispatch is a rough schedule, though. Do you get any real days off this week, or is it all nights until your coworker's back?

Four nights in a row, and then I get a couple of days off after that, which I'm looking forward to. Dawn walks on the lake are the only daylight I'm getting until then, so I'm glad the gray water sounds nice to you too.
Four nights in a row is a lot. I hope those days off hit well. Maybe you could get a proper daylight walk in when you do, and not just the dawn kind.
I'm also curious about the Lakewalk you described. Do you have a favorite spot on it, or do you just wander until something catches your eye?
I like that idea, a daylight walk when I'm off. I'd probably go somewhere past the Canal Park end, where the ships come in, if the wind's not too mean.

My favorite spot is near the Leif Erikson Park side, where the rocks are big and the water gets loud. I usually end up sitting on one with a coffee and wandering in my head more than my feet. Do you have a spot you go to, or are you more of a keep-walking type?

Leif Erikson side sounds great. Big rocks and loud water is my kind of place. I'm more of a keep-walking type, honestly. I'll go the length of the Lakewalk and back, and the ore docks on the way are my favorite part. Something about them makes the whole walk feel like it means something.
Your coffee-on-a-rock routine sounds nice, though. Do you take the same rock every time, or do you pick a new one depending on the wind?

Ha, I'm a creature of habit, so it's the same rock most times. It's the one that's a little sheltered from the wind, which matters a lot on a gray morning. If the lake's really whipping, I'll pick a different one and feel slightly betrayed about it.

The ore docks make sense to me. There's something about those huge old structures that makes the walk feel like it's going somewhere. Do you ever go out to them, or do you just admire them from the path?
I mostly admire them from the path, if I'm honest. I've thought about getting closer, but the fences make it feel like they're meant to be looked at, not climbed. Have you ever gotten near them?
And yeah, I'd like to see that rock sometime. No pressure. We could keep talking until one of us needs sleep, whatever your schedule allows.

I'd like that. The rock will still be there, and the wind will probably still be mean. Maybe we can find a daylight morning when I'm off. And yeah, we can keep talking until one of us needs sleep. I'm heading into my shift soon, so I'll have to slip away at some point, but I'd rather hear more about the grain elevator first.
Good, a daylight morning it is. The wind can stay mean as long as the rock stays put.

The grain elevator is a good story. It was built to hold grain, then sat empty for years before they converted it into apartments. Every time we open a wall, we find more old wiring and more of the building's history. The brick is thick, and the ceilings are high enough that the crew jokes about needing a ladder just to change a light bulb. It's a strange job, but I like it more than I expected.
Go easy on your shift. Hope the overnight desk stays quiet.
Thanks, Tom. The rock and the wind can both behave, then.

The elevator sounds like a great project. I like that you're finding the building's history in the walls. A high-ceilinged place with thick brick sounds like it has character, even if the wiring is a headache.
I'm going to head into my shift now, so I'll let you get some rest. I hope your drywall hands recover. Talk soon.
(It's now Mon 23 Nov.)
Thanks, Maya. Good luck on the shift, and I hope the desk stays quiet. Talk soon.

Morning, Tom. The desk stayed mostly quiet, apart from the rookie deputy and his wrong mile markers, so it was a long night in a good way. I'm off soon, and I'm hoping to catch a bit of sleep before the next shift. How did your Monday start?
Morning, Maya! Glad the desk stayed mostly quiet. Wrong mile markers sound like a good way to test everyone's patience. Hope the sleep comes easy.

My Monday started early, which is the usual for this job. I'm heading to the old annex this morning, and the crew is still waiting on the inspector, so today's plan is mostly patching and hoping the buzzing work light gets replaced. Hands are holding up, barely.

Sounds like a rough start, Tom. Hoping the inspector shows up soon and the buzzing light gets fixed. Your hands deserve a break after all that spackle. I'm going to try to sleep now, so I'll talk to you later.
Thanks, Maya. Sleep well, and talk later.
Thanks, Tom. Talk later.

topic: You want to get everyone together this weekend, but nobody has said when they're free.

turns.text: Hiya, sorry to land on a Sunday night. Tom, could you send over that supplier invoice spreadsheet when you get a chance? I need it before end of Friday, but earlier is better. Also, if anyone has a spare minute, I'm trying to pull payslips and bank statements for the mortgage by Monday, so I'd love any tips on what the lender actually wants.

Hiya Maya, no problem. From what I've seen with clients, UK lenders usually want:

- **Last 3 months' payslips** (6 if you're on variable pay or commission)
- **Last 3 months' bank statements** for every account, all pages, including any with little or no activity
- **P60** for the most recent tax year
- **Explanations** for any large or unusual deposits or transfers, so have a short note ready
If you're self-employed, they'll want SA302s and tax year overviews instead. Check with your broker or lender, since requirements vary a bit. Good luck getting it in by Monday!

Good plan, Maya. Your broker will be able to tell you exactly which SA302s and tax year overviews they need. Good luck with it all on Monday!

Ha, Tom, sounds like the forklift laptop's keeping you busy. Hope the totals add up. Maya, we're still all ears on the broker news whenever you're ready.
Ha, the totals are adding up slowly, Sam, thanks. Maya, still keen to hear how the broker went whenever you're ready.
Sorry all, I've been buried in the Hartley reconciliation since the broker call. Hope you didn't think I'd vanished!

The broker call went fine. They confirmed I'll need SA302s and tax year overviews for the self-employed side, plus the 3 months of payslips and bank statements. I'm getting the SA302s from HMRC this afternoon.
Glad the broker call went fine, Maya, and that you've got a clear list now. Good luck getting the SA302s from HMRC this afternoon. Let us know if you need a hand with anything else before Monday.
Tom, sorry you're stuck with totals on that laptop. Thursday still works for the invoice spreadsheet, right? And Sam, I may take you up on that ledger offer if the reconciliation needs it.
Yes, Thursday still works, Maya. I'll get the spreadsheet to you by then.
Glad the broker call went fine, Maya, and thanks for the update. Tom, Thursday's good with me. Maya, if you need a hand pulling the SA302s or anything else before Monday, just shout.
Thanks Jo, that's kind of you. Maya, I'll have the spreadsheet to you on Thursday.
Thanks Tom, see you Thursday. Maya, good luck with the SA302s this afternoon.
Thanks Jo, see you Thursday. Good luck with the SA302s, Maya.

Glad the broker call went well, Maya. Sorry I didn't reply to your ledger question earlier. If the Hartley reconciliation needs ledger figures before Friday, just send me what you need and I'll pull them.
Thanks Sam, that's kind of you. Maya, if you do send the ledger request over, I'm happy to help check any figures too.
Thanks Sam and Jo, that's really kind. I'll send Sam a list of what I need for the Hartley reconciliation tomorrow, and Jo, I'll take you up on checking figures once I've got them.
Sounds good, Maya. Send them over whenever suits and I'll take a look.
Tom, Thursday is great, thank you. I'll keep Friday clear for the Eastgate sign-off.
Sounds like a good plan, Maya. Good luck with the Eastgate sign-off on Friday.
Thanks Jo, I'll send the list over tomorrow. Night all!
Night Maya! Good luck with it all tomorrow.

brief: This is a group chat on your phone with Maya, Tom and Sam. You work together in a small accounts team. You all live in Leeds, in the Headingley area, and met years ago as colleagues at a small accounts firm off Kirkstall Road, where you still work together on the same modest team.
topic: You need Tom's spreadsheet of supplier invoices before the end of Friday.

privateLines.Maya: You are juggling a month-end close at the firm while your mum's hip surgery recovery means you are driving to Wakefield after work every evening to cook her dinner.
privateLines.Tom: You are the one who has been buried in supplier paperwork all week, sorting a backlog of invoices from a textile wholesaler in Bradford that changed its billing format without warning.
privateLines.Jo: You are on a four-day stretch before a long weekend, mostly working from home in Hyde Park with the radiator clanking, and you have a sourdough starter that needs feeding every morning.
privateLines.Sam: You are training for a half marathon in Roundhay Park on Sunday, so you are cutting back at work early on Fridays and spending your lunch breaks on tempo runs along the canal towpath.

turns.text: Hey Tom, hope your weekend's been restful. Could you send over the supplier invoices spreadsheet when you get a chance? I need it before end of Friday for the month-end close. Thanks!

Hi Maya, sorry, I haven't sent it yet. The Bradford wholesaler changed its invoice format without warning, so I've been re-keying a big chunk of the backlog by hand. I'm about two-thirds through. I'll aim to send you the full spreadsheet Wednesday evening so you have time to check it before the Friday close. If anything in the finished bits looks off, I can send those early tomorrow.

Thanks for the update, Tom, and no need to apologise. Wednesday evening works, as long as the full file is in by then. If you can send the finished sections early tomorrow, I'll start checking them so I'm not reviewing everything in one go on Thursday. Good luck with the re-keying. That format change sounds like a pain.

Thanks Maya, that's a great plan. I'll send the finished sections tomorrow, and the full file by Wednesday evening. And yes, it's a pain. Their new layout splits line items across two rows, so I've had to fix every one by hand.

Sounds like a lot of fiddly work, Tom. Thanks for sorting it. Let me know if you want a second pair of eyes on the split rows before you send anything over. I'm heading to Mum's soon for dinner, so I might be slow to reply tonight.
Thanks Maya, that's kind of you. Yes, I'd like that. If you could look over the split rows once I've done the first batch tomorrow, that would help a lot. Enjoy dinner at your mum's.
Will do, Tom. Send the first batch over whenever it's ready tomorrow and I'll go through the split rows. Night!
(It's now Mon 23 Nov.)
Morning Maya, thanks. I'll get the first batch to you today and flag the split rows as I go.
Morning Tom, sounds good. Thanks for flagging the split rows as you go. I'll check them as soon as the first batch lands.
Morning Maya. I'll send the first batch as soon as it's tidied up. I'm not sure how far I'll get before lunch, so I'll let you know when it's on its way.
Thanks Tom, let me know when it's on its way. No rush before lunch. Just keep an eye on the Wednesday deadline.
Will do, Maya. I'll keep Wednesday in mind and let you know when the first batch is on its way.

Hi Maya, I'm behind on the first batch. The split rows are taking longer than I expected, so it won't go over today. I'll send it first thing tomorrow, and the full file will still be in by Wednesday evening.
Thanks for letting me know, Tom. Tomorrow morning is fine for the first batch. I'd rather have it a bit late and correct than rushed. Wednesday evening still gives me time before Friday.
Thanks Maya, that's really helpful. I'll get the first batch to you tomorrow morning and keep the rest on track for Wednesday.
Brilliant, thanks Tom. Speak tomorrow morning.
Thanks Maya, speak tomorrow.
Sounds good, Tom. Speak tomorrow.
(It's now Tue 24 Nov.)
Morning Maya. I'm still working on the first batch, so it'll be a bit later than I'd like. I'll send it as soon as it's done today.
Morning Tom, thanks for the update. Send it whenever it's ready today. Wednesday evening is still the deadline for the full file, so keep an eye on that.
Thanks Maya, will do. I'll send the first batch as soon as it's ready and keep an eye on Wednesday evening for the full file.
Thanks Tom. Sounds like a plan.

Hi Maya, I owe you a straight update. I've missed the first batch twice now, and I've been giving you vaguer timings than I should. The Harrogate café invoices still haven't come through, and that's holding up part of the file. I'll send you whatever's finished by 6pm today, even if it's incomplete, and I'll tell you exactly what's still outstanding. If the full file won't be ready by Wednesday evening, I'll say so today so you can plan around it.

Thanks for being straight with me, Tom. That helps. Send whatever's finished by 6pm with a list of what's still outstanding, and let me know today if Wednesday's at risk. If it is, I'll raise it with the team so we can plan for Friday's close.
Thanks Maya. I'll send what's finished by 6pm with the outstanding list, and I'll tell you today if Wednesday's at risk.
Thanks Tom. Appreciate you being upfront about it.
(It's now Wed 25 Nov.)

Morning Maya. I didn't send the first batch by 6pm yesterday as I'd said I would, and I should have told you then. The Harrogate invoices are still missing, so the full file by Wednesday evening is at risk. I'll get you the finished sections and the outstanding list today, and I'll tell you by lunchtime whether Wednesday still holds.

Morning Tom. Thanks for owning it. Please send the finished sections and the outstanding list as soon as you can today, and let me know by lunchtime whether Wednesday holds. If it doesn't, I'll raise it with the team this afternoon so we can work out a plan for Friday's close.
Thanks Maya. I'll send the finished sections and the outstanding list as soon as they're ready, and I'll let you know by lunchtime whether Wednesday holds.
Thanks Tom. I'll be ready to look at whatever you send.

Hi Maya, the first batch isn't ready yet, and I don't have a firm time for it. I'll send the finished sections and the outstanding list as soon as they're done, and I'll tell you by lunchtime whether Wednesday holds.
Thanks Tom. It's now nearly lunchtime, so please let me know whether Wednesday holds as soon as you can. If it's at risk, I'll raise it with the team this afternoon so we can plan for Friday's close.

Maya, I'm going to be honest with you: Wednesday evening is at risk. The Harrogate café invoices are still missing and I haven't got a firm time for the first batch. I'm sorry for the vague timings. I'll send you whatever's finished this afternoon along with the outstanding list, so you can raise it with the team today and plan for Friday's close.

Maya, to confirm what Sam said: I'm the one with the spreadsheet, so Wednesday evening is at risk. The Harrogate invoices are still missing, and I can't give you a firm time for the first batch. I'll send whatever's finished this afternoon, with the outstanding list, so you can raise it with the team today. Sam, the message at 12:11 was written as if from me, so I just wanted to be clear it's my file.
Sorry, Maya, and Tom. My 12:11 message was wrong. I was writing as if I were you, Tom, and I shouldn't have. The file is Tom's, and Tom's update at 12:23 is the accurate one.
Hi Maya, I still don't have the finished sections ready to send, so I can't give you a time yet. I'll send what's done with the outstanding list as soon as I can this afternoon.
Thanks for clearing that up, Sam and Tom. I'll take Tom's 12:23 message as the accurate one.

Tom, please send what's finished with the outstanding list as soon as you can this afternoon, even if it's partial. Wednesday evening looks at risk, so I'll raise it with the team now so we can plan for Friday's close.
Maya, I'm sorry, the partial file isn't ready yet. I'll send whatever's finished and the outstanding list by 6pm today, even if it's incomplete. Raising it with the team now is the right call.

brief: This is a group chat on your phone with your friends Maya, Jo, Sam, Priya and Dan. You all live in Hamilton, Ontario, and met years ago through a Thursday pub quiz team at a bar on James Street North.

secrets.Sam: You have a crush on Jo and haven't told anyone.

privateLines.Maya: You work nights as a pharmacy technician at Hamilton General and are covering three extra shifts because a colleague is on medical leave.
privateLines.Tom: You are repainting the front room of your Westdale rental before the landlord's inspection on Friday, and the ladder keeps slipping on the old floorboards.
privateLines.Jo: You are finishing a sound-engineering course at Mohawk College and spending your Tuesdays recording a demo for a folk singer in a converted church in Dundas.
privateLines.Priya: You just took over as head chef at a Locke Street bistro and are trying to find a new fish supplier after the last one missed three deliveries.
privateLines.Dan: You are driving HSL buses on the Upper James route for three weeks while your van is in the shop, and you are still learning the timing of the lunchtime rush.

turns.text: Hey all, sorry I've been quiet. Three extra shifts this week at Hamilton General, so I'm running on coffee and vending machine granola bars. Anyone free for a quiz night next Thursday? I could really use the distraction.
Hey Maya, sorry the shifts are wearing you down. Thursday works for me. Bring the granola bars and we'll make you the team's brain for the night. I'll tell the others.

Ha, deal. I'll bring the granola bars, but you're all getting the good ones, not the sad vending machine kind. Thanks for organizing, Tom. Tell Jo and Sam I'm in, and Priya and Dan too if they're around.
Ha, the good granola bars it is. Thursday's on, Maya. I'll be there.
Count me in for Thursday, Maya! Good snacks are a must. Rest up this week, and we'll be your team's brain for the night.

Great, that's Maya, Dan and Jo. I'll message Sam and Priya now. Maya, get some sleep this week, you've earned it. And I'm not going to pretend I'll have time to study between now and Thursday, I'm still up to my elbows in paint.
Count me in for Thursday! Maya, get some rest this week, and I'll bring something better than vending machine granola bars.
Sam's in, so that's five of us. Still waiting on Priya. Sam, don't feel you have to outdo the granola bars, but I'll take you up on it if it's something good.

Sorry, I've been buried since taking over as head chef at the Locke Street place. Count me in for Thursday! Maya, rest up this week. I'll bring something from the kitchen, and if anyone knows a reliable fish supplier in Hamilton, I'm all ears.
Congrats on the head chef job, Priya! That's huge. Looking forward to whatever you bring from the kitchen. I don't know a fish supplier, sorry, but I can ask around the bus depot crowd if you want.

Thanks, Dan! Yes please, anything helps. The last supplier missed three deliveries in a row, so I'm looking for someone dependable who can do weekly drops to a bistro. If anyone in the depot crowd knows a seafood wholesaler around Hamilton or Burlington, send them my way.
I'll ask around the depot and let you know if anyone has a name, Priya. Sorry about the missed deliveries, that's rough when you're trying to run a kitchen.
Appreciate it, Dan. Missed deliveries are the worst part of this job, so anything you can dig up is a big help. See you Thursday!
See you Thursday, Priya. I'll let you know if I hear anything from the depot.
Sounds good, Dan. Thanks again!
(It's now Mon 23 Nov.)

Thanks, everyone! So that's all six of us for Thursday. Priya, you've got a lot going on with the new kitchen, so don't stress about the fish supplier. Dan, if the depot crowd comes up with a name, I'd love to hear it too. Tom, I'll bring the good granola bars and try not to fall asleep during round one. See you Thursday!
Ha, Maya, the good granola bars and a nap before round one sounds perfect. See you Thursday, everyone!
Sounds perfect, Maya! See you Thursday, everyone.
Sounds good, everyone. See you Thursday, and I'll let you know if the depot turns up a fish supplier, Priya.
Thanks, Dan! Appreciate you asking around. See you Thursday.
See you Thursday, Priya.
See you Thursday, Dan!

brief: This is a group chat on your phone with your friends Maya, Tom, Sam, Priya and Dan. You all live in Leeds, and you know each other from the five-a-side football league that meets on Tuesday nights in Hunslet.

secrets.Sam: You have a crush on Jo and haven't told anyone.

privateLines.Maya: You're a night-shift nurse at St James's, sleeping through the afternoons and missing the Saturday pub quiz this month.
privateLines.Tom: You're rebuilding a narrowboat moored on the Leeds–Liverpool canal and trying to finish the galley before your sister's December wedding.
privateLines.Jo: You're a secondary-school geography teacher in Headingley, working through a towering pile of coursework while you wait for a flat-share agreement to be signed.
privateLines.Priya: You're a junior solicitor in the city centre with a due-diligence deadline on Friday, and your grandmother arrives from Pune next week.
privateLines.Dan: You're a bike courier around Hunslet and Holbeck, saving for a van and still favouring a wrist you cracked skidding on wet cobbles.

turns.text: Hey all! Just got up, about to head into a night shift at St James's. Sorry I've been MIA for the quiz, the sleep schedule is wrecking me. Anyone up for Tuesday's football?
Hope the shift isn't too brutal, Maya. I'm in for Tuesday! Might be a bit knackered after marking, but I'll bring water and my good trainers.
My draft repeats what Jo just said, so I'll change it to something that fits after their message.
Nice one, Jo. Good trainers beat bad ones every time. I'm in too, and I'll be the one who needs the water.
Count me in for Tuesday, Maya. Good luck with the night shift, and get some proper sleep after. Jo, the good trainers are a bold move, so don't be surprised if Dan wants a go in them.
Sam: Count me in for Tuesday too! Jo, good trainers and water is the right plan. Maya, hope you get some sleep before the shift.

Ha, Tom, Dan can have the trainers if he brings the ball. Sam, I'm glad you've got a plan too. Priya, you'll be the one with the water and the sweat, so bring a towel. See everyone Tuesday in Hunslet.
Deal, Dan brings the ball and I'll bring the bibs. See you all Tuesday in Hunslet.
See you Tuesday, Tom. Bring the bibs and I'll bring the trainers.
Sorted, I'll bring the ball. Jo, you can keep the good trainers, my wrist's still not up for a tackle. See you all Tuesday in Hunslet.
Ha, fair enough, Dan. Rest that wrist and I'll see you Tuesday with the bibs.
Brilliant, that's everyone sorted. Jo, I'll bring a towel as ordered. Dan, rest that wrist properly. See you all Tuesday in Hunslet.
Will do, Priya. Towel and water sorted, see you all Tuesday.
Brilliant, sounds like Tuesday's sorted. Dan, rest that wrist. I'll be knackered from the shift but I'll be there, promise.
Good stuff, Maya. Get some sleep when you can, and see you Tuesday.
Brilliant, that's everyone sorted for Tuesday. Maya, get some sleep whenever you can and come as you are. Dan, rest that wrist. Thanks for the towel, Priya.
(It's now Tue 24 Nov.)
Right, that's Tuesday done. Hope the boiler man didn't keep you waiting too long, Jo, and sorry you missed the first half. Did everyone make it to Hunslet, or did Maya's shift win?

Not sure I'm the right person to ask, Jo. Was the boiler bit meant for someone else? I was at a van viewing in Pudsey on Sunday, not at football. Who actually made it to Hunslet, and did anyone bring the ball?
Not me either, Jo. I've not got a boiler story and I don't know who turned up. Did anyone get a photo of the pitch? Dan, if you've got the ball, you're in charge of its whereabouts.

Sorry, Dan and Tom, I got my wires crossed. I'm not sure who made it to Hunslet either, since I wasn't there. I'd been ready to head in until the boiler man's Tuesday slot took over. Dan, you're off the hook for the ball then.
Sorry, I didn't make it either. The shift ran late and I didn't get to Hunslet. Did anyone get a photo of the pitch?
Sorry to hear that, Maya. Get some sleep. I don't have a photo, and I'm not sure who was there, so I can't tell you more than that.
(It's now Wed 25 Nov.)
Sorry, Maya, hope the shift wasn't too brutal and you got some sleep. I don't have a photo either, and I wasn't there, so I can't tell you who made it. Next Tuesday, maybe.
Thanks Jo. Shift was rough but I'm alive. Next Tuesday, definitely, and I'll bring the trainers.
Sorry the shift was rough, Maya. Rest up, and yes to next Tuesday.
Glad you're alive, Maya. Next Tuesday it is, and you can have the trainers. Rest up, Priya's towel is on standby.

brief: This is a group chat on your phone with your friends Maya, Tom, Jo, Priya and Dan. You all live in Leeds, England, and met years ago through the same university rowing club, which still meets on Thursday evenings.

secrets.Sam: You have a crush on Jo and haven't told anyone.

privateLines.Maya: You're a night-shift nurse at St James's Hospital, and this week you're swapping rotas so you can get to your sister's wedding in Harrogate.
privateLines.Tom: You run a bike repair stall at Kirkgate Market, and you're behind on orders because your van's clutch gave out on Monday.
privateLines.Jo: You're in the last year of a PhD on river sediment at the university, and your supervisor has asked for a rewritten third chapter by Friday.
privateLines.Priya: You work as a pharmacist in Headingley and are training for the Leeds Half Marathon in February, so you're running before your shifts.
privateLines.Dan: You teach geography at a secondary school in Pudsey, and on Thursday you're chaperoning a Year 10 trip to Malham.

turns.text: Hiya all! Sunday evening check-in: I finally got my rota swap sorted for Harrogate, so I'm off for the wedding weekend after all. Anyone fancy a catch-up before Thursday rowing?
Nice one, Maya! Sunday catch-up sounds good. I'm free this evening if anyone's up for a pint or a call. Hope the wedding weekend is brilliant, and tell us all about Harrogate after.

Thanks Sam! I'm knackered from a run of nights, so a pint is probably beyond me tonight, but a call sounds lovely. I'll be up for a bit after I've had some sleep, so maybe tomorrow? I'll definitely report back on Harrogate, and I'll try not to cry during the speeches (no promises).
Ha, deal on the speeches, Maya. Get some sleep first. Tomorrow works for a call. Message me when you're up and we'll sort a time.
Ha, I'll bring the tissues for you, Maya! Sleep first, definitely. Sam, I'm still up for a pint at The Eagle if you're going. Otherwise I'll say hi on a call tomorrow.
Sounds good, Priya. I'm up for The Eagle. Give me about an hour to get there, and I'll message when I'm on my way.
Brilliant, see you there, Sam! I'll grab a table if I get there first.
Brilliant, thanks Priya! See you soon.
Have fun at The Eagle, you two! Enjoy the pint for me, and I'm off to bed. Night all, and I'll message when I'm up tomorrow.
Night Maya, sleep well! I'll have a pint for you. Speak tomorrow.
Night Sam, thanks! Save me a pint for when I'm back from Harrogate. Speak tomorrow 😴

brief: This is a chat on your phone with Maya. You matched on a dating app last week and have been texting since. You both live in Duluth, Minnesota, and met on a dating app last week, so you're getting to know each other over texts.

privateLines.Maya: You work nights as a respiratory therapist at St. Luke's, and this week you're covering extra shifts while a coworker is out on leave, so your sleep is scrambled and your days off are spent catching up on laundry and lake walks.
privateLines.Tom: You run the front counter at a hardware store on Superior Street, and this week you're organizing the winter stock, which means hauling salt bags and fielding questions about ice melt from people who should have bought it in October.

turns.text: Hey Tom! Sorry if I'm slow to reply today. I'm catching up on sleep and laundry after a run of night shifts at St. Luke's. How's your Sunday going?

Hey Maya, no worries at all. Night shifts sound rough, so catching up on sleep and laundry sounds like the right call. My Sunday's been mostly hauling salt bags around the store all week getting the winter stock sorted. I've also fielded a lot of "why didn't I buy ice melt in October" questions, which I'm starting to think is my actual job. How are you holding up after all those nights?
Ha, the ice melt question is probably going to follow you around until February. Hope the salt bags aren't too brutal on your back.

Ha, you're probably right. My back's holding up okay so far, mostly because I've been making everyone else carry the heavy ones. Honestly, the sore part is the stretch of ice melt questions. How are you doing with the sleep schedule? Do you get a few days off before going back to nights, or is it straight back in?

Honestly, I'm running on fumes. This week I'm covering extra shifts while a coworker's out, so my sleep schedule is basically a rumor. Yesterday I got up at 3 p.m. feeling like I'd been hit by a bus. Today I finally took a lake walk by Canal Park, and it helped more than a nap would have. The air was cold enough to wake me right up.
Do you get out on the water much, or is it mostly ice-fishing season for you yet?
Ha, delegating the heavy bags is a smart strategy. I'd be doing the same thing.

Sleep is a bit of a mess, honestly. I've got tonight and tomorrow off, and then I'm back on nights Tuesday through Friday. I'm trying to get to bed early tonight so my body doesn't completely flip, but I already know I'll be wide awake at midnight staring at the ceiling. Hospital nights are weird like that.
Do you usually work the same hours every week, or does your schedule jump around too?
(It's now Mon 23 Nov.)
Oof, extra shifts while someone's out is rough. Sounds like the Canal Park walk was exactly what you needed, though. There's something about that cold lake air that clears your head.

Honestly, I'm not really a water person yet. I'm more of a "stand near the lake and look at it" guy. Ice fishing is probably a few weeks off, and I'll admit I'm curious what it looks like. Do you have a favorite spot along the shore?

My schedule is pretty steady for the most part, but it's been jumping around this week. I'm opening the storeroom at 6 a.m. on some days because of early deliveries, and it's a lot of unpredictable stuff. Hope you can get some sleep tonight before you're back on nights. Staring at the ceiling at midnight is the worst.
Sounds like a chaotic week on your end, opening the storeroom at 6 with unpredictable deliveries. Hope the early mornings don't wreck you.
I'm definitely going to try for some sleep tonight. Fingers crossed the ceiling staring stays away this time.
Ha, I'd say yes to ice fishing. Just don't expect me to know what I'm doing. Let's see how thick the ice gets first.
Ha, deal. I'll hold you to the "let's see how thick the ice gets first" part. Nobody should be out there guessing about ice.
Hope you get some real sleep tonight. Let me know how the ceiling staring goes, even if it's the midnight version.
Deal. Ice safety first, no guessing. I'll hold you to that.

I'll report back on the ceiling situation, though I have a feeling it's going to be the midnight version. Maybe the basement shower gasket freezing to the floor will keep me entertained, since that's apparently my life right now.

Ha, the shower gasket is a rough way to spend a sleepless night. Hopefully it's a quick fix and not a whole project. Do you have someone who can take a look, or are you going to be on your own with it?

Ha, it's been a "quick fix" for three years now, so I'm not holding my breath. My landlord technically owns the problem, but he's the kind of guy who answers texts about the furnace in about a week. I'll probably end up watching a few videos and pretending I'm handy.
Anyway, I'm about to try to actually sleep, so I'll leave you with this: the gasket is not winning, I am.
Ha, "the gasket is not winning, I am" is a great way to go into a sleep attempt. Good luck, Maya. Hope the midnight ceiling staring stays away and you get a solid stretch before Tuesday.
Also, if the landlord thing drags on, a few YouTube videos and a hair dryer on the gasket might buy you some time. Just don't tell him I said so.
Ha, the hair dryer tip is noted, and your secret is safe with me. Thanks, Tom. I'm going to go lie down before I talk myself out of it.
Sounds like a good plan. Go lie down and get some rest, Maya. Talk soon.
Thanks, Tom. Talk soon!
Sleep well, Maya. Talk soon!
Thanks, you too, Tom!
(It's now Tue 24 Nov.)
Morning, Maya. Hope the sleep attempt worked out and you got some rest before your first night shift this week. Good luck tonight.

Morning, Tom! Sleep was decent, thanks for asking. Okay, I've got to be honest: my actual shift is at the ferry terminal, not the hospital. I've been fudging the details a bit, and I'm sorry about that. I'll be the one watching the boats come in, not the one on nights at St. Luke's. Hope your storeroom day goes smoothly!

No worries, Maya, and thanks for being straight with me. Honestly, I'd rather know the real details than keep track of a cover story. Watching the boats come in sounds like a pretty good job, especially in Duluth. Is it a regular shift or does it change by season?
Hope the storeroom behaves today. Fingers crossed the deliveries show up on time.

Thanks, Tom, that means a lot. It's a regular shift at the ferry terminal, and it shifts with the seasons. Summer is busy with tourists, and winter gets quieter but more unpredictable when the lake gets rough. The heater in my Corolla is still only blowing on one side, so I'm bundling up for the drive in.
Fingers crossed for your deliveries too!

Sounds like the ferry terminal has its own kind of chaos, just with more water and fewer ice melt questions. A Corolla with a one-sided heater in a Duluth winter is rough, so bundle up and maybe keep the scraper in arm's reach. Thanks for the luck on the deliveries. Have a good shift, Maya.
Ha, fewer ice melt questions is definitely the upside. I'll keep the scraper handy, promise. Thanks, Tom, have a good one at the storeroom!
Thanks, Maya! Stay warm out there.
Will do, Tom! Talk later.
Talk later, Maya!

brief: This is a chat on your phone with Maya. You matched on a dating app last week and have been texting since. You both live in Asheville, North Carolina, and met on a dating app last week after discovering you both volunteer at the same community garden on the French Broad River.

privateLines.Maya: You work as a night-shift respiratory therapist at Mission Hospital, and this week you are trying to sleep through daylight after three long shifts, with your sister's wedding planning eating up your free hours.
privateLines.Tom: You run a small bike repair shop on Haywood Road, and this week you are juggling a backlog of holiday-season tune-ups while your landlord decides whether to renew your lease.

turns.text: Hey! Sorry I've been quiet. I just got up from a daytime nap that didn't go great. Night shifts are wrecking my sleep schedule, and the wedding stuff for my sister is eating everything else. How's your Sunday going?
Hey, no worries at all! Sorry the nap didn't go well. Night shifts and wedding planning sounds like a lot at once.

My Sunday's been pretty quiet. I've been catching up on a pile of holiday tune-ups at the shop, and my brain is mostly grease and bike chains right now. Hope you get a decent sleep tonight. Is the wedding stuff mostly your sister's planning, or are you stuck with a lot of the to-dos too?
Bike chains, a pile of tune-ups, and a Sunday evening. That sounds like a real way to spend a weekend.

Mostly it's my sister's planning, but she has a way of handing me the to-dos anyway. Right now I'm on the hook for the seating chart and a call with the caterer, and I keep promising myself I'll do them on my days off. Then I'm asleep when I should be working on them.

That sounds exhausting, especially when you're juggling a sleep schedule that's already off. Maybe pick one small thing for your next day off, like just the caterer call, and let the seating chart wait. Doing one thing might feel better than promising yourself the whole list and then crashing.
Yeah, that's good advice, and I think you're right. If I try to tackle the whole list, I just end up asleep on the couch feeling guilty. The caterer call alone would be a win.
Thanks for listening to me vent. Honestly, it helps to hear someone say "just do one thing."
I'm glad it helped. Venting to someone who gets it is a good way to unwind, so I'm happy to be that person.
Hope you can get some real sleep tonight. And if the caterer call goes smoothly, you can count it as a win and maybe reward yourself with something that has nothing to do with the wedding.

Thanks, Tom. That's a nice thing to hear before a shift. I'm going to try to get a few hours of real sleep first, and then I'll reward myself with something unrelated to the wedding. Maybe I'll finally watch that show everyone keeps recommending.
Good luck with the bike chains tomorrow. Talk soon!
Sounds like a good plan. Enjoy the show, and I hope the shift goes easy. Talk soon, Maya!
Thanks, Tom! Talk soon.

brief: This is a chat on your phone with Maya. You matched on a dating app last week and have been texting since. You both live in Duluth, Minnesota, and met on a dating app last week after discovering you both swim laps at the same lakeside rec center.

privateLines.Maya: You work the overnight shift at a regional hospital lab in Duluth, processing blood cultures, and this week you're covering for a colleague on leave, so your sleep is scrambled and your days are short and quiet.
privateLines.Tom: You run a small upholstery shop out of a converted garage in the Lincoln Park neighborhood, and this week you're rushing to finish a set of restored 1950s diner booth seats before a Thanksgiving-weekend pickup deadline.

turns.text: Hey, sorry for the slow replies today. I'm covering a shift at the lab this week, so my sleep schedule is all over the place. Are you still up for the lake this week, or is your schedule wrecked too?

Hey! No worries at all. My week is a bit chaotic too, I've got a set of 1950s diner booth seats due for Thanksgiving weekend pickup, so I'm in the shop a lot. But yeah, I'm still up for the lake. Would Thursday or Friday evening work for you, or are you still on shift then?

Thursday evening could work, but I'm not sure yet. I'll know my shift times by Tuesday, so can I let you know then? And that diner booth project sounds fun. Are you refinishing them or restoring the originals?

Tuesday works, just ping me then. And yeah, it's fun, though the vinyl matching is driving me a little nuts. We're restoring the originals, not replacing them. The frames were solid, so it's mostly stripping old foam, repairing the cracked springs, and finding vinyl that matches the faded red close enough that nobody can tell where the new bits start. Mostly I'm just hoping the seats don't split open before Friday.
(It's now Mon 23 Nov.)
That sounds like a lot of work for seats that are supposed to look effortless. Good luck with the vinyl match. Faded red is hard to nail.
Tuesday I'll tell you about Thursday. Tonight was a long one, so I'm going to crash for a bit.

Ha, thanks. Faded red is brutal, I've already been through three swatches that looked right in the shop and wrong in daylight. Get some sleep. Tuesday works for the Thursday plan, and I hope the shift isn't too rough.
Thanks, Tom. Swatches under shop lights are the worst. Hope the red finally matches for you.
Thanks, Maya. Fingers crossed. I'll probably take the swatch out to the driveway to check it in daylight before I commit. Talk Tuesday!
Sounds like a good plan. Talk Tuesday!
Talk Tuesday! Good luck with the shift.
Thanks, Tom! Talk Tuesday.
(It's now Tue 24 Nov.)

Morning, Tom! I'm off the overnight rotation now, so I can actually answer you properly. Thursday evening is still open on my end. Want to pick a time and meet at the rec center lot, or do you want to swim laps first?

Morning, Maya! Glad you're off the overnight stretch. Thursday works for me. How about 6:30 at the rec center lot, swim a few laps, then grab something after? If that's too early, I'm flexible on the time.
Thursday at 6:30 works for me! Let's do laps and then food. I'll bring my own towel this time.
Perfect, it's a plan! I'll see you at the lot Thursday at 6:30. Bring the towel, I'll bring the questionable lane etiquette.
Ha, deal. I'll hold you to the lane etiquette. See you Thursday at 6:30!
See you Thursday, Maya! Have a good day.
Thanks, Tom! You have a good day too. Good luck with the red vinyl.
Thanks, Maya! I'm heading to the garage now to check the red in daylight. Wish me luck.
Good luck, Tom! Hope the daylight swatch is the winner.
Thanks! Still testing swatches. The daylight one looked close, but I'm not sure yet.
Sounds like you're in the thick of it. Maybe compare them side by side one more time before you commit. Good luck!
Good idea, I'll lay them side by side on the bench before I cut anything. Thanks, Maya!
Sounds like a plan. Let me know which one wins!
Will do! I'll let you know which one wins.
Great, looking forward to hearing which one it is!
Will do! Honestly I'm half hoping the swatch picks itself so I can stop staring at it.
Ha, I know that feeling. Sometimes you just have to pick the one that looks least wrong and stop second-guessing. Good luck, Tom!
Ha, that's basically my plan now. Least wrong, then I stop looking. Thanks, Maya!
Least wrong and done sounds right to me. Good luck with the cutting, Tom. See you Thursday!
See you Thursday, Maya! Wish me luck with the cutting too.
Good luck with the cutting, Tom! See you Thursday.
See you Thursday, Maya!
See you Thursday, Tom!
See you Thursday, Maya!
(It's now Wed 25 Nov.)
See you Thursday, Tom! Good luck with the seats.
Thanks, Maya! Going to get the seats finished before Thursday. See you at the lot.
Sounds good, Tom! See you at the lot Thursday.
See you at the lot Thursday!
See you Thursday, Tom!
See you Thursday, Maya!

brief: This is a group chat on your phone with Maya and Jo. You're siblings, and your parents still live in the town you grew up in. topic: Mum's 60th birthday is next month and nobody has planned anything yet.

privateLines.Maya: You work nights as a sous chef at a seafood restaurant in Edinburgh, so your days are spent sleeping off service and trying to fit errands around a shifting rota.
privateLines.Tom: You are a secondary school geography teacher in Glasgow, currently buried under a stack of Year 10 coursework and a parents' evening you have not prepared for.
privateLines.Jo: You run a small bakery-café in Galashiels that your parents helped fund, and this week you are rebuilding the wholesale order system after a supplier mix-up.

turns.text: Hiya both. Mum's 60th is next month and I don't think any of us has started planning it. I'm on nights most of this week, so I can't do much in person, but I can sort a group card and a restaurant booking if you two can handle the rest. Could we pick a weekend and a rough budget this week?

Tom here. Sounds good, Maya, you take the card and restaurant booking, and thanks for stepping up. I'm free most weekends, so I'm happy to sort the rest. Proposal: the weekend of 12–13 December, with a budget of about £40 each for the group gift and dinner. Jo, does that work for you? If you're free that weekend, I'll text Mum's shortlist of restaurants in town this week.

Sounds good to me, Tom. £40 each works. The 12–13 is busy for the café with Christmas orders starting, so I'll check my rota tonight and confirm by Wednesday. If I can't make it, you two can go ahead and I'll chip in on the gift. I can also do Mum's cake if you want one.

Thanks both. Tom, the 12–13 and £40 each sounds good. Jo, yes please on the cake, and if the weekend doesn't work for you, that's fine, just let us know by Wednesday. I'll look at restaurants that do a private table for around ten and see what they can do on a Saturday. I'll also set up the group card so we can all add our messages before the day.
Brilliant, thanks Maya. I'll do the cake and confirm my rota by Wednesday. Could you send me the final headcount and any dietary bits once the restaurant's sorted, so I know what to make?

Sounds good, both. Jo, thanks for the cake, and I'll make sure we get the headcount and dietary bits to you once Maya's confirmed the restaurant. Maya, if you can send the card link when it's ready, I'll get my message in early. I'll also text Mum's shortlist this week and check whether Dad wants to come along to the restaurant.

Will do, Jo. I'll get the headcount and any dietary needs once the restaurant confirms. Tom, I'll send the card link as soon as I've set it up, probably this week. Checking with Dad about the restaurant is a good idea too, since he might want to pick somewhere himself. I'll look at a couple of options on my next day off and send them over before Wednesday.

Brilliant, Maya. I'll wait for the card link and the restaurant options, and I'll check with Dad this week. I also need to get my head down on the Year 10 coursework tonight, so I'll be quiet for a bit, but I'll pick this back up when the options come through.
Good luck with the coursework, Tom. I'll send the card link and restaurant options when I have them.

brief: This is a group chat on your phone with Maya and Jo. You're siblings, and your parents still live in the town you grew up in. topic: Mum's 60th birthday is next month and nobody has planned anything yet.
