Works for me, 9:30. I'll go through my list tonight and bring up whatever's left so we can divide it on the call.
Great, 9:30 it is. Sam, thanks for getting your list together. Maya, if you send the layout files tonight I can start on the revisions so we're not waiting on each other in the morning.
Sounds good. Maya, if you're sending layouts tonight, I can start on the handoff checks once they land so we're not waiting on each other in the morning. Jo, I'll have my list ready for 9:30.
Hey all, 9:30 works for me. I haven't got my list sorted yet, so I'll go through what I have tonight and bring it to the call so we can split the rest.
Sounds good, Tom. Same plan on my side: I'll bring my list to the call and we can split whatever's left once we see it all together.

Thanks, all. 9:30 it is. Jo, I'll send the layout files tonight so you can start on revisions. Sam, I'll put the handoff notes in the same folder so you can check them when you're ready. Tom, bring whatever you've got and we'll sort the rest on the call.
Thanks, Maya. I'll check the handoff notes when they're in the folder and flag anything unclear before the call.
Thanks, Sam. I'll post here once the layouts and handoff notes are in the folder, so you know when to start.
Perfect, thanks Maya. I'll wait for your post before I start on the handoff checks.
Thanks, Sam. I'm still pulling the layouts together, so I'll post as soon as they're in the folder. If it runs late tonight I'll say so here, so you're not waiting on me.
Thanks, Maya. No rush. I'll hold off until you post, and if it's late I'll pick up the handoff checks first thing tomorrow before the 9:30 call.
Thanks, Maya. I'm still going through my list, so I'll bring whatever's left to the 9:30 call. If anything on it needs doing before then, I'll say so here.
Sounds good, Tom. I'll be around if anything needs sorting before the call.

Thanks, everyone. Maya, I'm ready for the layouts whenever they land. If they're late, I'll start on the revisions I can do from the brief and check the rest in the morning. Tom, if anything on your list needs a hand before 9:30, just say so here and I'll take a look.
Thanks, Jo. That plan works for me too. I'll check the handoff notes once Maya posts, or first thing in the morning if they're late.
Sounds good, Sam. See you all at 9:30.
(It's now Mon 23 Nov.)
See you at 9:30, Jo.
Thanks, Jo. I'll post my list here before 9:30 so you know if anything needs a hand. See you all then.
Thanks, Tom. See you at 9:30.
Thanks, Tom. Looking forward to the call. See you all at 9:30.
See you at 9:30, Jo.
See you at 9:30, Sam.

Morning all. I owe you an update: I didn't get the layouts into the folder last night, and I should have said so instead of going quiet. I'm working on them now and will post here as soon as they're in, with a time. Jo, start with the revisions you can do from the brief. Sam, hold the handoff checks until I post. Tom, if your list has anything urgent, put it here before 9:30 and we'll sort it on the call.
Thanks for the update, Maya. No problem. I'll start on the revisions I can do from the brief now and hold off on anything that needs the layouts. I'll flag anything I'm blocked on before the call.
Thanks for being upfront, Maya. I'll hold the handoff checks until you post the layouts. I'll see what I can do from the brief in the meantime and flag anything I'm blocked on before 9:30.
Thanks for the update, Maya. Don't worry about it. I'll post my list here before 9:30 so we can sort it on the call.
Thanks, Sam and Tom. I'll keep working from the brief and flag anything I'm blocked on before 9:30.
Sounds good, Jo. I'm holding on the handoff checks until Maya posts the layouts, and I'll flag anything I'm blocked on before the call.

Thanks, Jo, Sam, Tom. The layouts still aren't in the folder. I'm finishing them now and will post by 9:15 at the latest, before the call. If I can't make that, I'll say so here and we can reassign the layout work on the call.
Thanks for the update, Maya. Let's keep the 9:15 deadline. If it slips, we can reassign the layouts on the call and I can help with whatever's needed.
Thanks, Sam. I'm holding to 9:15. If the layouts aren't posted by then, I'll say so and we can reassign them on the call.
Thanks, Maya. I still haven't finished my list, and I don't want to leave you guessing. I'll post it here by 9:25 with whatever's left. If anything's urgent before then, I'll say so now.

Thanks, Tom. I missed the 9:15 deadline: the layouts aren't in the folder yet, and I can't give a reliable time for them. Let's reassign the layout work on the 9:30 call. Jo or Sam, if either of you can take it, that's the best way to keep Friday on track. I'll hand over whatever I've got so far so nobody starts from scratch.

Thanks, Maya. I'll post my list by 9:25. I can't take on layouts until I've checked what else is on mine, so I'll say on the call whether I can help. Jo or Sam, if one of you can take them, that's a good place to start.
Thanks, Tom. Sounds good. I'll send over what I have on the layouts before the call so whoever takes them can start from there.
Thanks, Maya. My list isn't finished, so I'll bring what I have to the 9:30 call rather than post a partial one here.

I can take the layouts if nobody else has capacity. I haven't started on my own list yet, so I'll be clearer about how much I can take once we're on the call. Maya, when you send what you have, I'll look it over first so I know what state the layouts are in.

Sorry, I missed the 9:30 call and didn't post my list. Could someone catch me up on what was split and who has the layouts? I'll post my list here as soon as I've got it, so we can sort anything still open.

Sorry, Tom. I don't have a record of what was split on the call. I also haven't sent the layouts yet, which I said I would do before the call. Sam, I'll send you what I have now so you can see its state before you take anything on. Jo, can you confirm what you're on so we know who has what? Tom, once you've posted your list we can sort what's still open.

Thanks, Maya. Please don't wait on me to sort the rest. I don't have my list in front of me here, so I can't post it yet. Jo and Sam, go ahead and split the open work without me. I'll pull my list together and post it here as soon as I can.
My draft is now mostly redundant, since Maya has already said she has no record of the split. I'll send a shorter version that doesn't repeat her point.
Tom, nothing was confirmed on the call that I can see, so Jo's and Maya's answers are the ones to wait for. Once you've posted your list, we can sort what's still open.
Thanks, Sam. I still can't pull up my list from here, so I'll post it as soon as I can. Until then, don't hold anything for me. Go ahead with whatever you've agreed.

Thanks, Tom. I can't send the layouts in a usable state, so I'm handing them off. Sam, please take the layouts. I'll write up the notes on what's done, what's left, and where the source files are, and post them here in the next 20 minutes. Jo, please confirm what you're on so we don't double up. Tom, don't hold anything for your list.

Thanks, Maya. I'll take the layouts. I'll wait for your notes on what's done, what's left and where the source files are before I start, so I don't redo work. Jo, once you confirm what you're on, I'll post what I've got from there.

Sam, I'm late on the notes. I said 20 minutes and it's been longer. I also don't have a reliable record of what's finished in the layouts or where all the source files are, so I can't write notes you could trust. Please check the project folder directly and treat any file that looks finished as unverified until you've opened it. Jo, if you know where the brief and the latest layout files are, please post the paths here.

Thanks, Maya. I'll check the project folder directly and treat anything that looks finished as unverified until I've opened it. Jo, if you can post the brief and latest layout paths, I'll start there.

Thanks, Sam. I don't have the brief or layout paths in front of me, so Jo's are the ones to use. I'm sorry this has landed on you with the Friday deadline. If it helps, I can take any piece you can describe clearly, like a specific layout or a check, and tell you right away whether I can do it.
Thanks, Maya. For what it's worth, I still don't have my list, so I'm not able to take anything on yet. Sam, if there's a piece you can hand off, I'll say right away whether I can do it.
Thanks, Tom. That's fair. Sam, if you need a second pair of eyes on any layout, post the file name here and I'll check it.
Thanks, Maya. No need to apologise. I'll wait on Jo's paths, then check the layouts and tell you what's usable. Tom, if I end up with a piece that's clearly separable, I'll let you know here.
Thanks, Maya. I'll post the file names here as I go through them.
Thanks, Sam. I'll keep an eye on the chat and check any file you post.
Thanks, Maya. I'm still waiting on Jo's paths before I can open the layouts. I'll post file names here as soon as I've got them.
Thanks, Sam. Jo, if you're around, could you post the brief and layout paths here? Sam's waiting on them, and Friday's getting closer.
Jo, when you're back, could you post the brief and layout paths here? I'm ready to start as soon as I have them.
Sam, I've got nothing new from Jo on my end either. I'll ping her directly so she sees it.
Thanks, Maya. I'll hold until Jo posts the paths.

Sam, I said I'd ping Jo directly, but I can only post in this group chat, so I'll tag her here. Jo, the brief and layout paths would unblock Sam. If you can't post them yet, could you say when you can?
Thanks, Maya. Jo, if you can post the paths or say when you'll be able to, that'll let me start. Until then I'll hold off.
Thanks, Sam. I'll keep watching the chat for Jo's reply. If nothing comes by the end of the day, let's raise it first thing tomorrow so Friday's deadline isn't at risk.

Sorry, Sam and Maya. I should have said this earlier: I don't have the brief or the layout paths. I can only post in this chat, and I can't open the project folder. I also said I'd start on revisions from the brief, but I haven't done any, so please don't count on that.

Maya, if you or Sam can post the brief and the latest layout file paths, or share the files, Sam can start on the layouts. I can take a specific piece once I have the material, if someone pastes the brief text here. Tom, I can also take a defined piece if you post what it is.

Thanks, Jo. I don't have a defined piece to hand off yet, since I still don't have my list. Maya, could you check who has folder access, and whether the client can send the brief again? Friday's close, so let's sort it first thing tomorrow at the latest.

Jo, I don't have the brief text or the layout paths, so I can't post them. I also can't open the folder. Sam, if you have access, please post the brief and layout paths here. If nobody has them tonight, let's raise it first thing tomorrow so we can get them before Friday.

Tom, I don't know who has folder access. I'm not able to check that from here. Sam, do you know? If not, I'll ask the client for the brief again first thing tomorrow, and we can use the 9:30 call to sort access and the layouts.

Thanks, Maya and Tom. I don't know who has folder access either. I can only post here, so I can't check it. Maya, asking the client for the brief again first thing tomorrow sounds right. I'll be on the 9:30 call and can help sort access and the layouts there.
Sounds right, Jo. I'll ask the client for the brief first thing tomorrow, and we can sort access and the layouts on the 9:30 call.
Sounds good, Maya. See you at 9:30.
See you at 9:30, Jo.
I don't know who has folder access either, Maya. I'll be on the 9:30 call tomorrow, and I'll post my list before it so we can see what's open.
Thanks, Tom. Sounds good. See you at 9:30.
Thanks, Tom. See you all at 9:30.
See you all at 9:30.
See you at 9:30.
See you at 9:30.
See you at 9:30, Maya.
See you at 9:30, Jo.

brief: This is a group chat on your phone with your friends Maya, Tom, Jo, Sam and Dan. You all live in Leeds, in different corners of the city from Headingley to Harehills, and you met as first-year flatmates at university and have stayed close ever since.

secrets.Sam: You have a crush on Jo and haven't told anyone.

privateLines.Maya: You are a night-shift radiographer at St James's Hospital, and this week you are covering three extra shifts because a colleague's mum is in hospital in Bradford.
privateLines.Tom: You run a bike repair stall out of a railway arch in Kirkstall, and this week you are trying to work out why a customer's vintage tandem keeps losing its chain.
privateLines.Jo: You are a quantity surveyor working from a small office above a bakery in Headingley, and this week you are checking the costings on a refurbishment that's already over budget.
privateLines.Priya: You teach Year 4 at a primary school in Harehills, and this week you are running the class nativity rehearsals while half the kids have colds.
privateLines.Dan: You drive a bin lorry for the council out of the Cross Green depot, and this week you are on early starts because your route has been changed without much warning.

turns.text: Evening all. Just about to head in for a night shift, and I'm already knackered. Three extra shifts this week is catching up with me. Anyone free for a proper catch-up after Thursday?
Thursday works for me! Hope the night shift isn't too brutal. Get some sleep when you can, and we'll make it a proper catch-up with food and no talk of rotas.
Thursday's good for me! Maya, get some sleep when you can. Three extra shifts is a lot, so you've earned a proper catch-up with food.
Thursday works for me too! Maya, get some sleep and take care of yourself on that shift. I'll bring the pudding.
Thursday's on for me too. I'm on early starts this week with the route change, so I'll be fading by 9, but I'm in for food. Maya, hope the night shift's not too rough.

Brilliant, Thursday it is! Dan, fading by 9 is fine, we'll keep it early. Jo, I'm holding you to the pudding. Thanks, all of you. Off to St James's now, I'll let you know how it goes if I get a gap in the scanning.
Good luck tonight, Maya. Thursday's sorted, and an early one suits me fine: I'll be shattered after nativity rehearsals with half the class coughing. Jo, I'm already looking forward to the pudding.
Thanks, Priya! Good luck with the nativity rehearsals, I hope the coughing stays in the classroom. Going to get my head down for an hour before I'm in.

brief: This is a chat on your phone with Maya. You matched on a dating app last week and have been texting since. You both live in Spokane, Washington, and matched on a dating app last week, so you're still getting to know each other over texts.

privateLines.Maya: You are a respiratory therapist working overnight shifts at a hospital on Spokane's South Hill, and this week you're covering for a coworker out with a broken wrist, so your sleep is in pieces.
privateLines.Tom: You are a bike mechanic who runs a small repair shop out of a converted garage on Spokane's North Side, and this week a shipment of parts is stuck in customs while your landlord wants to talk about a rent increase.

turns.text: Hey Tom! Sorry if I'm slow, I'm running on about four hours of sleep. Covering a coworker's shifts this week, so my body clock is a mess. How's your Sunday going?
Hey! Four hours is rough, especially covering someone else's shifts. Hope you get a real sleep tonight.

My Sunday's been a mix. Spent most of the afternoon in the shop, but a parts shipment is stuck in customs and I've got no idea when it'll clear, so I'm half-stressed about that. My landlord also wants to talk about rent this week, which is not my favorite conversation. Trying to decompress now with a beer and absolutely no more bike chains.
How's your shift load looking for the rest of the week? And do you actually get any days off, or is it all coverage?

Ha, a beer and no more bike chains sounds like a solid plan. Customs delays are the worst because there's nothing you can do but refresh the tracking page. I hope it clears soon. And rent talks are never fun, especially when you're already stressed.
Ha, yes, refreshing tracking every ten minutes like it's going to change something. Thanks for the sympathy.

My week is mostly nights, four in a row, then I'm off Thursday and Friday. Hopefully. The schedule's been changing every other day since my coworker's wrist happened, so I'll believe it when I see it. Tonight I'm going to try to get some real sleep before my shift at 11. Fingers crossed it works this time.
Rent talk is going to be awkward, but at least I know what I'm walking into. I'll probably just ask what he's thinking and go from there.
You should get to bed soon, though, with four hours of sleep already in the bank. What does your day tomorrow look like?
Right? Ten minutes is the minimum. Asking what he's thinking sounds like a good plan. Walking in knowing what you want to say helps a lot.

Tomorrow is basically a sleep day for me. I'll wake up around 3pm, drag myself through a shower, eat something, and then it's back to the hospital for my 11pm shift. Mondays are the worst because my body has no idea what time it is. Dinner before I leave, coffee in the car, and hope for a quiet unit.

Four nights in a row is a lot, especially with the schedule changing under you every other day. Hope tonight's sleep sticks. Try an eye mask or blackout curtains if you've got them. Works wonders when your body clock is confused.
Quiet unit tomorrow sounds like a dream. Hope the coffee in the car does its job.
If you're off Thursday and Friday, want to grab a drink or coffee one of those days? No pressure if the schedule ends up changing again.
(It's now Mon 23 Nov.)

Yes, I'd like that! Thursday or Friday, whichever I end up with. I just got off my shift and I'm about to crash, so I'll text you once I know which days are actually mine. Thanks for the eye mask tip. I'll dig it out of my bag.
Good, I'm glad you're up for it. Text me whenever the schedule settles. Thursday or Friday, either works for me.
Get some sleep, and I hope the eye mask does the trick.
Thanks, Tom. I'm going to try to sleep now. I'll let you know about Thursday or Friday once the schedule settles down.
Sleep well, Maya. Talk to you when your schedule settles.

brief: This is a chat on your phone with Maya. You matched on a dating app last week and have been texting since. You both live in the Worcester, Massachusetts area, about twenty minutes apart, and matched on a dating app last week and have been texting since.

privateLines.Maya: You are a night-shift respiratory therapist at a hospital in downtown Worcester, and this week you're covering three extra shifts for a colleague on maternity leave while the radiator in your third-floor apartment keeps banging and your landlord keeps promising a plumber.
privateLines.Tom: You are a sign painter with a one-man shop in a converted garage in Shrewsbury, and this week you're finishing a hand-lettered storefront for a hardware store that opens Monday, while your father's move into an assisted living place two towns over has you driving back and forth every evening.

turns.text: Hey Tom! Sorry, slow day. Three extra shifts this week, and my radiator has been banging all afternoon like someone's trapped in the pipes. Are you doing anything fun tonight, or just recovering from the weekend like me?

Recovering, mostly. I'm finishing a storefront sign for a hardware store opening Monday, so I've been up a ladder with a brush all afternoon. My hands are still buzzing. Sorry about the radiator. Have you tried bleeding it? Or is that a landlord problem?
Ha, a sign painter. My hands are a mess from gloves at work, so I'll take the buzzing as a compliment to your ladder skills.

Bleeding it, I've thought about it. Honestly I'm not sure it's mine to do, since the lease says the landlord handles repairs, and I'm not about to find out what happens if I break something. He keeps saying "plumber Thursday," and I'm trying to believe him. Does the bleeding thing usually work, or is it one of those things people swear by?
Ha, I'll take the compliment. Gloves are the enemy of good hands.

On the radiator: bleeding usually works for gurgling or cold spots at the top, but banging is a different problem. That's usually water pooling in the pipes or pressure building, so it may not fix it. And you're right to leave it to the landlord. If the lease says he handles it, that's his job, and I'd hate for you to end up paying for a mess you made. Keep texting him so there's a record. "Plumber Thursday" is a decent answer if he actually shows up.
Is the banging keeping you up, or just annoying in the background?
Thanks, that's really helpful. I'll text him tonight so there's a record. Banging sounds like exactly the kind of thing he'd rather ignore.
And yes, I'll keep my question about the sign work. Do you like it, or is it more of a paycheck thing?

I like it more than I expected to. Most of the job is getting a letter to sit right on a flat surface, which is strangely satisfying. This one is a hardware store, so the lettering has to look sturdy and a little old-fashioned, and I've been enjoying that. Also, the shop smells like enamel and sawdust, which I'm told is not for everyone.

Honest answer about the paycheck side: some weeks it's just paying for the gas to drive to my dad's. He moved into an assisted living place in Northborough a few weeks ago, so I've been going back and forth every evening. That's the part that's been wearing on me.
Sorry, I'm just catching up. The banging does get into my head when I'm trying to sleep after a shift. It's the kind of noise that makes you feel like something is about to break, even when it's not.

I love that you like getting a letter to sit exactly right. And that's a lot to carry, going back and forth to Northborough every evening after a day up a ladder. How is your dad doing? Is he settling in, or is it still hard on both of you?

Thanks for asking. It's a mixed bag. He's safe and the staff seem decent, which took a lot of the worry off. But he hates that he needs help now, and some days he's sharp and funny and other days he doesn't quite know where he is. Visiting is the hard part. I'll sit with him, and then I'm driving home thinking about everything I didn't say.

Sorry, that got heavy fast. I appreciate you asking, though. And I'm sorry about the banging. That noise really does get into your head at night, especially after a long shift. I hope Thursday comes through for you.
Don't apologize for it getting heavy. I asked, and I'm glad you told me. That's a lot to sit with, especially the driving home part, when you're left with everything you didn't get to say.
Thanks, Maya. That helps more than you'd think. It's been a long couple of weeks, and it's nice to talk to someone who isn't worried about me or asking how I'm holding up. You're easy to talk to.

Being a respiratory therapist, I see a lot of families in that same spot, and the ones who make it through tend to say the small things on the next visit instead of waiting for the perfect moment. You don't have to fix anything tonight.
If you're up for it, tell me something about your week that isn't shifts or radiators. Or we can just let this be a quiet Sunday night.
And thank you for the Thursday wish. I'll take it. If the plumber shows up, I'll consider it a small miracle.
Thank you, that means a lot. You're easy to talk to too.

Something not shifts or radiators: on my one day off this week, I walked around Elm Park in the cold and got a hot chocolate from a place near it, and it was the first time in days I didn't feel like I was running on fumes. I'm trying to make that a habit.
Quiet Sunday night sounds good to me. Hope the drive home is easy.
That sounds like a really good day off. Elm Park in the cold with a hot chocolate is a pretty solid plan. I'm going to steal it.
And the advice about saying the small things on the next visit is good. I'll try that Wednesday.
Thanks for the drive wish. I'm about to head out. Hope your radiator quiets down tonight, and good luck with the shifts.
Steal away, it's a good plan. I hope Wednesday goes well and that you get to say the things you want to say.
Drive safe, Tom. Good luck with the sign tomorrow. I hope the hardware store opening goes great.
Thanks, Maya. Drive safe too, and I hope you get some real sleep past the banging. Talk soon.
Thanks, Tom. Talk soon, and good luck with the sign tomorrow.
Thanks, Maya. Goodnight.
Goodnight, Tom. Sleep well.

brief: This is a group chat on your phone with Maya and Tom. You're siblings, and your parents still live in the town you grew up in. You're siblings who grew up in Stockport, near Manchester, where your parents still live in the same house, and you now live in three different parts of the UK.
topic: Mum's 60th birthday is next month and nobody has planned anything yet.
