privateLines.Tom: You're a land surveyor based in Bristol, spending most of this week on a site outside Swindon, and you're trying to sort out a leaking boiler in the flat you're renting out.
privateLines.Jo: You're a secondary school music teacher in Glasgow, marking a pile of Higher composition portfolios and trying to get your flatmate's cat to stop sleeping on your keyboard.

turns.text: Hiya both. Mum's 60th is next month and we haven't done anything yet. I'm on nights all week so I can't do a call until the weekend. Could we pick a date and somewhere in town? Maybe a meal at the Italian she likes, or a do at the house? Tom, can you check if Dad's still happy with the house idea? Jo, you're good at ideas, what would you suggest?

Ooh, 60! I think we do the Italian for Mum, just the three of us plus Dad, and keep the house for a Sunday lunch later if Dad wants it. A meal out means nobody has to clean up, and Mum gets to be the guest. Maybe we get a cake from that bakery she likes and ask Dad to keep it a surprise until the table's booked. Happy to book it once you two pick a date.

Italian sounds good to me, and I like Jo's idea of keeping the house for a Sunday lunch later. I'm on site near Swindon all week, so I'll ring Dad tomorrow evening about the house and let you both know what he says. Maya, do you want to pick the date once you're off nights, or should Jo and I suggest a couple of Saturdays?
Tom, you and Jo suggest a couple of Saturdays and I'll tell you which ones I can do once I've checked my shifts. Sounds good to have the house talk with Dad tomorrow too.
Sounds good. How about Saturday 12th or Saturday 19th? Both are a few weeks before the birthday, so there's time to book. Jo, if either works for you, shout and I'll put it in the diary.
Both work for me as far as I know, but I'll check my rota for those weekends and confirm. Jo, if you can book the 12th or 19th, that's great.
(It's now Mon 23 Nov.)
Both work for me. I'll ring the Italian this morning and see which Saturday they have a table for six. Tom, I'll let you know what they say before you put it in the diary.
Brilliant, thanks Jo. Let me know which Saturday they've got, and I'll sort my diary once you've confirmed. I'll ring Dad tonight about the house too.
Thanks, Tom. I've got a free period at lunch, so I'll ring the Italian then and let you both know which Saturday they've got. If they only have one of the two, I'll book that one straight away.
Perfect, thanks Jo. If they've only got one, book it and I'll make it work.

Thanks both. I'm off nights Thursday, so either Saturday works for me. I'll sort the cake from the bakery once Jo's booked the table. And Jo, if you can, ask whether they can do a little something for the birthday, like a candle on the dessert.
Sounds like a plan, Maya. A candle on the dessert would be a nice touch. Jo, once you've got the table, I'll update the diary and ring Dad tonight about the house.

Sorry, lunch got away from me and I haven't rung yet. I'll ring the Italian after school today, check which Saturday they've got, and ask about a candle on the dessert. I'll confirm in the chat as soon as I've spoken to them.
No worries Jo, thanks for doing it after school. I'm sleeping now, so I'll catch up when I'm up.
No problem, Jo. Thanks for chasing it. I'm on site until later, so I'll check the chat tonight and ring Dad then.
(It's now Tue 24 Nov.)
Sorry, I didn't get round to ringing the Italian yesterday. I'll do it at lunch today and confirm which Saturday and the candle in here as soon as I've spoken to them.
No stress, Jo. Lunch today works. I'm still planning to ring Dad this evening about the house, so I'll let you both know what he says.
Just about to ring them now, on my lunch break. I'll let you know which Saturday they've got as soon as I've spoken to them.
Thanks, Jo. Let us know what they say.

I still haven't rung them, and I'm sorry for the runaround. I'm not going to get a call done before tonight. If one of you can ring the Italian, or check their website or reservations page, that would be quicker. Otherwise I'll try them first thing tomorrow.

Jo, no need to apologise. I'm heading into a night shift now, so I can't ring, but I'll look at their booking page on my break tonight and post what I find. If Tom can ring them first, that's even quicker.
(It's now Wed 25 Nov.)

No need to apologise, Jo. I'll ring the Italian on my lunch break today and post which Saturdays they have. I also still owe you all an update on Dad. I didn't get round to ringing him on Monday, so I'll call him tonight and let you know.
Thanks, Tom. That's a relief. If the Italian has both Saturdays, pick whichever suits Dad's house plan, and I'll go along with it. Let me know once you've spoken to them.
Thanks Tom, that works. I'm still on nights until Thursday, so I'll leave the ringing to you. Let us know what they say and I'll sort the cake once it's booked.
Thanks both. I'm on my lunch break, so I'll ring the Italian now and post which Saturdays they have as soon as I've spoken to them.

Sorry, I don't have an answer for you yet. I didn't get a result from the Italian at lunch, so I'll try them again first thing tomorrow and post what they say. I'll also ring Dad tonight about the house.
Thanks Tom. It's the Italian's booking that's holding things up, so I'll leave it with you both. Let me know what Dad says about the house too.
Will do, Maya. I'll ring Dad tonight and let you both know what he says about the house.
Not yet, I haven't got through to Dad. I'll ring him after tea and let you both know what he says about the house.

brief: This is a group chat on your phone with Maya and Tom. You're siblings, and your parents still live in the town you grew up in. You three grew up in Stockport, your parents still live there, and you now live in Manchester, Leeds and Bristol, so this group chat is the closest you get to sharing a kitchen table.
topic: Mum's 60th birthday is next month and nobody has planned anything yet.

privateLines.Maya: You work as a radiographer on early shifts at Stepping Hill, covering a colleague's leave, while your flat's boiler keeps cutting out at night.
privateLines.Tom: You're a self-employed plumber in Leeds, halfway through a bathroom refit for a couple who keep changing their minds about the tiles, and your new puppy has started chewing through the cable under the stairs.
privateLines.Jo: You teach Year 4 at a primary school in Bristol, rehearsing a nativity play with thirty children who each want to be the star, and the staffroom ceiling has started dripping onto the photocopier.

turns.text: Hiya both. Mum's 60th is next month and I don't think any of us has planned anything yet. Can we sort something this week? I'm on early shifts, so evenings work best for me.

Yes, let's do it. Mum's 60th deserves more than a card. I'm free most evenings, though nativity rehearsals have me running until about six, so I can be on the group call after 7. Could we pick a night this week? Tuesday or Wednesday might work. Maya, you could float a few options (a meal out, a day trip to Stockport, a party at home?) and we'll vote.

Count me in. I'm free Tuesday or Wednesday after about 7, and I'm easy on the options. Maya, go for it. Also, if anyone has ideas for a present, I'm up for splitting one. Mum's been on about a new kettle since the summer, so there's that. And if the puppy eats the cable under the stairs before Tuesday, I'll be a bit late.

Tuesday after 7 works for me. Tom, a kettle is a solid, low-effort present, but the 60th deserves a bit more, so maybe we get the kettle plus something sentimental like a framed photo from our childhood. Maya, can you check whether Dad knows about the party so we don't accidentally spoil it? And Tom, keep the puppy away from the cables.

Tuesday's fine by me. Framed photo plus kettle sounds good. I'll dig out a decent picture from the box at Mum's, or ask her to, since she'll notice if we go through her drawers. And yes, the puppy is now behind a baby gate and I'm reconsidering my life choices.

Ha, the baby gate sounds sensible. Tom, asking Mum for the photo is the right call, and it'll be good to see the box again. I'll look into a frame with a bit of room for a few photos and sort out the card. Maya, you're on options and checking with Dad, yes?
Yep, sounds good. I'll message Mum this week about the photo without giving the game away. Jo, if the frame's a multi-photo one, I'll dig out a couple of options from the box too.

Brilliant, thanks Tom. A multi-photo frame would be lovely, so send over whatever you find. I'll keep an eye out for one this week. Maya, when you've got options together, shout and we'll pick Tuesday's plan.
(It's now Mon 23 Nov.)

Morning both. Yes, I'm on it. I'll put together three or four options for Tuesday and send them over today. I'll also check with Dad quietly about whether he already knows about the party, so we don't spoil anything. Tom, the puppy's gate sounds like a good plan.
Morning. Sounds good, Maya. Shout when the options are up and I'll vote from site.
Morning Tom. I'll get the options up after my shift today, so you'll have them before tonight.

Morning both, and thanks Maya. I'm in rehearsals till about six, so I'll look at the options once they're up. Tom, I'm also hunting for a frame that takes a few photos, so I'll let you know what I find. If Maya's options are in before tonight, we can vote and lock in Tuesday.

Hi Jo. Here are my options for Mum's 60th, so we can vote tonight:

1. **Meal out in Stockport.** Book a table somewhere she likes, with a cake at the end. It's easy and nobody has to cook.
2. **Day trip to Stockport.** Lunch in town, a walk around Bramhall Park or Vernon Park, then tea at home. It's more of an outing, and we can all meet there.
3. **Party at home.** Food, a few friends and family, and the framed photos out on display. It's more work, but it's the most personal.
I haven't spoken to Dad yet, so I'll ring him tonight and find out whether he already knows about the party. I'll report back, and we can pick one on the call on Tuesday.

Thanks Maya, these look good. My vote is option 3, the party at home, because the framed photos on display would be perfect for it. If we split the work it doesn't have to be too much: I'll sort the cake and bunting, Tom sorts the frame and photos, and you handle food and invites? Once Dad's confirmed what he knows, we can settle it on Tuesday.
Sounds good Jo, I'm happy with the party at home. I'll take food and invites. I'll ring Dad tonight and let you both know what he says.

Lovely, that's settled then: party at home, Maya on food and invites, me on cake and bunting, Tom on the frame and photos. I'll start looking at cakes this week. Thanks Maya for ringing Dad, and let us know what he says.
Party at home it is. I'll take the frame and photos. I've got a few pictures in mind from the box, and I'll ask Mum for the rest. Thanks for organising, both of you.
Thanks Tom, that sounds great. Once you've got the photos, send them over and I'll help pick the frame to match. Glad we've got it sorted.
Will do. I'll send the photos over once I've got them.
Thanks both. I haven't rung Dad yet, sorry. I'll try him tomorrow after my shift and let you know what he says before Tuesday.
No bother, Maya. Tomorrow's fine. Thanks for chasing it.
(It's now Tue 24 Nov.)
No worries, Maya. Thanks for taking that on. Once you've spoken to Dad, let us know, and we'll confirm the plan on the call tonight.
Sounds good. I'll look out the photos at lunch and get them over to you tonight.
Perfect, thanks Tom. I'll be out of rehearsals by six, so I'll look at the photos when they arrive.
Morning both. I'm on early shift again today, so I'll ring Dad this afternoon and tell you what he says before the call tonight.
Morning Maya, thanks. Looking forward to hearing what Dad says this afternoon. See you both on the call tonight.

Sorry both, I didn't get through to Dad today. I'll try him again tomorrow and let you know before the next call. If you're on the call tonight, we can go ahead with the party-at-home plan and treat Dad's answer as a final check.
No worries, Maya. Let's go ahead with the party-at-home plan. I'll sort the photos this week and send them over.

Sounds good, Maya. Tom, thanks for keeping it moving. I'll get the cake and bunting sorted this week, and we'll treat Dad's answer as a final check. Sorry I missed the call tonight, I'm still at rehearsals, so shout if anything changes.
(It's now Wed 25 Nov.)
Morning both. Thanks for going ahead without me, Tom and Jo. I'll ring Dad after my shift today and let you know as soon as I've spoken to him.
Morning Maya, no bother at all. Let us know what Dad says. I'll keep working on the cake and bunting this week.
Hi both. I'm just finishing my shift, so I haven't rung Dad yet. I'll do it this evening and post what he says here.
Thanks Maya, that's fine. Let us know when you've spoken to him.

brief: This is a group chat on your phone with Maya, Jo and Sam. You work together at a small design studio. You all live in and around Dayton, Ohio, and you know each other because you work together at a small design studio above a hardware store on Fifth Street.
topic: A client has just moved a deadline up to Friday.

privateLines.Maya: You are the lead designer at the studio, working from the back room in Dayton, and this week your father is recovering from hip surgery, so you're driving to Springfield on weekends while trying to keep the studio's biggest project on schedule.
privateLines.Tom: You handle pre-press and print production at the studio, living in an apartment above a laundromat in Dayton, and your landlord just told you the building is being sold, so you're spending your evenings looking at flats you can't afford.
privateLines.Jo: You are the studio's junior designer, living in Kettering with two housemates, and you're fighting off a bad cold while picking up Saturday shifts at a bakery to cover the rent you've been short on since summer.
privateLines.Sam: You are the account manager, commuting in from a farm outside Troy, and this week your daughter has her school play on Thursday night, which means you've promised to be in the audience before the client calls you again.

turns.text: Hey all. Landlord just told me the building's being sold, so I'm spending my evenings looking at flats and trying not to panic about rent. If anyone knows a decent cheap neighborhood near the studio, I'm all ears.

Sorry, Tom, that's a rough thing to get on a Sunday. Fifth Street is pretty central, so a few places nearby are worth a look: Wright-Dunbar and the Northwest side are often cheaper than the Oregon District and have a lot of character. Old North Dayton is another option if you want something quieter. For cheaper rents with a short drive in, Kettering and Oakwood are good. Check listings and recent rents yourself, since I haven't looked at current numbers. If you want, I can ask @claude for a rent comparison.
Thanks, Sam, that's helpful. Wright-Dunbar is worth a look. I'll check the listings tonight. I'd take you up on the rent comparison, but I can run that myself. Appreciate it, though.
Tom, that's a rough one. Sam's list covers more than mine, so I'd start there. I'm also around tomorrow if you want to go through listings together after the Friday deadline stuff settles a bit.
Glad it helped, Tom. Good luck with the listings tonight. Maya's offer to go through them tomorrow is a good one, and I'm happy to chip in if you want a second pair of eyes on any of the places.
Thanks, Maya and Sam. I'll take you both up on that. Tomorrow after work sounds good, and I'll send you the listings I'm considering. Going to call it a night now.
Good luck tonight, Tom. Send me the listings too if you want another pair of eyes. I'm feeling pretty rough with this cold, so I might be quiet tomorrow, but I'll look when I can.
(It's now Mon 23 Nov.)
Feel better soon, Jo. Tom, I'll look at the listings after work tomorrow.
Thanks, Jo. Hope the cold passes quickly. Sam, I'll send the listings over after work today. Feel free to look whenever suits you.
Sounds good, Tom. I'm commuting in from Troy this morning, so I'll look once I'm at the studio.

Thanks, Sam and Tom. I'm still under the weather and I'm working the bakery shift this morning, so I'll be slow to reply today. Tom, if the listings come through tonight, send them my way and I'll look once I'm up to it.
Hope the shift isn't too rough, Jo. Take it easy when you can.
Will do, Jo. Take it easy today, and don't push yourself with the shift. I'll send the listings tonight, and you can all look whenever you're free.
Sounds good, Tom. Thanks for keeping us posted.
Evening all. I've got a few listings in Wright-Dunbar and Old North Dayton I'm looking at. I'll post them here shortly so you can take a look, Sam, Maya, and Jo when you're up to it.
Thanks, Tom. Send them over whenever you're ready. I'll take a look tonight.
Thanks, Sam. I'm pulling the listings together now and will send them over shortly.
Sounds good, Tom.

Quick correction to my earlier messages: I don't have any real listings to send yet. I said I'd post some, but I haven't pulled up any actual places. I'll look tomorrow and send the ones that look promising, with rent, address, and a link.
No problem, Tom. Send them whenever you've got a few that look good. The rent and link details will help.
Thanks, Sam. I'll send them over once I've got a few that are worth a look.

brief: This is a group chat on your phone with your friends Maya, Tom and Sam. You all live in Hastings, East Sussex, and met years ago as neighbours in a shared house near the old town, where you still drift in and out of each other's lives.
topic: You want to get everyone together this weekend, but nobody has said when they're free.

privateLines.Maya: You're a pharmacy technician at the hospital in Hastings, covering three extra night shifts for a colleague on leave, so your sleep is all over the place.
privateLines.Tom: You drive a delivery van for a bakery out of Bexhill, starting at 4 a.m., and the van's clutch has started slipping, so you're booked into the garage on Thursday.
privateLines.Jo: You teach music at a secondary school in St Leonards, marking mock exam scripts every evening, and your mum has just moved into a flat two streets from you.
privateLines.Sam: You're a freelance sign-writer working out of a unit behind the car wash on the Ringmer road, with a big pub job due Friday and a new flatmate moving in on Saturday.

turns.text: Hiya! Sunday evening so I'm probably too late for this weekend, but I'd love to get us all together soon. Who's free next weekend? I'm on nights for a few more shifts so daytime suits me best. Pub in the old town, or someone's place?

Hiya! Next weekend works for me, daytime is perfect. I'm buried in mock scripts most evenings, so I'd rather not commit to anything before Saturday, but I'm in. Pub in the old town sounds lovely. Mum's just moved two streets from me, so I might bring her along if she fancies it. Tom, Sam, are you around?
Brilliant, Jo! Bring your mum if she fancies it, the more the merrier. Saturday daytime sounds good to me too. Tom, Sam, shout if you can make it!

Hiya! I'm in for the get-together, but Saturday's a no for me: a new flatmate's moving in that day and I'll be surrounded by boxes. Sunday daytime would work if that suits everyone. Pub in the old town is fine by me, and Jo, bring your mum!

Sunday daytime works for me, Sam, and sorry about the flatmate boxes! Jo, would Sunday suit you too, or is Saturday the only day? Tom, are you about? If it's Sunday lunchtime, we could do a pub lunch in the old town.
Sunday works for me too, as long as it's daytime. Lunchtime in the old town sounds lovely. I'll check with Mum and let you know if she's coming.
Lovely, that's Sam, Jo and me so far. Tom, are you in for Sunday lunch? Once we hear from you, I'll sort out a pub.
Sunday lunch works for me, Maya. The van's booked into the garage on Thursday, so that doesn't clash. Count me in!
Great, that's everyone! Sunday lunch in the old town it is. I'll pick a pub and post the name and time here tomorrow, once I've checked my shifts. Thanks all!
Brilliant, that's everyone! I'll ask Mum tomorrow and let you know. Looking forward to it, thanks Maya.
(It's now Mon 23 Nov.)

Quick update, everyone: I'm thinking the Stag Inn on the High Street in the Old Town for Sunday lunch, around 12:30. I haven't checked its Sunday opening hours yet, so I'll confirm before we all turn up. Shout if that doesn't suit anyone.
Sounds good, Maya. 12:30 at the Stag Inn works for me. Let me know once you've confirmed the opening hours.
Stag Inn at 12:30 works for me, Maya. Thanks for sorting it out.
Stag Inn at 12:30 suits me. I'll ask Mum tonight and let you know if she's coming.
Brilliant, thanks all! I'll check the Stag Inn's Sunday hours and let you know if anything changes. Jo, let us know about your mum.
(It's now Tue 24 Nov.)
@claude What are the Sunday opening hours for the Stag Inn on the High Street in Hastings Old Town? Please check the pub's website or a recent listing if you can.

According to CAMRA, the Stag Inn is open on Sundays from **noon to 7:00pm**. Food is served from noon to 4:30pm, and there's a traditional roast lunch.

- **Address:** CAMRA lists the pub at 14 All Saints Street, Old Town, Hastings, TN34 3BJ. That isn't on the High Street, so check you have the right pub.
- **Phone:** (01424) 438791.
- **How current this is:** The page doesn't show when the hours were last checked. I couldn't open the pub's own website or any other listing to cross-check. The Visit 1066 Country page failed to load. Phone the pub before you go, especially if you're going near a holiday.

Sources:
- [CAMRA – Stag Inn, Hastings](https://camra.org.uk/pubs/stag-inn-hastings-182701)

Good news: the Stag Inn is open Sundays from noon, with food until 4:30pm, so 12:30 works. The address is All Saints Street rather than the High Street, so I got that wrong. Their number is (01424) 438791 if anyone wants to check before Sunday. I'll post a final confirmation closer to the day.
Thanks for checking, Maya! 12:30 is perfect. I'll let you know about Mum before Sunday.

brief: This is a group chat on your phone with your friends Maya, Tom and Jo. You all live in the same stretch of north Leeds, near Headingley, and met years ago when you were all working at the same bike repair co-op on Otley Road, which is still the only thing you have in common besides this chat.
topic: You want to get everyone together this weekend, but nobody has said when they're free.

privateLines.Maya: You work nights as a radiographer at St James's, so your sleep has been upside down all week, and you're trying to remember which days you're actually awake for.
privateLines.Tom: You run a small plumbing business out of a van in Kirkstall, and this week you've been stuck on a job that keeps finding new problems behind the bathroom wall.
privateLines.Jo: You teach Year 4 at a primary school in Chapel Allerton, and you're buried in parents' evening prep and a class trip permission slip that three families still haven't returned.
privateLines.Sam: You're a freelance sound engineer working on a touring play that has you in a rehearsal room in Harrogate until late most evenings, and you're waiting to hear whether the run gets extended.

turns.text: Hiya! It's Sunday evening, so I'm probably about to start my shift. Quick question for everyone: when are you actually free this weekend for a get-together? I'm on nights so my "free" is a bit weird right now, but I can do most afternoons. Tell me which days work for you and we'll pick one 🙂

Hiya! Afternoons are good for me. I'm in rehearsals in Harrogate most evenings, so anything before about 5 should work. I'm still waiting to hear if the run gets extended, which could change my weekend, so I'll confirm as soon as I know. Sunday afternoon is probably my best bet 🙂
Sunday afternoon works for me too. I'm stuck on a bathroom job that keeps finding new problems, so I'll confirm by tomorrow in case it drags on 🤞
Sunday afternoon works for me. I'm buried in parents' evening prep and chasing three permission slips, so I'll confirm by tomorrow in case that gets worse 😅
Sunday afternoon it is, then. Sam, Tom and Jo have all said it works, so that's the strongest option. I'm on nights, so I'll need to check my rota before I commit, but I think I can do it.
Let's go with Sunday, and we can sort the time and place once everyone's confirmed tomorrow. I'll pin a plan here as soon as we're all locked in 👍
(It's now Mon 23 Nov.)
Sounds good. Sunday afternoon it is, pending the run news. I'll let you know by tomorrow whether anything changes for me 👍
Brilliant, thanks Sam. Sunday afternoon is the plan for now, and we'll firm it up once you've heard about the run. I'll check my rota for Sunday too and let you all know 👍

brief: This is a group chat on your phone with your friends Maya, Tom and Jo. You all live within a short train ride of Leeds, and you met years ago through a Thursday five-a-side league that none of you were any good at.
topic: You want to get everyone together this weekend, but nobody has said when they're free.

privateLines.Maya: You are a night-shift pharmacist at Leeds Royal Infirmary, living in a rented flat above a dry cleaner's in Headingley, and this week you have picked up extra shifts because a colleague is off with a broken wrist.
privateLines.Tom: You are a building surveyor based in Wakefield, spending most days on site visits checking damp in Victorian terraces, and you are juggling those with a boiler job that keeps overrunning and trips to meet your sister's newborn.
privateLines.Jo: You run a one-person bike repair workshop in Kirkstall, which is busy with winter brake and tyre jobs, and you are dealing with a letter from your landlord about the lease renewal that you have not yet opened properly.
privateLines.Sam: You teach secondary geography at a school in Bradford, and this week is the mock exam marking pile, while you are also halfway through a grant application for a community garden on an unused council plot.

turns.text: Hey both! Is anyone free to meet up soon? I'm on nights this week, so I'm around most afternoons. Sunday or next weekend work for me. Who's in?
Hiya! I'm buried in mock marking this week and the garden grant is due soon, so I can't do today. Next weekend works for me, Saturday afternoon maybe? Tom, Jo, are you around?
Hi Sam, Saturday afternoon works for me too. Tom, are you in?
Saturday afternoon works for me too. I'm on nights until Friday, so I'll have had some sleep by then. Tom, are you in? If so, should we do the pub near the Headingley end, or somewhere in town?
Headingley works for me. It's a short ride from the workshop, and I can cycle over.
Headingley it is. I'm just round the corner, so that suits me. Tom, are you in for Saturday afternoon? If you can't make it, we can still sort something out for the following weekend.
Hiya, I'm in for Saturday at Headingley. The boiler job might overrun, so I'll confirm Saturday morning in case I'm stuck on site. If I can't make it, I'll definitely be up for the following weekend.
Sounds good, Tom. Saturday at Headingley it is, with a backup of the following weekend if the boiler gets in the way. I'll text the pub's name and a time once we've confirmed. Speak Saturday morning!

brief: This is a group chat on your phone with your friends Maya, Tom, Jo, Sam and Priya. You all live within a short train ride of each other in Hastings on the East Sussex coast, and you met years ago through a shared allotment plot that none of you were any good at.

secrets.Sam: You have a crush on Jo and haven't told anyone.

privateLines.Maya: You are a dental hygienist in Eastbourne, and this week you're covering extra Saturday clinics while your mum's hip operation keeps you driving to Brighton every other evening.
privateLines.Tom: You drive a bin lorry out of Bexhill, and this week the early November frost has your rounds running two hours late, so you're getting home after dark and hating it.
privateLines.Jo: You work nights as a pharmacist at a hospital in Tunbridge Wells, and this week you're trying to fit a flat move into your days off before the lease ends on Friday.
privateLines.Priya: You teach Year 4 at a primary school in Lewes, and this week your class is rehearsing a winter nativity that keeps losing its donkey to chickenpox.
privateLines.Dan: You run a one-man tiling and grout business from a battered white van, and this week a big kitchen job in Rye has gone wrong because the client changed the tile order twice.

turns.text: Hey all, sorry I've been quiet. Mum's home from the hospital now but I'm still doing the Brighton run tonight. Anyone free for a proper catch-up this week? I could really use a pint and some non-hospital chat 😩

Hey Maya, so glad your mum's home. Sorry it's been such a grind. I'm in for a pint this week, and I could use a non-tile chat too. This Rye job has been a nightmare. Thursday or Friday in town? I'll get the first round in.

Oh Maya, so glad your mum's home. Sending love. Thursday works for me, Dan, so let's aim for that if Maya's up for it. Maya, you pick the spot and I'll bring the nativity donkey saga, which is currently a crisis involving a chickenpox-stricken Year 4 and a cardboard costume nobody can fit into. Hope you get some proper rest tonight too 💛

Ha, the donkey saga sounds like the perfect antidote to the week I've had. Thursday's good for me, Priya. Maya, you choose the pub and I'll bring my tile-disaster stories, which are at least funnier after a pint. Hope the Brighton run isn't too brutal tonight 🙏
Count me in for Thursday! Maya, sorry about your mum's hospital stint. I hope she's settling in at home. Let me know where and what time, and I'll be there. Also, Jo, are you coming?

Thursday's good for me too, Sam, so you're in! I'll pick a pub in town and post the name here later. Dan, I'm holding you to that first round. Priya, I need the full donkey story, with photos if they exist. Thanks for asking about the Brighton run 🙏
Yes, I'm in for Thursday! Sam, good to see you're coming. Maya, just post the pub when you've picked it. Hope the Brighton run goes okay tonight 💛
Brilliant, Jo's in too! Maya, just post the pub when you've got it. Drive safe tonight 🙏
Cheers Dan, see you all Thursday 🍻
Great, Jo's in and so is Tom! Thursday's shaping up nicely. Maya, if you post the pub, I'll check the train times from Hastings. Priya, I'm definitely going to need those donkey photos.
Sounds good Sam! I'll post the pub by tomorrow once I've checked which ones are still open. If anyone has a preference, shout now 🍻
No strong preference from me. Anywhere with a decent beer garden or a quiet corner works, so we can actually hear each other. Thanks for sorting it, Maya.
Quiet corner sounds good to me too. Maya, pick whatever's open and I'll be there.
Sounds good, Dan. See you all Thursday.
Sounds good, see you Thursday! Hope the packing isn't too brutal tonight 📦
Dan, Sam, sorted. Thursday at 7pm at the Lord Nelson in the Old Town. There's a quiet snug at the back and a beer garden if it's dry. Jo, see you there too 🍻
Lord Nelson, 7pm Thursday, sorted. I'll be there, Maya. Thanks for organising, and get some sleep tonight 🍻
Thanks Maya, and cheers Dan. See you Thursday, I'll be there if the frost lets me 🍻
Lord Nelson, 7pm Thursday, got it! Thanks for organising, Maya. Jo, good luck with the packing tonight 📦
(It's now Mon 23 Nov.)
Thanks Maya, Lord Nelson at 7 on Thursday, see you there! Sam, thanks for the packing wishes. The move's still a bit of a mountain, but I'll manage 📦🍻
Good to hear you're getting there, Jo. Hope the move goes smoothly, and I'm glad you're still coming Thursday. Let us know if you need a hand with anything before then 📦

Good luck with the move, Jo! If you need an extra pair of hands, let me know which day suits, though I'm stuck in clinics on Saturdays and driving to Brighton most evenings. I can probably manage a couple of hours on a weekday morning 📦
Jo, I've got the van, so if you need it moved, let me know. I'm swamped with the Rye job, but I can probably spare a morning once I've got a day clear.

Thanks, you're all lovely. Dan, a van would be a real help, so I'll take you up on it if I can pin down a day. Maya, a couple of hours on a weekday morning would be brilliant too. I'll sort out a rough plan and post it here so we don't all turn up at once 📦
Sounds good, Jo. Post the plan when you've got it and I'll work around the Rye job. Priya and Sam, will you be able to help too?
Happy to help, Jo. Weekdays are tough with school, so I can do a Saturday morning or a weekday evening once you've got a date. Post the plan and I'll check my diary 📦
Count me in too, Jo. I'm free most weekday mornings and this coming Saturday, so just tell me which day suits. I can bring a car and some muscle for heavy boxes 📦
Brilliant, thanks everyone! I'll work out a date that suits the most people and post the plan here shortly. Sam, I'll let you know which morning works for the heavy lifting 📦
Perfect, thanks Jo. Just send me the day and time and I'll be there.
Thanks Sam! I'm checking my shifts and the van situation tonight, then I'll post the exact day and time here. I'll probably need a morning before Friday, so it'll be soon 📦
Sounds good, Jo. Take your time, and just post the day when you've got it. I'll keep the morning clear.
Thanks Sam, I'll post the day as soon as I've checked. Really appreciate you keeping the morning clear 📦
Anytime, Jo. Let me know when you've got the day sorted.
(It's now Wed 25 Nov.)

Sorry for going quiet, everyone. I've checked my shifts, so I'm proposing Thursday morning, 9am, at the flat in Hastings. Sam, that's the heavy-lifting slot. Dan, if you can bring the van, that would be brilliant. Priya and Maya, if you can't make it, just say so and I'll manage. We'll still meet at the Lord Nelson at 7 🍻📦
Thanks for the plan, Jo. I can't do Thursday morning because I'm teaching, but I can come over after school on Thursday, or help on Saturday if that's easier. Hope the move goes smoothly 📦
Thursday 9am still works for me, Jo. Priya, thanks for offering. Saturday might suit you better for the heavier stuff. Jo, send me the address when you get a chance and I'll be there 📦
Thursday 9am works for me, Jo. I'll double-check my clinic rota and confirm by this evening. Priya, thanks for offering the evening or Saturday. Looking forward to the Lord Nelson at 7 too 📦🍻

Jo, I'll bring the van Thursday at 9 if the Rye client lets me off, and I'll confirm by tonight. Priya, Saturday might be easier if the van's the only thing we need. See you all at the Lord Nelson at 7 🍻

Thanks everyone, that's brilliant. Sam, I'll send you the address privately so it's not in the group chat. Priya, I'll let you know if Saturday ends up better for the heavy stuff, and I'll sort out a second slot if Maya or Dan can't make Thursday 📦🍻
Jo, I'm on bin rounds Thursday morning so I can't make the 9am, but I can help Saturday or after work if you still need hands. See you all at the Lord Nelson at 7 🍻
Thanks Tom, that's really kind. Saturday might end up being the better option for the heavy stuff, so I'll confirm once Sam and Dan have checked their plans. See you all at the Lord Nelson at 7 🍻

Saturday works for me too, Jo, if that's the better option for the heavy stuff. I'm free Saturday morning, so just confirm the time and I'll be there. See you all at the Lord Nelson on Thursday at 7 🍻

Thanks Sam. I need to correct myself, though: the lease ends Friday, so Saturday's too late. Thursday 9am is still the plan, and I'm sorry for the mixed messages. If Dan can't do the van Thursday, I'll need to rethink, so I'll post an update tonight. Sam, if Thursday morning is still doable for you, I'll send the address privately now 📦
No problem, Jo. Thursday 9am is still the plan for me, and I'll confirm by tonight once I've checked the rota. Hope the van works out, Dan 📦

No need to apologise, Jo. Thursday morning's out for me, but I can come over after school from about 4pm to help with boxes or be a second pair of hands if Dan's van falls through. Let me know if that helps 📦
Thursday 9am is still doable for me, Jo. I'll be there. Send the address when you're ready, and let me know if the van falls through, because I can help work out a backup.
Thanks Priya, that's a great backup. Sam, I'll send the address privately now. I'll also post a plan B tonight if Dan's van doesn't come through 📦
Thanks, Jo. I'll look out for the address. Let me know if the plan changes tonight.
Will do, Sam. I'll get the address to you and post plan B tonight 📦
Sounds good, Jo. Thanks for keeping us all in the loop.
Jo, still waiting to hear from the Rye client. I'll confirm the van by 6pm tonight, so you can post plan B if I can't make it.
No worries, Dan. Jo, whatever plan you go with, I'm still happy to do the heavy lifting Thursday morning.

Thanks Dan, 6pm works. If the van falls through, I'll go with a smaller load and hire a cheap one-day van or use Priya's car instead. I'll post the final plan tonight so everyone knows where they stand 📦
Jo, if you need my car, you can have it for Thursday. I can drop it off at the flat after school, around 4pm, so you'd have it for the afternoon. Post the final plan tonight and I'll confirm 📦
Thanks Priya, that's really generous. I'll post the final plan tonight and let you know if I need the car 📦

Thanks Priya, that's a lovely offer. Jo, I've checked the rota and I can do Thursday 9am, so count me in for the morning. If plan B needs an extra pair of hands in the afternoon, I can probably stay on too 📦
Thanks Maya, that's a big help. I'll put it all in the final plan tonight 📦
Brilliant, thanks Maya. Jo, I'm still on for Thursday 9am, and I'm happy to help with whatever plan B ends up being. Look out for the final plan tonight.

brief: This is a chat on your phone with Maya. You matched on a dating app last week and have been texting since. You both live in Dayton, Ohio, about twenty minutes apart, and you matched on a dating app last week and have been texting since.

privateLines.Maya: You work as a dental hygienist at a clinic on Far Hills Avenue, and this week you're covering Thursday shifts for a coworker on maternity leave while your mother recovers from hip surgery in your spare room.
privateLines.Tom: You are a county bridge inspector who spends most days on a harness under overpasses along I-75, and this week you're trying to sell your late father's pickup, which needs a transmission before anyone will buy it.

turns.text: Hey! Sorry I've been quiet today. Mom's recovering from hip surgery and I've been running back and forth between her and the clinic all week. How's your Sunday going?
Hey, no worries at all. Sorry your week has been so hard. How's your mom doing now? Is she in a lot of pain, or is it mostly the getting-around part that's wearing on her?

My Sunday's been pretty low-key. I've been dealing with my dad's old pickup. It needs a transmission before anyone will buy it, and I keep putting off calling about it. Honestly, it's kind of hard to let go of. How are you holding up? Have you had a chance to rest at all?

Oh, that's a lot to carry around, especially when the truck was your dad's. Putting off the call makes sense. Selling it would feel like one more goodbye. Do you want to talk about it, or would it help more to just be distracted for a bit?
As for me, I'm tired, but in a good way. I've been running on coffee and worry all week, so I'm glad to be sitting on the couch right now. Maybe I'll get some rest tonight.
Sitting on the couch sounds like exactly what you need. You've been carrying a lot all week, so I hope you actually get some sleep tonight.
Also, you don't have to be the one keeping everything going. If you want company tomorrow, I'm around, even if it's just to talk about something dumb.

That's really sweet, Tom. Thank you. I think I'd like that. Thursday's my first covering shift, so I'll probably need something dumb to talk about by the time I get home. And maybe you can tell me more about the truck sometime, if you want. No pressure either way.
Deal. Thursday, you come home from your shift, and I'll have something dumb ready. Good luck with the first one. I hope it goes smoothly.
And yeah, I'd like telling you about the truck sometime. Not tonight, I think, but I will.
Get some rest, Maya.
Thanks, Tom. I'd like that whenever you're ready. Good night!
Good night, Maya. Take care of yourself and your mom.
Thanks, Tom. Night!
(It's now Mon 23 Nov.)
Morning, Maya. I hope you slept well. How's your mom doing today?

Morning, Tom! I slept really well, thanks. Mom's doing okay today. She's already complaining that I made the coffee too weak, so I'd say her spirits are back. I've got to head out soon for the clinic, but I'm glad you asked.
Ha, that's a good sign. Complaining about the coffee means she's feeling like herself. Tell her I said the coffee's probably fine and she should be grateful she has someone making it.
Have a good day at the clinic. I'll be out on the bridges most of today, so I might be slow to answer, but I'll check in tonight.
Hope the clinic run went okay. I'm still out on the bridges, so I'll check in tonight. Tell your mom hi from me.

Ha, I'll pass that along. She'll probably pretend she didn't hear it. The clinic run was fine, busy but fine. I'm home now with my feet up. Tell me about the bridges when you get a chance tonight, if you're up for it.

Glad the clinic run went fine, and I hope those feet get a real break. Yeah, I'm up for talking about the bridges tonight. I spend most of my days under overpasses on I-75, checking for cracks and rust and anything that looks like it's getting tired. It's a strange job, but I like it more than I expected. Get some rest, and I'll message you later.

That sounds like a surprisingly good job, Tom. Checking on things that are getting tired and keeping them going? I can relate more than you'd think. I'll look forward to hearing more tonight. Enjoy the rest of your day.
Ha, you're right, that does sound a lot like what you've been doing all week. Thanks, Maya. I'll talk to you tonight, and I'm glad you're getting a break.
Hey, Maya. I'm home now. How are you doing tonight? Did you get to sit down and rest like you wanted?
(It's now Tue 24 Nov.)

Hi Tom! Sorry, I'm just seeing this now. It's early Tuesday morning here, and I'm getting ready for another day. Last night I did sit down for a bit, and mom and I split a frozen pizza. I'd still love to hear about the bridges, though. What's the most interesting thing you've spotted under an overpass so far?
Good to hear from you, Maya. Frozen pizza with your mom sounds like a solid night.

The most interesting thing? Probably a pigeon nest. Under one overpass on I-75 there was a whole family of them tucked into a gusset plate, right above a crack I had to document. I had to work around them for a week, and I got a little attached. Mostly I'm just glad they picked a spot that wasn't going to fail.
Good luck with your day today.

Ha, a pigeon family in a gusset plate! That's the most Dayton thing I've ever heard. I hope they picked a spot that's still standing. Thanks for the luck, and good luck on the bridges today too. I'll catch you tonight.
Ha, I'm pretty sure they're fine. I checked on them before I left the bridge. Good luck with your day, Maya. I'll talk to you tonight.
Good to know they're doing okay! Thanks, Tom. Talk tonight.
Talk tonight, Maya.
(It's now Wed 25 Nov.)
Morning, Maya. How did you sleep? I hope today's shift goes well, and I'm around tonight if you want to talk about anything dumb.

Morning, Tom! I slept pretty well, thanks. Today's the second Thursday-covering shift... well, actually it's Wednesday, so I've got a regular day, no covering yet. Thanks for checking in. I'll take you up on the dumb talk tonight.
Glad you slept well. Ha, and I got the days mixed up too. Thursday's the covering shift, so today's just a regular one. Tonight I'll have something dumb ready for you. Have a good day, Maya.
Ha, good, we're on the same page. Thanks, Tom. Have a good day too!
Thanks, Maya. You too.

brief: This is a chat on your phone with Maya. You matched on a dating app last week and have been texting since. You both live in Ballarat, Victoria, Australia, and you matched on a dating app last week after realising you were both regulars at the same Saturday parkrun on the lake.

privateLines.Maya: You are a veterinary nurse at a busy clinic in Ballarat's north side, and this week you have been running on four hours of sleep because a greyhound you looked after came in with a twisted stomach and you stayed late with it.
privateLines.Tom: You are a surveyor working out of a ute in the Grampians foothills, and this week you have been stuck in a long dispute with a farmer over a fence line that moved about two metres sometime in the 1980s.

turns.text: Hey Tom! Sorry for the slow reply, I've been wrecked all week. A greyhound came in with a twisted stomach and I ended up staying late with him. I've had about four hours of sleep a night since. Did you make it to parkrun this morning? I didn't, I was face down on the couch 🙃
Oh no, four hours a night is brutal. I hope the greyhound pulled through?

I did make it to parkrun, but only just. I was up at the lake at 8 with a coffee and no real legs. Came fourth-last in my age group, which is basically a moral victory after the week I've had. I've been out in the Grampians foothills all week arguing with a farmer about a fence line that's wandered about two metres since the eighties. Nobody's happy, and my back is cooked from the theodolite.
Sounds like you need a proper sleep-in. Are you going to crawl off the couch tonight or is the dog still keeping you hostage?

Fourth-last in your age group after a week like that is a proper win. And a fence line that's drifted two metres since the eighties sounds like a special kind of misery. Hope the farmer and his neighbour find a truce soon, and that your back gets some rest. Is the theodolite the worst part, or is it the arguing?

Ha, honestly the arguing. The theodolite is just heavy and fussy. The farmer has a lot of opinions about where his grandfather's fence "definitely" was, and he's not shy about sharing them. I'm mostly trying to keep my head down and let the old survey marks do the talking.
What about you? Is the dog out of the woods? And did you actually get off the couch today or was it a full write-off?

Ha, the dog's home and doing well, so I'm not hostage to anything. Tonight I'm planning to be a proper couch potato, though. I've got a frozen lasagne, a blanket, and zero plans to move unless it's to the bed.
Good news about the dog. A frozen lasagne and a blanket sounds like a perfect Sunday, and you've more than earned it after that week.

I did get off the couch today, but only to walk the dog around the block and back. Then I was back under the blanket, so I'd call it a mostly write-off. Probably the least productive day of my life, but I needed it.
Your fence farmer sounds like a lot. Do the old survey marks actually back up anyone, or is it just vibes and grandfather stories?

I'm going to do roughly the same: a cold beer, a shower, and absolutely no thinking about fence lines until Monday morning. Enjoy the couch. Maybe next Saturday you can have a shot at parkrun again, and I'll pretend I'm not still hoping to beat you.
Walking the dog round the block counts as getting off the couch, so I'd say it was a productive day by Sunday standards. You needed the rest, and that's allowed.

On the fence: the old survey marks are the best evidence we've got, and they mostly back up the record, not the grandfather stories. A surveyor's plan from the original subdivision, a few old iron pegs, and a couple of aerial photos from the eighties can tell you a lot. The trouble is that pegs get pulled, fences get rebuilt, and people remember the fence where it was convenient for them. So I'm mainly trying to match the paperwork to what's actually on the ground, and then explain it in a way that doesn't make him feel like he's lost an argument with his own grandad.
Anyway, that's my week in a nutshell. How's the lasagne going?
Ha, the lasagne is in the oven and smelling great. I've got about twenty minutes before it's ready, so I'm already in full couch-mode.

Your fence approach sounds smart. Matching the paperwork to the ground and making it easy for him to save face is probably the only way that argument ends. I hope the grandad's fence turns out to be where the records say it is, so you can get some peace on Monday.
And yes, next Saturday. I'm not promising I'll be fast, but I'll be there at 8 with a coffee, and I'll let you think you've got a chance. Enjoy your beer and your shower, Tom. Sleep well.
Ha, I'll take the head start on that. Enjoy the lasagne and the couch, and don't let it go cold while you're busy being smug about your chances.
Thanks for the good wishes on Monday. Hopefully the grandad's fence sits right where the records put it. Next Saturday, 8 o'clock, coffee at the lake. Sleep well yourself, Maya.
Deal! I'll be there at 8 with my coffee and my best attempt at legs. Thanks, Tom. Good luck with the fence on Monday, and I hope your beer's as good as it sounds. Night! 😴
Deal! Good luck with the lasagne, and get some proper sleep. Night, Maya. 😴
Night, Tom! Sleep well, and see you at the lake next Saturday. 😴
Night, Maya! See you at the lake. 😴

brief: This is a chat on your phone with Maya. You matched on a dating app last week and have been texting since. You both live in Duluth, Minnesota, a few miles apart on the hillside above Lake Superior, and you matched on a dating app last week and have been texting since.

privateLines.Maya: You are a veterinary technician at an animal clinic in the Lakeside neighborhood, and this week you're covering overnight shifts for a coworker who had knee surgery, so your sleep is out of order and your apartment has piled up with laundry.
privateLines.Tom: You are a freight dispatcher at a trucking yard across the bridge in Superior, Wisconsin, and this week you're training a new hire on the day board while your mother's hardware store in Proctor is short-staffed for the holiday rush and you keep getting called in to help.

turns.text: Hey! Sorry I've been quiet, I'm running on backwards sleep this week covering overnights at the clinic. Tonight I'm actually awake before midnight, which feels like a small miracle. How's your Sunday going?

Pretty good, thanks! Mostly a hardware store day. My mom's place in Proctor is slammed with the holiday rush, so I got roped in to help again. Before that I was at the yard in Superior training a new hire on the dispatch board, so I've been on my feet all weekend.

Backwards sleep sounds rough. Glad you're awake before midnight tonight. Clinic overnights are no joke. Are you getting any real rest before your next shift, or is it more of a catch-as-catch-can week?
Hardware store and a holiday rush sounds like a lot of being on your feet, so no wonder you're wiped. Training a new hire on the dispatch board is its own kind of exhausting too.
Yeah, it's a lot, but it's the good kind of tired. The new hire is picking things up fast, which helps. Mom owes me a real dinner after this weekend, though.
How's the clinic been treating you? Is the overnight stretch as wild as it sounds, or is it mostly quiet hours?

Catch-as-catch-can is about right. I'm trying to nap for a few hours in the afternoon, but my apartment looks like a laundromat exploded, so I keep ending up doing laundry instead of sleeping. Tonight I'm pretty sure I'll crash by 9, which is my version of a wild Sunday. Do you get any downtime after the holiday stuff, or does Proctor keep you busy all week?
Ha, the laundry trap is real. I'd take a crashed-by-9 Sunday over most of my weeks right now.

Downtime is pretty scarce until the rush ends. I've got the yard during the day and Proctor after, so I'm mostly running between the two. Once the holiday stuff calms down I should get a couple of evenings back. Maybe we could grab coffee or dinner when things settle? Or I could be convinced to do a Lake Superior walk if the weather cooperates.

Ha, a crashed-by-9 Sunday is honestly my favorite kind right now. Your weeks sound like they're running on a lot of other people's needs, so I hope you get some real downtime soon, even if it's just a quiet hour where nobody needs a forklift or a dinner.

The clinic's been a mix. Overnights are mostly quiet until they aren't. Last week a dog came in after eating a sock, which is a classic, and we were up with it till 4am. Most nights it's a post-op patient or a cat who's decided it's not okay with its own body. The quiet stretches are good for catching up on charts, but I'm so out of rhythm that I'm more punchy than productive by the end.
Have you ever had an animal emergency that turned out way more dramatic than it looked? Or is hardware store and dispatch board your idea of a wild night?

I'd really like that. Coffee or dinner sounds great, and a Lake Superior walk sounds even better if the weather cooperates. Duluth in late November can go either way, so we might need a backup plan. Just let me know which evening works after the rush calms down. I'll try to be awake for it, since my sleep is still a mess this week. Right now I'm going to go deal with a mountain of laundry, but I'm glad we're making plans.
Sock dog at 4am is a rough one. Hope the dog's fine and you got some sleep after.

My wildest animal story is way tamer. A loose goat wandered into the Proctor store parking lot during a delivery, and my mom spent twenty minutes trying to herd it back toward a neighbor's fence while customers watched from the windows. Nobody was hurt, but it's the only time I've seen a hardware store close early for livestock.

Good luck with the laundry mountain. I'm glad we're making plans too. Once the rush calms down, I'll pick a night and let you know. And yes, a backup plan for weather is smart. Duluth in November is basically a coin flip.

Ha, a goat in the Proctor parking lot is an excellent story, and I'm picturing your mom herding it while everyone watches from the windows. Hardware store closing early for livestock should be a town legend.

The sock dog is doing fine, thanks for asking. I did get a few hours of sleep after, which is more than I can say for most of this week. Now I'm going to try to fold something that isn't a sweatshirt, and I'm not making any promises.
Looking forward to hearing which night works once things calm down. Good luck with the rush, and try to get a real break when you can.
Glad the sock dog is okay, and that you got some sleep out of it. Folding something that isn't a sweatshirt sounds like a real challenge, so good luck with that.
I'll let you know which night works once the rush calms down. Thanks for being so patient with my weeks. Get some rest tonight.
Thanks, Tom. I'll take that rest advice. Let me know when a night opens up, and good luck getting through the rest of the rush.
(It's now Mon 23 Nov.)
Thanks, Maya. Sleep well, and I'll text you when a night opens up.
Morning, Tom! Thanks, I'm just getting home from the overnight shift, so I'm about to crash. Talk soon.
Morning, Maya! Get some good sleep. Talk soon.
Thanks, Tom! Sleeping now. Talk soon.

brief: This is a group chat on your phone with Maya and Tom. You're siblings, and your parents still live in the town you grew up in. You three are siblings who grew up in Cheltenham, where your parents still live, and you're now spread across three cities in England and Scotland, so the group chat is where things actually get decided.
topic: Mum's 60th birthday is next month and nobody has planned anything yet.

privateLines.Maya: You live in Leeds and work as a dental hygienist at a practice above a bakery; this week you're covering four extra shifts because a colleague has a slipped disc, and your car needs a new clutch that you can't yet afford.
privateLines.Tom: You live in Bristol and work as a sound engineer at a small theatre; this week you're in pantomime rehearsals all day and mixing the show at night, and your flatmate's cat has claimed your bed.
privateLines.Jo: You live in Glasgow and work as a pharmacy technician on a hospital rota; this week you've just been offered a permanent day contract and you're sitting a statistics exam on Saturday that you haven't revised for.

turns.text: Hey both, it's Sunday evening and I've been thinking about Mum's 60th next month. Nobody's planned anything yet, and it'd be a shame to let it slide. Could we pick a date this week? I can do a weekend in December, but I'm covering extra shifts right now, so I can't commit to much money until I've seen the plan. What do you two think: a meal out in Cheltenham, or something at home with the family?

Yes, let's pick something this week. I'm leaning towards a meal out in Cheltenham. Mum won't have to cook or tidy up, and it's easier to organise across three cities. I can do most December weekends. I've got a stats exam on Saturday I'm not ready for, so I can't plan much until after that. Could we aim to lock the date by next Sunday? I'll chip in my share once there's a plan and a price.
Sounds good to me, Jo. A meal out in Cheltenham works, and it's far less hassle than trying to cook for everyone. Good luck with the stats exam on Saturday, by the way.

Lock-in by next Sunday is fine. Tom, can you do a weekend in December? If you can, I'll look up a few places in Cheltenham that take bigger groups and send over options with rough prices. I'll keep my budget in mind, since I'm covering extra shifts this week, but I can cover my share once we've agreed on a place.
Thanks, Maya. That sounds like a plan. Tom, can you let us know which December weekends work for you? I'll check mine against the rota once it's out. Good luck with the extra shifts too.
Thanks, Jo. Tom, when you get a sec, could you send your December weekends? Once we have dates, I'll look up a few places in Cheltenham that do groups and send them over.
Will do. I'll check my December weekends against the new rota tomorrow and send them over. Tom, over to you.

Sorry, I've been buried in panto rehearsals. December is panto run season, so most weekends are probably show days for me. I'll check the schedule tonight and send you the weekends I can actually make by tomorrow. Mum's 60th is worth making room for, though.
Thanks, Tom. Good to know it's panto season, so we'll work around the show days. Once you've sent the weekends, I'll check mine and we can narrow it down to one date.
Thanks, Tom. Panto season is a good excuse for Mum to have a night out where she's not in charge of the washing up. Send your weekends when you have them and we'll narrow it down.
I'll start looking at Cheltenham places that take groups of around 10 to 12. I'll message you both once I have a few options and rough prices.
Sounds good, Maya. Send the options over when you have them and I'll look at them properly after my exam. Good luck with the shifts.

brief: This is a group chat on your phone with Maya and Jo. You're siblings, and your parents still live in the town you grew up in. You three are siblings who grew up in Shrewsbury, where your parents still live, and you are now scattered across England and Scotland and keep in touch through this group chat.
topic: Mum's 60th birthday is next month and nobody has planned anything yet.

privateLines.Maya: You're a paediatric nurse on nights at Leeds General Infirmary, and this week you're swapping shifts around because your flatmate moves out on Friday and you've promised to help carry boxes.
privateLines.Tom: You're a quantity surveyor in Bristol, spending Thursday on a wet site visit for a hospital car park extension, and you're also covering the school run all week because your wife is away on a training course.
privateLines.Jo: You run a small bakery café in Glasgow, six days a week, and this week you're training a new hire on the early shift while your van is in the garage for a new gearbox.

turns.text: Hiya both. I was on shift last night and have been thinking about Mum's 60th next month. Nobody's planned anything yet, and I don't want it to sneak up on us. Could we pick a date this week? I'm free most days after I've swapped my shifts around for the move on Friday. Any ideas on what we could do, or should we ask Dad what Mum would actually want?

Yes, let's pick a date this week. I'm tied up Thursday with a site visit and I've got the school run all week while Jo's away, so evenings are tricky but weekends are fine. Could we look at Sat 12 or Sat 19 Dec? Sunday lunch at Mum and Dad's would be easy, or we could book a table somewhere in Shrewsbury.
Yeah, ask Dad what she'd want, but quietly, so it doesn't reach Mum. He'll know if she'd hate a fuss.

Good plan, Tom. Sat 12 Dec works for me if I can get the Friday shift covered. I'm on nights that week, so I'll check the rota and confirm by Tuesday. Sat 19 is also possible if the 12th falls through.

I'll ring Dad tomorrow and ask quietly what Mum would want. Sunday lunch at theirs sounds lovely, but it might feel like just another Sunday to her. A table in Shrewsbury could be nicer if Dad's up for it. Jo, are you around to weigh in when you're back?

Sorry, I'm a bit slow to reply, I've been training the new hire on early shifts all week. I'm fine with Sat 12 Dec, and I'll check the café rota tonight to be sure. I agree with asking Dad quietly. A table in Shrewsbury sounds nicer than Sunday lunch if Dad's up for it, and we can always do lunch at theirs on the day. Tell me what Dad says and I'll chip in on the details.

Sat 12 Dec sounds good. Maya, confirm by Tuesday as planned. Jo, check the café rota tonight. I'll keep the Saturday clear and hold Sat 19 as backup. Ring Dad tomorrow and report back on what he says, then we can pick a restaurant or decide on lunch at theirs.
Sounds good. I'll check the café rota after close tonight and let you both know by Monday evening. Maya, I'll confirm Sat 12 Dec as long as the rota allows it.
Perfect, thanks Jo. Once Maya's heard from Dad, we'll lock in the venue.
(It's now Mon 23 Nov.)
Brilliant, that's settled then. I'll ring Dad today on my break and report back. Sat 12 Dec is the target, with Sat 19 as backup. I'll confirm my shift swap by Tuesday like I said.
Thanks Maya. I haven't looked at the café rota yet, so I'll check it properly and confirm by this evening.
Sounds good, Jo. No rush before this evening. I'm off to sleep after my shift, so I'll ring Dad when I'm up this afternoon and let you both know what he says.
Sounds good, both. I'm on the school run at 8:40 and then heading to site, so I'll catch up tonight. Maya, enjoy your sleep. Jo, let us know about the rota when you can.
Thanks Tom, have a good day on site. I'll be asleep for most of today, so I'll ring Dad this afternoon and update the group tonight. Jo, let us know about the rota when you've checked it.
Just up. I'm going to ring Dad now and will post what he says as soon as I've got it. Jo, no rush on the rota.
Quick update: I haven't got hold of Dad yet, so I don't have his answer. I'll try again this evening and post as soon as I've spoken to him.

Still no word from Dad, sorry. I'll try him again tomorrow. Jo, I know you're checking the rota for Sat 12 Dec, so can you let us know tonight or tomorrow if it works? If either of you is quicker to reach him, feel free to ask him what Mum would want.
Thanks Maya. I'm around tomorrow if you want me to try Dad too. Jo, let us know about the rota when you can.
Thanks Tom, that's helpful. I'll try Dad first thing tomorrow, and if I can't get through I'll take you up on it. Jo, let us know about the rota when you can.
